author: Redação
title: A Mão Invisível das Big Techs
content:
Quando o economista escocês Adam Smith, conhecido como pai do liberalismo, falou no século 18 sobre “a mão invisível do mercado”, ele previa que ao buscar seu próprio benefício os indivíduos poderiam favorecer o conjunto da sociedade. Mas Smith também advertiu que os comerciantes costumam mancomunar-se e manipular as regras a seu favor e que o Estado deve evitar monopólios e garantir bens públicos. Hoje está claro que, se não fiscalizadas, Big Techs e demais empresas atuam como Smith temia:

moldam as leis, cooptam governos e manipulam a opinião pública em benefício próprio.


Diante de avanços legislativos, existe um setor que tem se destacado nas ações de lobby anti-regulação em todo o mundo: as Big Techs, um grupo seleto de companhias bilionárias como Meta (dona do Facebook, WhatsApp e Instagram), Alphabet (dona do Google), Amazon, Microsoft e Apple – conhecida como as “Big Five” – e outras, como a chinesa ByteDance (dona do TikTok), a gigante argentina Mercado Livre, e novos

players

 da corrida pela inteligência artificial, como a OpenAI. 


Juntas, as gigantes da tecnologia têm um

impacto maior em todos os aspectos da vida das pessoas do que muitos governos.

 No entanto, diferentemente dos governos, cujo objetivo é servir ao público e que têm de responder a ele, as Big Techs têm como objetivo maximizar lucros e prestar contas a seus acionistas.


Há poucos dados sobre como elas agem para influenciar legislações. Hoje, as Big Techs são o setor que mais gasta em lobby na União Europeia, onde são obrigadas a declarar seus investimentos. Em 2024, o setor

gastou

 67 milhões de euros, um aumento de 57% desde 2020. Nos Estados Unidos – onde também são forçadas a publicizar seu gasto em lobby, elas gastaram 61 milhões de dólares no mesmo ano, um

aumento

 de 13% em comparação com 2023. Para abrir portas com a administração Trump, empresas como Amazon, Meta, Google e Microsoft doaram 1 milhão de dólares cada para o comitê da cerimônia de posse, e os CEOs se enfileiraram durante o evento.


Pela primeira vez, uma investigação colaborativa e transfronteiriça conseguiu identificar quase 3 mil ações de lobby das Big Techs realizadas em parlamentos e governos de todo o mundo, que podem ser acessadas nesta

base de dados interativa

. Também registramos processos judiciais e projetos de lei envolvendo as regras do jogo na indústria de tecnologia.


Conheça aqui as táticas de lobby identificadas neste projeto e a

nota metodológica

.


Explore o lobby das Big Techs em 2.977 ações de influência: clique e navegue no painel interativo


Tornar visíveis a “mão invisível” das Big Techs é uma tarefa que as organizações participantes deste projeto consideram urgente.

 Por isso, todas realizam um

disclaimer

 coletivo sobre financiamentos recebidos de empresas tecnológicas atualmente ou no passado. Veja

aqui

 a lista completa.  


Depois do lançamento, a RSF publicou um comunicado sobre as revelações:


“Essa investigação inédita, conduzida com ajuda da RSF, mostra a enorme influência que as grandes corporações de tecnologia exercem sobre decisões estratégicas que afetam diretamente o futuro do jornalismo, seja por meio de lobbies contra legislações democráticas ou de esforços para evitar uma remuneração justa pelo conteúdo jornalístico. O projeto confirma a necessidade de enfrentar o desequilíbrio de poder que favorece as grandes plataformas online em detrimento da saúde das sociedades democráticas. Se legisladores cederem ao lobby das big techs, o futuro do jornalismo estará ameaçado — assim como o direito dos cidadãos a acessar informação confiável.


Artur Romeu, Diretor da RSF América Latina


Mas como as Big Techs operam no resto do mundo? 


As grandes empresas de tecnologia têm mais dinheiro do que muitos países. Segundo seu relatório financeiro, a Alphabet, dona do Google, teve uma receita de 350 bilhões de dólares em 2024, quase o equivalente ao PIB do Chile, três vezes o do Equador e dez vezes o de El Salvador. A Meta teve uma receita de 164 bilhões de dólares em 2024, mais de três vezes a produção econômica do Paraguai. A receita da Amazon no ano passado foi de quase 638 bilhões de dólares, um valor equivalente ao PIB da Argentina e um terço do PIB brasileiro.


Seu poder de barganha é maior em países menos desenvolvidos, e as Big Techs sabem usá-lo.

Em alguns países – como é o caso da maioria dos países da América Latina e do Sul Global, inclusive o Brasil – o lobby não é regulamentado, e, portanto, é ainda …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: “Levantar nuestras voces y decir 'acá estamos las mujeres indígenas'”
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Claudia Aguirre es qom, profesora intercultural de idiomas y vive en el asentamiento Cristo Rey, en el norte de Resistencia (Chaco). Trabaja en el Instituto de Formación Superior San Fernando Rey e integra Alpi Huaqaanepi (Mujeres Estrellas, en qom), espacio intercultural de mujeres y disidencias feministas cristianas. Promueve el idioma originario como parte de la defensa de su cultura y de la espiritualidad ancestral. Advierte que el panorama político es "muy difícil", pero señala: "Ojalá que podamos conquistar más derechos y que también se nos visibilice. Tratamos de levantar nuestras voces y de decir 'acá estamos las mujeres indígenas'".


En el barrio donde vive, relata, se ve mucha pobreza: dificultades en el acceso a la salud, falta de trabajo, precariedad de las viviendas. “Todos los que estamos en esta zona estamos por debajo de la línea de pobreza”, sintetiza.


—¿Qué ocurre con respecto a los derechos indígenas?


—Seguimos peleando por los derechos, tratando de insertarnos en distintos espacios.

 Hay muchas mujeres indígenas que, desde sus lugares y espacios, militan por los derechos, aportan su granito de arena. Pero es difícil.

En el ámbito educativo, por ejemplo, no se da una buena interculturalidad porque hay mucho desconocimiento. Hace poco fui a un colegio a hablar sobre la

Masacre de Napalpí

. Y muchos chicos no conocían esa historia. O quizás la habían escuchado nombrar, pero no la conocían en profundidad.

 Las comunidades indígenas no somos algo del pasado.

En Chaco hay tres pueblos, Wichí, Qom y Moqoit, que estamos, que resistimos y que queremos contar la historia. Pero no la historia oficial que siempre se contó, sino la de nuestros pueblos. Chaco es una de las provincias pioneras en cuanto a educación intercultural. En el Barrio Toba, en Resistencia, hay un complejo educativo donde se trabaja la lengua materna en todos los niveles y la identidad porque es una escuela de gestión comunitaria bilingüe e intercultural. En Fontana (localidad vecina a Resistencia) también hay una escuela bilingüe; en el barrio Mapic, de Resistencia, también se trabaja la lengua qom. Pero falta mucho, si tenemos en cuenta que en la provincia las tres lenguas indígenas fueron declaradas lenguas oficiales.


Mujeres Estrellas está integrada por mujeres qom y

por mujeres de identidad marrón

. Recientemente se sumaron jóvenes de entre 17 y 20 años. Una de sus tareas principales es la promoción de la lengua qom y la sensibilización sobre la violencia de género en los ámbitos religiosos.


—¿Por qué se conformó la organización Mujeres Estrellas?


—Surgió porque las mujeres sufríamos muchas violencias en espacios religiosos.

Un día nos juntamos a compartir todo lo que nos pasaba y nos dimos cuenta de que no estábamos solas.

 A través de Mujeres Estrellas fuimos conociendo otras redes de contención y nos dimos cuenta de que teníamos que buscar nuestra espiritualidad ancestral, porque nosotras como mujeres indígenas tenemos una espiritualidad ancestral, la espiritualidad de nuestras ancestras, de nuestro pueblo. Todo eso se fue perdiendo. Entonces la idea es rescatar la cosmovisión a través de los relatos. Tenemos una anciana que es nuestra asesora lingüística y a la que recurrimos cuando tenemos alguna inquietud o queremos saber algo de cómo era antes.


Foto: Claudia Aguirre


—¿Qué cuestiones fueron recuperando?


—La identidad. Por eso creo que ahora se sumaron estas chicas tan jovencitas, porque particularmente en la ciudad tenemos una gran pérdida de la lengua materna. No pasa lo mismo en el interior de la provincia. Acá, al estar en contacto todo el tiempo con el castellano por este proceso de aculturación o transculturación, las personas que pertenecemos a pueblos originarios vamos perdiendo la lengua. No porque queramos, sino porque si uno se tiene que implantar en el sistema educativo, en la sociedad, todo es en castellano.

Y al perder nuestra lengua, perdemos nuestra identidad.

 Sobre eso estuvimos trabajando mucho.


—¿Cómo llevan adelante ese trabajo?


—A través de talleres con infancias y con mujeres. Armamos carteles con palabras o frases simples, de uso cotidiano. También trabajamos a través de canciones y de relatos. Les enseñamos la forma de saludar a sus abuelos o palabras básicas, cosas que ellos puedan repetir. También les damos un refrigerio, pero ahora está tan difícil la situación económica que cuesta un poco compartir eso.

author: A.N.A.
title: Sou a Anarquia!!!
content:
Nasci com a primeira revolta insubmissa, inquieta, desgrenhada. Construí a mim mesma desnuda, bela, irreverente. Desde meus ossos inermes partiu a primeira blasfêmia ao criador… Neguei-me a ser submetida, dirigida, apadrinhada. Transformei-me em apóstata, fui acusada de irreligiosidade. Fui condenada, mas minhas asas eram de fênix, e rapidamente abandonei as fogueiras e atravessei os oceanos… Vi jugos em todo lugar, dores e fome, discursos e lamentos, aprendi o desespero. Cavei com as unhas uma trincheira de sonhos e me embriaguei com esse bando de jovens loucos, poetas náufragos de volta à Espanha de trinta e seis… Olhei à esquerda, olhei à direita e vi rostos sujos escondidos atrás de limpos uniformes vertendo o sangue dos povos em nome da justiça, da dialética e outras quintessências enjoativas… E peguei a raiva e afiei-a e lancei raios contra os tronos, inimiga dos governos, inimiga das pátrias, inimiga da dor. Abraço o mundo, vivo e não imploro, amo e resisto suas tiranias.


Sou a Anarquia!!!


(Anônimo)

author: Andrés
title: Arauco, la forestal, está involucrada en el incendio de 10 casas
content:
Arauco vuelve a atacar en San Pedro. En la provincia de Misiones ostenta la cara violenta del extractivismo forestal. Allí donde tampoco falta la complicidad del gobierno de misiones con la policía, que le cuida las enormes extensiones de tierra a esta multinacional criminal que amenaza a las familias campesinas apropiarse de sus tierras.

Por Clarisa Néztor (ANRed).


Este viernes, Cristian Marcelo Dos Santos no pudo entrar a su casa. Alguien la había incendiado, y el lugar donde había vivido muchos años ya no existía más. Nada quedaba de las paredes, las piezas y todas sus pertenencias. Habían entrado a su chacra de Puerto Argentino 3, y aprovechado su ausencia para incendiarle la casa.


El martes 1° de septiembre la policía había entrado junto a personal de Arauco para exigirle que deje de trabajar su chacra. Lo habían apretado, amenazándolo con 6 meses de cárcel por carpir la tierra, su tierra. Y todo sin mediar orden judicial. El crimen: vivir en su casa, cultivar su tierra, producir lo necesario para la propia subsistencia. Y Cristian, el productor campesino, tuvo miedo. En los últimos  30 días habían incendiado 10 casas de la misma comunidad. Ante el miedo, sacó a sus animales y se llevó algunas pertenencias.


El miércoles pasado, camionetas de Arauco volvieron a recorrer la chacra. Pero este viernes a la tarde, los que vieron el humo proveniente llegaron cuando apenas quedaban unos pilotes en llamas. Demasiado tarde: solo cenizas quedaban de la casa.


Ayer tenía un techo. Hoy ya no. El jueves Cristian Marcelo Dos Santos había cerrado la puerta de un hogar donde se había guarecido de tormentas bravas y veranos voraces. Esta noche no. Tampoco habría puerta que cerrar mañana o el domingo para matear unas horas en el silencio de la tarde.


Y esto que acaba de pasar le sucedió a otras 9 familias el pasado mes. Y volverá a suceder tantas veces como el interés de la clase dominante entre en conflicto con el de la clase desposeída.


Si nos quedamos de brazos cruzados, agarrándonos la cabeza para exclamar “oh, qué horror” y seguir dejándola pasar, no hay chances. Desde que Senadores aprobó la ley de desalojo exprés, y aunque aún no se haya tratado en diputados, ya son 10 las viviendas incendiadas. Y son familias que están perdiendo todo: sus casas, animales, herramientas, cultivos y el lugar donde producen sus alimentos. Vidas truncadas, desarraigadas, desposeídas por políticas mezquinas que le quitan más al débil para acumularlo todo. Familias que sufren amenazas, golpes y criminalización por intentar permanecer en sus territorios.


El despojo territorial en Misiones muestra el entramado mafioso de política, empresa y justicia.


Demandamos al gobierno de Misiones @gobiernodemisiones que Arauco cese inmediatamente el accionar criminal sobre las familias rurales y que se investiguen todos los incendios intencionales denunciados, las amenazas y la participación de la Policía de Misiones en los procedimientos. El gobierno y la justicia está operando en complicidad con la mafia forestal de Arauco.


Defender a las familias también es defender su derecho a la tierra, a producir alimentos y a vivir sin miedo.


Estos son los nombres de quienes se animaron a elevar la denuncia y aparecer públicamente:


Ayala, Julio Martín


Molina, María


Borges, Juan


Antúnez, Diego (presidente de la asoación de colonos unidos por la chacra)


Dos Santos, Cristian Marcelo


Hay otros cinco, que se fueron, que dejaron de pertenecer al grupo por la intimidación sufrida.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Los defensores del capitalismo son víctimas de sus propios sesgos cognitivos
content:
Las personas que creen que el capitalismo está funcionando maravillosamente son pensadores negligentes que han caído víctimas del

sesgo del superviviente

 y de la

falacia del mundo justo

.


El

sesgo del superviviente

 ocurre cuando tu análisis se enfoca en quienes lograron salir adelante, mientras ignora a quienes no lo lograron. Vos sí conseguiste un buen trabajo, te compraste una casa, vivís cómodamente, lo que significa que el sistema funciona bien y debe haber un problema con cualquier persona que no pueda prosperar bajo él.


Todas las personas que trabajan tan duro como vos, pero que aún así están pasando dificultades, desaparecen por completo de tu perspectiva. Todas las personas que son tan inteligentes e ingeniosas como vos, pero que no lograron una estabilidad financiera, son convenientemente ignoradas. Todos aquellos cuya iniciativa empresarial fracasó en lugar de prosperar, todos los que fueron despedidos en lugar de ascender, todos aquellos cuyas circunstancias familiares fueron menos afortunadas que las tuyas, todos los que tienen un color de piel, género, discapacidad o situación socioeconómica que les dificulta la vida más que a vos, simplemente no influyen en tu comprensión de cómo funcionan las cosas.


Tuviste suerte, y podés señalar a otras personas que también la tuvieron, y usás esos ejemplos para esconderte de la incómoda realidad de que fácilmente podrías haber sido vos quien podría estar llevándose la peor parte del capitalismo. Ves a un hombre desde tu ventana durmiendo en la vereda y te decís que hay una razón perfectamente válida por la que vos estás acá adentro, mientras él está allá afuera, y para que ese tango cognitivo funcione en tu cabeza, tenés que contarte un cuento de hadas.


Ahí es donde entra

la falacia del mundo justo

.


La falacia del mundo justo es un sesgo cognitivo que asume que todos reciben lo que se merecen: que a las personas buenas les pasan cosas buenas y a las personas malas les pasan cosas malas.


El atractivo de esta falacia es que nos da una sensación de control. Nos permite creer que nada malo nos sucederá si simplemente hacemos lo correcto y evitamos cometer errores estúpidos. También nos permite creer que merecemos toda la buena suerte que la vida nos ha brindado, y que los pobres existen porque no son tan virtuosos y sabios como nosotros.


El problema con la falacia del mundo justo es que sólo funciona si no pensás mucho sobre ella. Cualquiera que haya vivido unos pocos años sabe que a la gente buena le pasan cosas malas y a la gente mala le pasan cosas buenas. Todos lo hemos visto ocurrir innumerables veces, con personas que conocemos personalmente. El mundo simplemente no es justo. Si te va bien bajo el sistema actual, es solo porque tuviste suerte. Tenés lo que tenés por total, estúpida, suerte.


Si podés ser honesto con vos mismo al respecto, vas a entender por qué el sistema debe cambiar. Un sistema que insiste en mantener un sector muy amplio de la sociedad que debe sufrir y luchar duramente a lo largo de toda su vida no es un sistema justo ni moral. Nadie con una mente racional y una conciencia bien formada puede defenderlo.


Las personas que se oponen al movimiento hacia una sociedad más equitativa suelen acusar a los socialistas de “envidia” y “codicia”, pero eso no es más que una proyección; es su propia codicia y egoísmo lo que les impide reconocer sinceramente la naturaleza injusta de la sociedad en la que, por casualidad, terminaron en la cima.


Es cierto que quienes apoyan el socialismo suelen estar en una situación económica menos privilegiada que el defensor promedio del capitalismo, pero eso se debe únicamente a que tienen una perspectiva basada en la realidad sobre la naturaleza abusiva del

statu quo

 capitalista.


A quienes les ha ido bien bajo el capitalismo a menudo les cuesta más formarse una comprensión basada en la realidad del sistema en el que viven, porque tienen que abrirse camino a través de todos los cómodos sesgos cognitivos que insisten en que todo está más o menos bien tal como está. Si aún así insisten en que el capitalismo es genial, es solo porque su propia pereza intelectual, su ego y su cobardía moral les han impedido ver con realismo sus circunstancias.


Caitlin Johnstone es una periodista australiana. Escribe sobre política, economía, medios, feminismo y la naturaleza de la conciencia.

author: Eunice Stoltz
title: África do Sul abre portas para data centers, mas leis ainda tratam unidades como armazéns
content:
Essa matéria foi realizada com o apoio do Pulitzer Center e é parte do etapa africana da “Mão Invisível das Big Techs”, um projeto transnacional liderado pela Agência Pública e pelo Centro Latinoamericano de Investigación Periodística (CLIP).


Todos os dias, Ncediwe Vanqa, de 66 anos, caminha de sua casa de 18 m² em Barcelona, uma ocupação informal em Gugulethu, na Cidade do Cabo, até uma torneira comunitária. Vanqa chega a fazer esse percurso sete vezes por dia. Ela usa uma fossa comunitária e, em situações de emergência, um balde. Para economizar eletricidade, assa pão usando um aquecedor a parafina e aproveita o calor para aquecer sua casa.


No entanto, do outro lado da estrada, a menos de dois quilômetros de distância, a Cidade do Cabo abriu as portas para uma infraestrutura que pode operar em uma escala completamente diferente. Em julho, o Tribunal de Planejamento da cidade

aprovou

 um pedido apresentado pela King Air Industria, um parque industrial e logístico avaliado em dezenas de milhões de dólares, para dois data centers que, segundo documentos, ficarão a serviço da Equinix, uma multinacional norte-americana.


No entanto, a Equinix, uma das maiores operadoras de data centers do mundo e importante fornecedora de infraestrutura para empresas como Amazon, Microsoft e Google, nega essa versão dos fatos.


A expansão da empresa na Cidade do Cabo é o tema da nova reportagem do projeto transnacional “

A Mão Invisível das Big Techs

”, que investiga como as maiores empresas de tecnologia do mundo fazem lobby para influenciar leis e políticas públicas a fim de evitar a regulação em vários países.


A Equinix disse ao

The Continent

 que “não apresentou nenhum pedido de planejamento de data center na Cidade do Cabo”. 


Mas os registros oficiais do município mostram que a Equinix se reuniu com autoridades pelo menos três vezes para discutir seus planos. Dezenas de documentos também vinculam o pedido de uso do terreno ao projeto da Equinix para o local.


No centro da disputa está a quantidade de água e eletricidade que os data centers

hyperscale

 da Equinix irão exigir.

Data centers

hyperscale

 são conhecidos pelo consumo exorbitante de água e/ou eletricidade para resfriar as máquinas.


Em construção: do outro lado da estrada, data center da King Air Industries, na Cidade do Cabo, ficará a serviço da multinacional Equinix


Em seu recurso contra a construção de um desses empreendimentos na Cidade do Cabo, o Legal Resources Centre (LRC), uma organização legal da sociedade civil, estimou que, caso fosse utilizado um sistema convencional de resfriamento por evaporação, os dois data centers poderiam consumir cerca de 4,4 bilhões de litros de água por ano. 


Isso equivale a quase 11 milhões de litros por dia, aproximadamente o consumo diário de água de 68.500 moradores da Cidade do Cabo, com base na

referência de consumo médio

 da cidade. 


Para uma cidade que por pouco não chegou ao “Dia Zero” durante a seca de 2018, a demanda potencial é significativa. A data se referia a uma previsão de que registros de água das residências e do comércio da Cidade do Cabo

poderiam ser fechados

 por causa do baixo nível dos reservatórios.  


A Equinix não respondeu às perguntas sobre os recursos necessários para o data center proposto. No entanto, em seus documentos, a King Air informou ao Tribunal de Planejamento da Cidade do Cabo que os números sobre os recursos seriam apresentados na etapa de planejamento da instalação. 


Nos Estados Unidos, a expansão dos data centers vem enfrentando uma resistência cada vez maior das comunidades. Segundo a Data & Society, um instituto independente de pesquisa e políticas públicas sem fins lucrativos dos EUA, o consumo global de energia dos data centers

cresceu

 12% em cinco anos e pode dobrar até 2030. 


O uso de água também está aumentando. A organização afirma que o consumo da Meta, Apple, Microsoft e Google cresceu 60% desde 2020. À medida que os data centers se expandem nas comunidades, a Data & Society argumenta que a escolha dos locais onde são construídos se tornou uma decisão cada vez mais política, com consequências para as economias locais, a saúde e o abastecimento de água e energia.


Segundo os documentos apresentados ao Tribunal Municipal de Planejamento, o sistema proposto poderia demandar cerca de 174 MVA. “Se operados continuamente perto desse nível” ao longo do ano, os data centers poderiam consumir aproximadamente 1,4 a 1,5 bilhão de kWh de eletricidade …

author: Darío Aranda
title: El Niño despertó: lluvias extremas y olas de calor para un planeta en crisis climática
content:
Por Silvia Oliviero Ghietto*


La Organización Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) emitió un comunicado en el que advirtió que el fenómeno climático El Niño, que ya está en marcha, puede alcanzar una intensidad mayor que la habitual. En Argentina, a partir de noviembre-diciembre, aumenta la posibilidad de que ocurran

eventos de precipitaciones extremas en la Cuenca del Plata

 (integrada por Corrientes, Misiones, Formosa, Santa Fe, Entre Ríos, Buenos Aires, Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires y Chaco)

y en el Noroeste de la Patagonia

.


El Niño continúa intensificándose de forma constante combinado con océanos globales excepcionalmente cálidos y la probabilidad de un dipolo positivo en el Océano Índico, lo que determina una

probabilidad

de casi el 100 por ciento

 de un evento “muy fuerte”

. Por lo tanto, se espera que domine los patrones climáticos globales durante la temporada 2026-2027, con

aumento de probabilidad de temperaturas superiores a lo normal

 en gran parte del mundo y con cambios significativos en los patrones de lluvia, segúnel

C

entro de Predicción Climática de la Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica de Estados Unidos.


Las proyecciones científicas actuales sugieren que este El Niño podría convertirse en un evento comparable con algunos de los episodios más impactantes de las últimas décadas superando incluso el ocurrido en 1998. Los eventos de El Niño suelen alcanzar su punto máximo hacia finales del año, con la máxima influencia que suele sentirse entre noviembre y febrero.


Vale la pena aclarar que la Organización Meteorológica Mundial y las Instituciones de Referencia Climática clasifican los eventos de la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO) como débiles, moderados, fuertes o muy fuertes. Por lo tanto, el término "súper El Niño" utilizado por los medios de comunicación no forma parte del sistema de clasificación operativo y oficial.


Infografía: Organización Meteorológica Mundial


¿Que sabemos del fenómeno del Niño?


El Niño y La Niña son fases opuestas de

un patrón climático natural

 conocido como la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO), que

implica fluctuaciones de las temperaturas oceánicas en el Pacífico ecuatorial central y oriental, junto con cambios en la atmósfera

 suprayacente. Cuando la “Circulación Walker” (un flujo masivo de aire de este a oeste impulsado por las diferencias de temperatura y presión entre los océanos cálido occidental y el frío del este) se modifica desplazándose hacia el este en dirección a Sudamérica y la temperatura oceánica supera los 0,5 °C, se declara El Niño.


La transición entre estas fases extremas suele ocurrir cada dos a siete años. Tanto El Niño como La Niña generalmente comienzan a desarrollarse entre marzo y junio y alcanzan su máxima intensidad entre noviembre y febrero.


El Niño se caracteriza por temperaturas superficiales oceánicas inusualmente cálidas en el Pacífico

 central y oriental.

El nombre proviene de pescadores y marineros peruanos que notaron una corriente cálida

, asociada a la reducción de capturas de pescado, y la llamaron El Niño (probablemente porque se hacía visible en torno a Navidad).


El Niño se predice mediante el monitoreo de las condiciones en el océano Pacífico tropical. A través de modelos climáticos, la comunidad científica puede estimar cómo puede evolucionar en los próximos meses y

predecir patrones climáticos con seis meses de anticipación

. Se basa en una red global de observaciones, incluidos satélites, buques de océano, barcos de investigación y medidas atmosféricas operadas por los Servicios Meteorológicos y Hidrológicos Nacionales y Organizaciones Internacionales.


Desde la década de 1980, el enfoque dominante para medir o identificar El Niño ha sido el uso del Índice Oceánico Niño (ONI), que calcula a lo largo de un promedio de tres meses la Anomalía de Temperatura Superficial del Mar en una región específica del Pacífico llamada región Niño. En los últimos años y con la presencia del calentamiento global, una métrica más reciente llamada Índice Relativo Oceánico Niño (RONI) ha ganado terreno. Este enfoque mide el calentamiento relativo, no solo el absoluto, ayudando a la comunidad científica a evaluar si un evento de calentamiento está impulsado por el ENSO o se debe principalmente al calentamiento global oceánico.

author: Unknown
title: Indictment prepared against comedian Göktaş seeks 11-year prison sentence
content:
An indictment has been prepared against comedian Deniz Göktaş, who was detained and subsequently arrested over remarks he made during his show “Dead Sea” at the Harbiye Cemil Topuzlu Open-Air Theatre.


The indictment charges Göktaş with “insulting the President,” “inciting the public to hatred and hostility through the press,” and “praising a crime and a criminal.” Prosecutors are seeking up to 11 years and 2 months in prison for these charges.


The indictment was sent to the Istanbul 14th Criminal Court of First Instance.

author: groundxero
title: গৌরি লঙ্কেশ-এর পথে হেঁটে সাংবাদিকতার সাহসের নাম শাহিন, নাফিসা
content:
শাহিন, নাফিসার শরীরের প্রতিটি কালসিটে মনে করিয়ে দিক গৌরি লঙ্কেশ-এর লাল রক্তর কথা। আসলে তো ভয় নয়, সাহসই সংক্রামক।    


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তী 


 


“

ম্যায় এক ভারতীয় মুসলিম মহিলা পত্রকার হু।”


“আমি একজন ভারতীয় মুসলমান মহিলা সাংবাদিক।”


“I am an Indian Muslim woman Journalist.”


 


মাথার চুল থেকে পায়ের নখ পর্যন্ত ব্যাখ্যাতীত ট্রমা-য় আক্রান্ত, প্রবল শারীরিক যন্ত্রণার পাশাপাশি মানসিক আঘাতে বিপর্যস্ত সাংবাদিক নাফিসা খান, যখন সাংবাদিক সম্মেলনে বসে এ কথা বলছেন তখন তাঁর গলা কাঁপছে। কিন্তু সেই সাহসী গলার স্বরটুকু এতটাই জোরালো যে তা কাঁপিয়ে দিয়েছে এই দেশের, ভারত রাষ্ট্রের মাথা থেকে পা। 


 


এর ঠিক কয়েক ঘন্টা আগে, দিল্লি পুলিসের হাতে চরম নিগৃহীত হওয়ার পর, লাথি, চড় এবং লাঠির নৃশংস আঘাতে সারা শরীরে আঘাতের চিহ্ন নিয়ে তিনি যখন প্রায় সংজ্ঞাহীন, তখন বাড়ির মানুষের বুকে মুখ গুঁজে কাঁদছেন, তখন কেন তাঁকে মারা হয়েছে এই প্রশ্নের উত্তরে আতঙ্কে ঠেলে বেরিয়ে আসা চোখে তাকিয়ে থেকে এক নাগাড়ে আউড়ে যাচ্ছেন – ‘মুসলিম, মুসলিম, মুসলিম’।


 


কথায় বলে ভয় কেটে গেলে আর ভয় থাকে না। ফোর পিএম ইউ টিউব চ্যানেল-এর সাংবাদিক শাহিন খান আর নাফিসা খান দেখিয়ে দিয়েছেন ভয়ের মুখে, চরমতম আতঙ্কের মুখে কীভাবে সবটুকু সাহস এক করে রুখে দাঁড়াতে হয়। এবং মহিলা ও ধর্মীয় পরিচয়ে মুসলমান হওয়ার এই আন্তঃসম্পর্ক পেশাগরভাবে সাংবাদিক পরিচিতির থেকে যে আজকের ভারতবর্ষে দাঁড়িয়ে কোনোভাবেই বিচ্ছিন্ন হওয়ার নয়, তা এরচেয়ে স্পষ্টভাবে সম্ভবত আর বোঝার কোনো উপায় নেই। সাংবাদিক পরিচিতির সঙ্গে কেন লিঙ্গ পরিচিতি, ধর্ম-জাত-বর্ণের পরিচিতি সবকিছু জুড়ে যাচ্ছে, রাষ্ট্রের দমন-পীড়নের স্বাধীন, সৎ, সাহসী, বস্তুনীষ্ঠ গণমাধ্যমের টুঁটি যেভাবে টিপে ধরছে, তার রোজকার চিত্রটা সামনে আসলেই স্পষ্ট হয়ে যাচ্ছে। শাহিন আর নাফিসার ঘটনা  আবারও দেখিয়ে দেয় সরকার বাহাদুরের চোখে চোখ রেখে কথা বললে তার মাশুল গুনতে হয়।


 


তবে সাহসী শব্দটা শুধু বইতেই থাকে না। পুলিসি হেফাজতে বেআইনিভাবে তুলে নিয়ে যাওয়ার পর, সেখানে প্রাথমিকভাবে হেনস্থার পর যখন ধর্মীয় পরিচয় ঘটনাচক্রে জানতে পারে কর্তব্যরত পুলিসেরা তখন সেই পরিচয় তুলেই বলা হয় তাঁদের এবার আরো বেশি নির্মমভাবে মারা হবে। জল চাইলে বলা হয় পিপাসার্ত রেখেই মেরে ফেলা হবে। টানা ত্রিশ থেকে চল্লিশ মিনিট ধরে চলে নৃশংস মার। যার চিহ্ন দগদগে হয়ে আছে শাহিন আর নাফিসার সারা গায়ে। 


 


মার খেয়ে প্রায় অচৈতন্য অবস্থায় থাকার পর পরিবার, সহকর্মী, আন্দোলনকর্মীরা আসার পর, শাহিন বুম হাতে উঠে দাঁড়ান। সামনে কাওকে ফোন ধরিয়ে বলেন, “আপ রোল কিজিয়ে”। যে থানায় যে পুলিস কর্মীরা তাঁদের স্রেফ মুসলমান হওয়ার জন্য, সাংবাদিকতার আদর্শ মেনে দিল্লির মুখ্যমন্ত্রী আর দেশের স্বরাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রীকে কিছু প্রশ্ন করতে চাওয়ার ‘অপরাধে’ বেআইনিভাবে তুলে এনে মারতে মারতে প্রায় মেরেই ফেলছিল, সেখানে দাঁড়িয়ে তিনি নিজে নিজেদের ঘটনা ও সেই সময়ের পরিস্থিতির রিপোর্টিং করেন। তুলে ধরেন সত্য, তথ্য, যা বিকৃত করার উপায় থাকবে না গোদী মিডিয়ার, যা একমাত্র প্রতিরোধ। উচ্চপদস্থ পুলিস আধিকারিককে মুখের উপর বলেন ‘অন ক্যামেরা’ – “আপনি আমাদের বাঁচাননি। আমরা কোনক্রমে বেঁচেছি।”


 


শাহিন, নাফিসার মতো সাহস, চূড়ান্ত আক্রমণের সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে এবং যা নেমে এসেছে সরাসরি রাষ্ট্র চালিত পুলিসের মাধ্যমে, তা সাম্প্রতিক সময়ে স্বাধীন সাংবাদিকতার আবহেও বিরল। মনে রাখতে হবে তাঁদের পেছনে স্বাধীন সাংবাদিকতার ক্ষেত্রেরও কোনোও তথাকথিত বড় ব্র্যান্ড নেই। তাঁরা একেবারেই তরুণ। কিন্তু জানেন, সাংবাদিকতার সঠিক পাঠ মেনে প্রশ্ন করার মতো কলজের জোর থাকতে হয়। সেই প্রশ্ন করার পরিণতি এমন হতে পারে। মরে গেলে তা যেমন সাংবাদিককে কীভাবে নিজের জীবন দিয়ে দাম দিতে হয়, তা সামনে নিয়ে আসে, তেমনি, শাহিন, নাফিসার মতো বেঁচে গেলে নিজেরাই প্রমাণ দিতে পারেন, কীভাবে ফ্যাসিস্ট, সাম্প্রদায়িক রাষ্ট্র ব্যবস্থা প্রশ্ন গুঁড়িয়ে দিতে চায়। কিন্তু, হায়! বারেবারেই শাহিন, নাফিসারা ঋজু উঠে দাঁড়ান। 


 


দাঁড়াতেই হয়, কারণ সাংবাদিক পরিচয়ে কেউ স্বতন্ত্র ভরদ্বাজের মতো হিন্দুত্ববাদী, রাষ্ট্র পোষিত গুন্ডার সাক্ষাৎকার নেয় হাসি মুখে, আন্দোলনরত ছাত্রীর বাবার মাথার খুলি ফাটিয়ে চৌচির করে দিয়েও গ্রেফতার হয় না, দিল্লি পুলিসের জুতো পরে ঘোরে, লক্ষাধিক টাকা মাস খরচের জন্য কীভাবে যেন এসে যায় – এসব কথা স্বতন্ত্রর সামনে বসে শোনে বিনা প্রতিবাদে, বিনা প্রশ্নে। এই সাংবাদিকতাকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করার জন্যই মার খেতে খেতেও, প্রাণ থাকলে হাতে বুম নিয়ে উঠে দাঁড়ান শাহিন। ভয় কাটিয়ে নাফিসা দেশ জুড়ে হিন্দুত্ববাদী রাষ্ট্র ব্যবস্থার কানে পৌঁছায় এমন চিৎকারে বলতে পারেন – এই দেশে মুসলমান হওয়া কতটা বিপজ্জনক তিনি শুনেছিলেন, আর এবার দেখেও নিলেন, কিন্তু না তিনি নিজের পরিচয় ছাড়বেন, না সাংবাদিকতা। ধর্ম নিরপেক্ষ স্বাধীন ভারতের সংবিধান তাঁকে, তাঁদের সেই অধিকার দেয়।


 


৫ সেপ্টেম্বর গৌরি লঙ্কেশ-এর মৃত্যু দিবস। ৫ সেপ্টেম্বর এখন থেকে শাহিন আর নাফিসাকেও বারেবারে মনে করার দিন হয়ে থাক। বস্তারে, কাশ্মীরে, মণিপুরে যে মেয়েরা জাতি-ধর্ম-বর্ণ-আদিবাসী-মূলবাসী পরিচয় নিয়েই স্বাধীন সাংবাদিকতা করছেন তাঁদের মনে করার দিন হয়ে থাক। আজ এত বছর পর  – ‘গৌরি হম শর্মিন্দা হ্যায়/ তেরে কাতিল আভি জিন্দা হ্যায়’ এই কথার পাশাপাশি আমরা বলতে পারি “গৌরি হাম আভি ভি উম্মিদ পে খাড়ে হ্যায়/শাহিন, নাফিসা আভি জিন্দা …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Chinese Government Forces Artists to Withdraw from the Gwangju Biennale
content:
THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT has forced the withdrawal of Chinese artists from the Gwangju Biennale. This took place after the Gwangju Biennale reversed course on its decision to force Taiwanese artists to participate under the name “NTMOFA”, rather than as the “Taiwan Pavilion”, as they were originally supposed to.

As organized by the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts, that the Taiwanese artists were to participate as the “Taiwan Pavilion” was agreed on beforehand with organizers. Taiwanese artists had participated in the 2025 Gwangju Design Biennale under the name “Taiwan Pavilion” without incident.

Nevertheless, promotional images released by the Gwangju Biennale on its website instead censored any mention of Taiwan, so as to refer to the artists as displaying under “NTMOFA.” NTMOFA is an abbreviation of the National Taiwan Museum of Five Arts.

In response, ten Taiwanese artists and curators released a statement criticizing the Gwangju Biennale. The artists stated that efforts to negotiate with the Gwangju Biennale were ignored, and criticized what was termed “political censorship.”

Afterward, a group of South Korean artists, who referred to themselves as “Artists Against Censorship,” released their own statement. This statement criticized the actions of the Biennale, particularly as the Biennale was formed as a response to the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which opposed the military dictatorship of Chun Doo-hwan. As such, the statement emphasized that it was “disheartening to learn that such political censorship is being carried out in Gwangju, which is called the ‘hometown of Korean democracy.’”

The statement by Artists Against Censorship hit out at artistic censorship as a whole. The statement reads, “[I]n today’s international art world, artworks are being unilaterally altered or removed, exhibitions and speeches are being canceled, and artists and cultural workers are being forced into silence based on discriminatory and exclusionary perceptions of their nationality, race, gender, religion, and political stance. In particular, in a situation where the political and diplomatic pressures and economic influence of some countries unfairly interfere with the realm of cultural arts, the Biennale has the duty to […] to ensure the autonomy of exhibitions and creations.”

It proves disappointing, then, that the response from the Chinese government has been to instead punish Chinese artists by forcing them to withdraw from the exhibition–so as to pin the blame on Taiwanese artists for standing up for themselves. This would not be the first time that this has occurred.

In 2018, when the documentary Our Youth in Taiwan–which depicted the 2014 Sunflower Movement–won the Golden Horse Award for Best Documentary, the response from Chinese authorities was similar. Chinese participants in the award ceremony were forced to immediately depart. In the years to come, Chinese filmmakers were banned by their government from participating in the Golden Horse Awards.

It can be seen, then, that the Chinese government has a history of punishing its own artists as a way to hit back at Taiwan, depriving them of opportunities and forcing them to withdraw from international events that they are participating in. This more broadly reflects the Chinese government’s views of artists, seeing them as its property, and forcing them to comply with its will whenever it wishes to express geopolitical angst.

author: rti_admin
title: India’s Gen-Z Movement: Challenges Ahead for the Teachers and the Buddhist Way Forward
content:
The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, Minister of Education, Government of India (a Gen-X person born between 1965–1980), has come as a shock, as it was considered impossible to get a resignation from any minister of the Narendra Modi-led NDA government from 2014 till now. However, the students of Gen-Z (born between 1997–2012, now in the age group 14–29) made it possible, along with the Millennials (born between 1981–1996), Gen-X, and Gen-Alpha (born between 2013–2020). The Gen-Z students would be mostly from class 10th onwards, and some may be working professionals as well. The protests (mostly) by Gen-Z have shown the other generations that they have accomplished something that other generations could not have achieved in the last 12 years (although the support of other generations cannot be neglected). The Gen-Z students would then have a new level of confidence when they go to their classes and interact with their teachers. However, without the right guidance to channel it properly, this surge of confidence can easily tip into an obdurate, impudent, and supercilious attitude, turning their outlook entirely quixotic. Therefore, the role of teachers, supervisors, universities, institutes, etc., would come into the picture, and they would have to face certain challenges. The challenges mentioned are not exhaustive; instead, they are suggestive.

The first challenge that universities/institutes (overall) and individual teachers as well would face is: Are the Gen-Z students going to listen (śravaṇa in Sanskrit—the first step of learning) to their teachers and universities? Are they going to follow the rules and regulations of the university/institute and maintain the decorum of the classes? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students, with their creativity of language and presentation, have shut the mouths of many mainstream media channels and politicians, and have also astonished political scientists who never expected the occurrence of this nation-wide protest (if not in India, then at least not under the present government). These students have not been in the mood to listen to anything that has no bearing on the government’s accountability for the suicides of many NEET aspirants. This is understandable considering the seriousness of the issue. However, some videos have shown that students have hooted at the biased media channels, as they have been determined not to listen to anything from them.

The second challenge deals with humility and humbleness. Humility is an important aspect of learning. Learning results in humility (as said, vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ). Learning also results from humility—if I think that I am superior to others in terms of knowledge, how can I learn from others? I would then do whatever I think is fit according to ‘me’, even if that act disrespects someone. Are the Gen-Z students going to contemplate their continuous learning from life (manan in Sanskrit—the second step for learning), or would they feel supercilious? Are the Gen-Z students going to be in the disposition to learn from their teachers? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students have already contemplated the inevitable consequences of the ruining of the country if the lacuna in education is not fixed. For this, they have raised their voice for their right to education, and thereby they have taught the world the peaceful management of crowds, connecting people, and leading a crowd. However, this same sense of achievement may let them feel that they know everything. It is also possible that they may not contemplate new learning, reflect deeply, or sharpen their arguments and creativity. Rather, they may take refuge in harsh and abusive language to assert their points, which has already been seen in the protests by some of the students. This aggression might block any novel and meaningful discoveries in their learning journey.

The third challenge is the continuity and culmination of the above two and deals with real-life experiences (nidhidhyāsana). The real-life experiences of unexpected events occur only when we listen to others and continuously contemplate them. Without that, we would continuously live in one set of habituated thinking caused by our external environments. But by continuously listening to others, like our well-wishers—teachers, parents, friends, etc.—and critics, we would be able to contemplate and improve our habituated practices. But without checks and balances …

title: Serok Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê kir
content:
Roja Şemiyê 22ê Tebaxa 2026an Serok Mesûd Barzanî pêşwaziyê li birêz Rado Botom, Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê li Herêma Kurdistanê kir. Di hevdîtinê de Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê li Herêma Kurdistanê ku bi boneya bidawîhatina erkên xwe û malavayîkirinê serdana Serok Barzanî kiribû, her wiha pîrozbahiyê li Serok Barzanî kir bi boneya wergirtina Nîşana Asta Bilind a Papayê Pîrozê Vatîkanê û, rola dîrokî ya Serok Barzanî di parastina mafê pêkhatan û kûrkirina kultura pêkvejiyan û hevgirtinê di navbera hemû pêkhatên neteweyî û olî yên Kurdistan û Iraqê de bilind nirxand. Her di wê hevdîtinê de Serok Barzanî spasiya Papayê Pîrozê Vatîkanê kir û tekez li ser wê yekê kir ku em serbilind in bi wê yekê ku kultura dewlemend a pêkvejiyan û hevgirtina di navbera ol û neteweyên cuda de ji me re maye û wê piştrastiyê jî da ku ew kultur dê parastî bimîne û kûrtir bibe. Her wiha destxweşiyê li erk û keda Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê kir di dema karê wî de li Herêma Kurdistanê û hêviya serkeftinê jê re xwest. author: Unknown
title: 34th International Kurdish Culture Festival ends with message of “unity among Kurds”
content:
Following Abdullah Öcalan’s message, the 34th International Kurdish Culture Festival continued with speeches alongside cultural and artistic events, with slogans of “There can be no peace without a leader” rising from the crowd. Kurds from Kurdistan and their friends gathered at the festival grounds, continuing the festive atmosphere with music and traditional halay dances, while speeches from the stage emphasized the importance of preserving the Kurdish people’s language, culture, and identity. The festival’s music program continued with performances by Nahîde and Rizgar Hewramanî, while TEV-ÇAND artist Hekîm Sefkan also addressed the festival audience.


We kept our culture alive for 34 years


Drawing attention to the fact that the International Kurdish Culture Festival has continued uninterrupted for 34 years, Sefkan said the festival should not be viewed merely as a cultural and artistic event. Sefkan added that for 34 years they have gathered in the same venues to keep Kurdish culture alive, emphasizing the importance of efforts in Europe to preserve the Kurdish language and culture.


Sefkan said: “For 34 years, we have been working together in these places to keep our culture alive. We have always worked to preserve our language and culture here, in Europe. This festival is not merely a cultural and artistic event; it is also an expression of the national struggle.”


Drawing attention to the significance of the festival in the struggle to preserve the Kurdish people’s identity and sense of belonging, Sefkan said that one of the fundamental aims of the Martyrs of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement was to protect the Kurdish people’s language, culture, and identity. Emphasizing that the values created by the martyrs must be kept alive, Sefkan said: “The struggle of our martyrs, their purpose in life, was to protect our language, culture, identity, and sense of belonging. We salute their martyrdom. We once again reiterate that we will keep alive the values they created and continue along the path of their struggle.”


Sefkan added that the culture of Kurdistan should not be viewed as being limited solely to the values of the Kurdish people, adding that they also embrace the cultural and artistic values of the different peoples living in Kurdistan. Stating that the cultures of Arab, Assyrian, and Turkmen peoples are also regarded as values of Kurdistan, Sefkan continued: “We have valued our culture as well as the art and values of the other peoples of Kurdistan—the Arabs, Assyrians, and Turkmen. We have regarded them as values of Kurdistan. It has always been this way, and it will remain this way. We have always prioritized all the values and all the peoples of Kurdistan.”


Sefkan underlined that the individuals whose deaths as martyrs have been announced recently also lost their lives for this struggle and these values, stating that the martyrs’ struggle was connected to preserving the freedom, culture, and identity of the Kurdish people. “Their martyrdoms have been announced and made public recently,” Sefkan said, emphasizing that the martyrs’ struggle and aspirations were connected to the freedom of the people. “They struggled to protect our culture and identity. We owe them a debt. That is why we say once again: Martyrs never die.”

author: groundxero
title: After the Dissolution of the SDF: Time for the Left to Rethink the Kurdish Question
content:
The events of 2026 have demonstrated the fragility of nationalist entities that rely heavily on support from major powers.


 


Rezgar Akrawi


This article was produced by 

Globetrotter

.


 


The People’s Palace Scene: The End of an Experiment and the Beginning of a Question


 


On 25 August 2026, Mazloum Abdi 

announced

 from the People’s Palace in Damascus the end of the mission of the 

Syrian Democratic Forces

 (SDF) and their dissolution as an independent military force, alongside the dissolution of the Autonomous Administration and its affiliated military and civilian structures and their integration into the institutions of the Syrian state. This announcement followed the extensive military operation in January, which paved the way for a negotiating track that culminated in the 

integration

 of its forces and institutions within the Syrian state.


 


The conclusion of this armed conflict and the avoidance of further ethnic warfare are generally assessed as positive developments,  given the victims of such wars are ultimately the working men and women, both manual and intellectual, from various ethnicities. Although the agreement reduced the likelihood of war and spared the region’s masses further destruction, critics note it omitted clear provisions regarding the issues by the left,  such as women’s rights, the secularization of the state, halting privatization, protecting the public sector, guaranteeing the rights of working men and women, both manual and intellectual, and holding democratic elections for all officials.


 


This development raises broader questions to the left. The model presented for years by a broad segment of the Kurdish and international left as a grassroots social, feminist, and democratic revolution ended with a top-down decision announced from a presidential palace, without a popular referendum and without a clear decision from the councils and communes that were presented to the world as holding actual authority within the Autonomous Administration. Furthermore, the United States, which provided the SDF with substantial military and political 

support

, was a key actor in shaping the course of the war and, ultimately, its resolution. This reveals the limits of relying on major imperialist powers.


 


At the same time, a portion of the military and party elite within the SDF were absorbed into the institutions of the new state and given important positions, despite the authoritarian and conservative religious character of the new political order, while the Kurdish, Arab, Syriac, and other communities continue to face their economic, social, and political challenges.


 


Significant gains were achieved for the Kurds, including recognition as an integral part of the Syrian people, recognition of the Kurdish language as a national language and Nowruz as a national holiday, and the annulment of the effects of the 1962 Al-Hasakah census. These are real gains that generations have fought for, and they must be constitutionally entrenched so they are not left dependent on decrees that could be altered. 

Concerns

 are heightened due to the nature of the new authority in Damascus and its record of repression and violations, and the absence of clear and binding guarantees. Therefore, transforming national and democratic rights into constitutional guarantees is a fundamental part of any genuine political transition.


 


The Contradiction Between Rhetoric and Practice


 


A large part of the left was drawn to the concept of “

Democratic Confederalism

” and the theories of Abdullah Öcalan, viewing the Autonomous Administration experience as a model transcending the nation-state. However, practice revealed contradictions between the rhetoric of grassroots democracy and the concentration of military and financial decision-making in the hands of unaccountable party cadres.


 


Furthermore, the heavy reliance on American funding and military support tied the project to the calculations of a major imperialist power. When the priorities of this power shifted, the fragility of the model quickly became apparent. In 2018, as an observer of this region I warned about the vulnerability of such an alliance with the United States.This is an important lesson for any movement that presents itself as liberatory or revolutionary: an independent project cannot be built by relying on a major power, especially American imperialism, whose primary concern is the protection of its own …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taitung Graft Probe Highlights Recurrent Issues of Rural Corruption
content:
ISSUES REGARDING local corruption are again in the news, with a number of pan-Blue Taitung city councilors questioned about the use of public funds to build a resort.

The resort, the Dongying International Resort, is linked to the family of Taitung County Council Speaker Wu Hsiu-hua. In May, independent city councillor Lin Tsan-tian raised during a county council meeting that public funds had been used to expand a road leading to the Dongying International Resort. Though the road was originally supposed to be three meters wide, it was expanded to nine meters wide. Reportedly, the road is also at least partly on state-owned land. For its part, Taitung authorities claimed the road was to benefit local farmers and prevent accidents, though no accidents had occurred on the road in the past decade.

What raised suspicion was that the discretionary funding of several city councilors was used on the road. Lin pointed to that while county councilors usually use discretionary funding to help repair roads or assist farmers to construct water tanks, they do not usually pool their discretionary funding on a road in this way.

In the wake of Lin’s questioning, a probe was launched. Seven city councilors have been questioned to date, six of whom are members of the KMT, and one of whom is a member of the People First Party. Wu was recently endorsed by Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen of the KMT in the upcoming elections.

Nevertheless, issues of corruption are far from unheard of in rural areas in Miaoli. Recently, KMT Legislative Caucus Leader Fu Kun-chi, who represents Hualien, came under scrutiny after former Financial Times journalist Kathrin Hille referenced widespread vote buying in Hualien during an interview on FTV.

Fu has long faced allegations of vote buying, not only in Hualien, but in the KMT Central Standing Committee election. Fu’s wife, Hsu Cheng-wei, is currently Hualien county magistrate, and she originally took up the post after Fu was arrested on corruption charges. Prior to his jailing, Fu divorced Hsu and named her deputy county commissioner to skirt nepotism laws, leading to a lawsuit against him over a fake divorce. Though Fu was previously kicked out of the KMT for his actions, he has since been welcomed back in because of his ability to win elections, and consequently risen to become KMT legislative caucus leader.

Other recent cases of high-profile corruption have also involved pan-Blue county magistrates. In January 2025, former Nantou county magistrate Lee Chao-ching, a former KMT member, was sentenced on charges totaling 656 years and four months in jail.

Charges facing Lee were mostly regarding kickbacks for reconstruction projects after Typhoon Morakot, which struck Taiwan in August 2009. Lee reportedly demanded 10% in kickbacks for reconstruction projects, which were passed to him in gift boxes of tea and fruit.

In December 2024, former Yilan county magistrate Lin Zi-miao was sentenced to 12.5 years in jail on charges of corruption. The charges against Lin date to 2022, when Lin came under scrutiny in connection to a development project on a 108-hectare plot of land in Luodong that was originally protected. However, the land was later rezoned for agricultural use in 2018, though residential building construction and public infrastructure development were allowed on the plot. The plot’s rezoning, as well as related land disputes, were seen as suggesting lawbreaking. This was quickly linked to Lin, seeing as the purchaser of the plot of land after its rezoning was Lin Shu-mei’s son. Lin Shu-mei, a former member of the National Assembly before its abolition, is Lin Zi-miao’s cousin and is a fellow member of the KMT.

Lin then came under scrutiny for checks worth over 100 million NT received by Lin or her family members from former KMT legislator Yang Chi-hsiung. Yang was known to have had a close relationship with Lin when he served as legislator, assisting Lin electorally. Likewise, several of Lin Zi-miao’s children worked in a mining company under Yang’s name.

Issues of local corruption continue to be commonplace in Taiwan, then. It is to be seen if charges stick in Taitung or, as with so many other cases, they simply bounce off.

author: rti_admin
title: India’s Unfinished Independence
content:
Every August 15, the flag goes up over the Red Fort, the anthem plays in every school and University for a day to celebrate being free. We call it Independence Day — the day India stopped being ruled by the British after two hundred years. And I celebrate it too. But every year, sitting with it a little longer than a headline or a holiday usually gets, one question won’t leave me. Free from what, exactly, and free for whom? The British extracted our wealth, silenced us, and treated us like subjects and inhumane instead of people. They eventually left. But did the thing they left behind actually go with them? Seventy-five-plus years later, many people are still living under a kind of threat, inhuman, and subject to no major change, and the political power is transferred from one hand to another. That time, foreign rule, and the present time, the elite and the oppressed class. caste, patriarchy, or social hierarchy systems- nobody ever really dismantled them, just handed them down like inheritance. The face in charge changed. For too many people, the situation underneath it didn’t. None of this is me rejecting the freedom we won or the people who died for it. It’s me refusing to let “freedom” become something we wave on a flagpole once a year without looking at who still doesn’t have it. After independence, many have hope for major change. We are ruling ourselves at least; nobody discriminates against us, but it is only theoretical, not practical.

We, the people of India, aren’t one religion. We’re not just Hindu, or just Muslim, or Christian, or Sikh — and the Constitution doesn’t lean on any of that in its opening line. It says: “India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.” That’s a bigger sentence than it looks. India was never built to belong to one group. Many people are sacrificing their lives, their homes, their hope, their relatives, etc., every family, every tongue, every tradition, without asking anyone to give up who they are to be let in. The Constitution doesn’t just govern us. It protects the different ways we live, our culture, tradition, and language. But that raises a fair question: why does a free people need a document telling them how to live? If human beings are born free, shouldn’t that be enough on its own? For most of history, freedom on paper and freedom in real life were two completely different things. Before the Constitution, millions of people on this land weren’t fully recognized as human, and they were denied all human rights. No education, no right to object to injustice out loud, no fundamental rights. treated as animals; they were not counted as citizens. Two hundred years of British rule made all of that worse, and many people gave everything to end it. Even now, it’s worth asking: is that independence something everyone actually gets to feel, or is it still a promise some people are still waiting on? The Ambedkar Constitution is not just a rulebook. They wrote down a vision; it is a way of life, what Ambedkar called Prabuddha Bharat, an “Enlightened India” where every person could live with dignity and respect, no exceptions. A constitution isn’t a book or a scripture. It’s that imagination of a glorious society, made enforceable.

When Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and the others wrote the Constitution, they weren’t just setting up a government. They were imagining a civilization. Ambedkar called it Prabuddha Bharat — an Enlightened India — where a person’s caste, gender, religion, or birth wouldn’t determine how freely they could move, speak, or live. Liberty, equality, and fraternity weren’t supposed to just sit in the preamble looking nice. They were supposed to be alive. On the eve of the Constitution’s adoption, Ambedkar warned that India was walking into a life full of contradictions — political equality on paper, and deep social and economic inequality in daily life. He said if that contradiction were allowed to go unaddressed, the people suffering under it would eventually blow up the whole structure of political democracy. That warning is still hanging over us, mostly ignored. Caste wasn’t invented by the British — it existed long before them, and it outlived them too. Dalits and Adivasis still face discrimination in villages, in workplaces, in schools, and even in death — separate cremation grounds, separate wells, and separate seating still exist in parts of this country. People still get attacked over things as small as riding a horse to their own wedding, wearing certain …

author: Danilo Arao
title: Kapamilya
content:
At least 5,000 workers have been retrenched since the shutdown (Photo by Carlo Manalansan / Bulatlat)

Sa ngayon, tahimik ang mga lansangan. Pero hindi permanente ang pananahimik.

Posibleng huling pagbisita. Pero sana’y maulit pa hangga’t hindi pa huli ang lahat.

Sa halip na phone patch o Zoom interview na madalas na nangyayari, naisipan nilang gawin ang panayam sa mismong studio ng ABS-CBN. Nangangahulugan itong muling pagbisita sa gusaling medyo kabisado na dahil wala namang masyadong nagbago sa mga nakaraang dekada.

Alam pa rin ang mesa o estasyon ng mga kakilala’t kaibigan, lalo na ang mga dating estudyante sa Unibersidad ng Pilipinas (UP). Wala pa ring nagbago sa lokasyon ng mga kubeta kaya alam ang pupuntahan kung kailangang tugunan ang tawag ng kalikasan.

Siyempre’y likas pa rin ang ngiti’t pagbati, lalo na sa mga saksi sa nangyari noong 2020. Sa mga medyo bata pang staff at reporter, may mga nakipagkamay at nagpakilala. Ganyan talaga ang mga may alam sa kasaysayan at kolektibong paninindigan.

Halata ang saya sa pagkikita pero iba ang pahiwatig ng mga mata. Tila may gustong sabihin pero huwag muna. Tulad ng ibang newsroom, abala kasi ang lahat sa pagbabalita ng nagmamadaling kasaysayan.

Pero halata namang may kakaiba sa ABS-CBN newsroom sa kasalukuyan dahil sa hindi katanggap-tanggap na nakaraan. Anim na taon ang nakalipas mula nang ipagkait ng mga nasa kapangyarihan ang broadcast franchise nito. Tuwang-tuwa ang mga bulag na tagasuporta ng nakaraang administrasyon. Sa loob-loob nila, “Sa wakas, napatahimik ang kritiko!”

Pero nanahimik nga ba? Kung ano ang ingay para ipaglaban ang kalayaan sa pamamahayag, mas tumindi pa mula nang marinig ang mga baluktot na depensa ng maraming personaheng may kakabit na “His Excellency” o “Honorable” sa pangalan.

Sabi nila, walang kinalaman sa kalayaan sa pamamahayag ang pagpapasara dahil simpleng paglabag lang ito sa regulasyon tungkol sa prangkisa. Pero ilang beses nang napabulaanan ang mga walang batayang akusasyon tulad ng diumanong hindi pagbabayad ng buwis, dayuhang pagmamay-ari at pagpapakalat ng pekeng balita.

Dahil isinapubliko ang pagdinig sa Kamara de Representantes noong 2020, saksi ang buong Pilipinas sa sinabi ng isang mambabatas na nagagalit siya sa ABS-CBN dahil hindi iniulat ang pamimigay niya ng bigas. Ito rin ang mambabatas na binanggit ngayong taon lang na bayaran daw ang karamihan sa midya. Kahit na nakakulong siya sa kasalukuyan dahil sa isang non-bailable na kaso, wala pa ring hustisya dahil wala pang napapanagot sa naging maling desisyon ng Kongreso tungkol sa ABS-CBN.

Hahayaan na lang ba ang nangyari? Tama bang “Move on!” ang maging perspektiba dahil sinabi ng pamunuan ng ABS-CBN na hindi na kasama sa kanilang estratehiya ang aplikasyon para sa bagong prangkisa? Nararapat bang tumahimik na lang dahil naibenta na ang mga ari-arian, partikular ang lupang kinatitirikan ng gusali?

Batay sa impormasyong isinapubliko, ang tatlong ektaryang lupain ng ABS-CBN ay nasa kamay na ng Ayala Land, Inc. Magtatayo raw ng “mixed use commercial and residential development.” Posibleng magkakaron ng condominium units, office rental spaces, commercial centers at kahit na shopping malls kung pagbabatayan ang mga proyekto nito sa Cloverleaf, Arca South at Makati Central Business District.

Ano kaya ang plano sa ABS-CBN Main Broadcast Building, Dolphy Theater at ang Millennium Transmitter? Tuluyan bang gigibain ang mga ito sa kabila ng halaga nito sa kasaysayan ng midya sa Pilipinas?

Bilang paghahanda sa demolisyon, nakasara na ang Sgt. Esguerra main gate na ilang beses na pinasok at pinaradahan. Kaya sa pagpasok muli sa gusali, kailangang dumaan sa side entrance. Nakaparada pa rin ang maraming sasakyan ng ABS-CBN pero halatang marurumi na ang iba dahil hindi na masyadong nagagamit.

Sa loob ng gusali, may mga nagtatrabaho pa rin pero may ilang lugar na halos wala nang tao. Halatang medyo napapabayaan na ang ilang bahagi dahil hindi na masyadong nalilinis. Ang studio na pinagdausan ng taping, malinis naman pero halatang make-shift na lang at hindi permanente. Kung sabagay, nalalapit na ang paglipat para magbigay-daan sa mga bagong may-ari.

Pagkatapos ng taping at habang hinihintay ang sasakyang maghahatid pabalik sa kampus, pansamantalang nakausap ang isang taga-ABS-CBN. Maraming off-the-record na napagkuwentuhan. Halata ang lungkot sa nangyari noong 2020. Nang mapag-usapan ang isang nakakulong na mambabatas, pinagkuwentuhan ang “karma” sa kabila ng patuloy na …

author: Nick Reich
title: Fed up with FedEx
content:
On any given day, the FedEx facility in the Melbourne suburb of Tullamarine is a hub of activity, as trucks roar in and out of huge warehouses amid clouds of diesel smoke. On 28 August, something new cut through the routine noise. Just after 8am, hundreds of workers walked off the job, along with thousands of others around the country, costing FedEx millions. As the workers marched defiantly up the driveway, they were met by Transport Workers Union (TWU) officials there with flags to show support.

The previous week, 91 percent of FedEx workers had voted to strike for two hours, after management offered them a previously rejected agreement without any improvements.

The union is asking for an above-inflation pay rise, job security measures that limit AI usage and an end to direct service contracts. FedEx uses these contracts to employ third party drivers without the rights or protections of employees, and they are paid piece rates rather than wages. According to the union, contractors are under pressure to make deliveries every four minutes, which leads to dangerous road conditions not only for the contractors but also for other motorists. Road transport is already the most dangerous industry in Australia—according to the government’s quarterly heavy vehicle road deaths report, in the year to March 2026, 225 people were killed in incidents involving heavy vehicles.

In response to workers voting for a two-hour strike and walking off, FedEx locked them out for the entire day.

I attended their action to show solidarity as a socialist and TWU workplace delegate. Some of the workers I spoke to had been with the company for decades, while for others, this was their first strike. Consistently, the workers expressed anger towards FedEx management, and a keenness to escalate the fight.

“I left Ceva, around the corner, because of bad management” one worker, who was on strike for the first time, told me, “but the same things come up here all the time. Disrespect for the workers”. A longer-term worker said, “I’ve been with this company for 25 years, from when it was TNT to now. It’s always been the same, but especially now this American company thinks they can bring in their model, as if we’re the same as America over here”. The US company, FedEx, bought Australian trucking company TNT in 2016. FedEx has a long history of anti-union practices and undercutting wages. It made more than $4 billion profit last year. 

This strike comes right in the middle of a pivotal year for the TWU’s “Our roads, our skies, our futures” campaign. The day before the FedEx strike, I was at a TWU-run delegates training session. At that, Sam Lynch, lead organiser of the Victorian/Tasmanian branch of the union, explained that a key aim of the campaign is to stop the new operators who are entering the industry in significant numbers from undercutting and driving down workers’ conditions. The union wants to organise workers at these new trucking companies to protect wages and conditions across the industry.

Another is to improve the conditions in unionised companies. To do this, the union is attempting to line up all the major road transport agreements to expire around the same time. Having them all being renegotiated simultaneously opens up the potential for joint, industry-wide industrial action. The union has used this to strengthen its hand at the bargaining table, and the Murdoch press has even run a few stories about the potential chaos an industry-wide strike would cause.

While this all sounds good, the TWU has so far been reluctant to push for the sort of serious industrial action that would be needed to win real gains. Social media posts, press releases and speeches to delegates often labour the point that strikes are a difficult and undesirable last resort. They fail to mention how powerful and unifying strikes can be, especially when they are big enough to cause real problems for the bosses. The TWU leadership have never seriously raised the prospect of industry-wide strikes with members, and they have already signed contracts with two major companies, Linfox and Team Global Express, which weakens the potential for a real industry-wide campaign.

2026 is a key test for the TWU’s strategy, and so far, it isn’t looking like the major surge forward it could have been. There is little advantage that industry-wide bargaining can deliver at the negotiating table if the prospect of industry-wide strikes is so remote that it barely qualifies as …

title: “There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band touring Australia …”
content:
I was contacted a little while ago by somebody raising concerns about a couple of upcoming black metal gigs. Below is the text they sent.

There’s this sketchy Dutch black metal band, Helleruin, playing in Melbourne at the Northcote Social Club on September 11 and in Sydney at Crowbar on September 12.

Most of Helleruin’s records have been released on New Era Productions, which has put out a number of releases by fash black metal bands and which is run by Jasper Velzel, a NSBM and RAC musician. In addition, another project of Helleruin’s Carchost — Orewoet — is on the label Heidens Hart, which — along with releasing some far-right stuff — is owned by a former live guitarist of prominent fash band Graveland.

Moreover, a number of the local supporting acts have sketchy connections.

Order of Orias, one of two supports in Melbourne along with Petrol (see below), are on World Terror Committee, which releases fashy stuff and is owned by Sven Zimper, a member of prominent NSBM group Absurd.

Of the bands playing Sydney with Helleruin (Krvna, Pestilential Shadows, Destruktor, Vicissitude, Gravgöt, Grotesque Bliss, Petrol, Blasfemancia and Akhoth) at the ‘Call from the Grave’ festival:

Pestilential Shadows have released music on the Chinese label, GoatowaRex, who are very friendly to NSBM acts. Additionally, PS is part of a collective called Ordo Ater Anguis/Order of the Black Serpent, which includes numerous far right acts. Michael W Ford of Black Funeral appears to be a former Order of Nine Angles (09A) member in the United States who — after distancing himself from O9A — attempted to formulate a social Darwinist version of the Satanic Temple (lol), which coalesce around the Australian fash-friendly label, Dark Adversary. Indeed, one of the members of PS is also a member of Varw, a band on Dark Adversary. Further, Akhoth released a demo, ‘Storm of Pagan Fury’, on CD on Dark Adversary this year.

Grotesque Bliss are on Iron Bonehead which, along with the suspect name, appears to be run by a (if only barely) crypto-fascist.

Destruktor is on a label, Hells Headbangers, which has previously released and re-released stuff by Satanic Warmaster and Deströyer 666, including re-releasing Deströyer 666’s debut album, ‘Unchain the Wolves’, on a few different mediums over the last few years. Additionally, Inquisition had a few releases on Hells Headbangers after their lead singer (who is also a Satanist pedo) released openly fash music on fash label Satanic Skinhead Propaganda (a label which the Iron Bonehead guy sold in his old fash-friendly record store).

The most recent (2024) EP of Krvna, formally of PS, was released on Zazen Sounds, run by Greek nazi black metaller Acherontass of Αχέροντας (Krvna played guest guitar on their most recent album). For what it’s also worth, Third Eye Temple — the Polish label on which Krvna’s 2022 album was released — have released one split and re-issued an EP by Voidhanger, a side project of Polish far right black metallers, Infernal War.

Finally, Petrol were previously on a cancelled bill with Gurn. They also played a gig with Japanese band Abigail, who are signed to Nuclear Now Productions, a fash-friendly label linked to Iron Bonehead (similarly exposed by the nsbmboneheads blog linked above). In addition, Petrol played at Crowbar Sydney last year with Bolzer (see nsbmboneheads blog), who released all but their last record on Iron Bonehead. The other headliner was Portal, who have released lots of records on Hells Headbangers including, recently, a split with Blood of Kingu — a side-project of the Ukrainian ultra-nationalists from Drudkh — on the label in 2014.

author: Alma Torlakovic
title: ‘Working 9 to 5, should be able to make a living’—Sydney Uni staff shut down campus over pay, conditions
content:
The first strike of Sydney University staff in our new enterprise agreement campaign was a banger. The campus was a ghost town, with very few people even attempting to enter. Services were disrupted all over because significant numbers of staff were on strike or “absent” in solidarity. All the libraries closed for the day, and classes were cancelled or rescheduled.

The picket line was well-attended, jubilant and colourful. About 600 staff and students set up pickets around campus entrances from 7am. Between chanting classic union slogans, talking to passersby and arguing with people to turn around and not work today, we found time to sing and dance.

By far the most popular song of the day was “9 to 5”, by Dolly Parton. It’s just what a striking worker wants to hear, and you gotta admit, it’s contagious:

Working 9 to 5, what a way to make a living

Barely getting by, it’s all taking and no giving

They just use your mind, and they never give you credit

It’s enough to drive you crazy if you let it (but you won’t let it)

Parton’s song sums up exactly how we’re feeling at the moment, barely able to keep up with rent, mortgages and bills. With all the added mental and physical stress of counting every dime to make ends meet, we’re somehow still expected to perform our jobs to a high standard. And accept that management doesn’t really care for our lives or opinions.

The collective solidarity at the pickets was a natural antidote to the everyday experience of being at work. You look around the campus and see that nothing is moving without us, and suddenly, we don’t feel so disposable.

Staff brought their own placards, and food to share. We spent the day sharing stories and reasons for why we’re on strike. At the Parramatta Road main gate picket, we played a fun guessing game we dubbed “The Price is Outrageous!” to highlight the cost-of-living crisis.

An all-in rally culminated outside the vice-chancellor’s administration building with more chanting and speeches.

The strike was for 24 hours, and we will need many more if we are to win. NTEU Fightback, a rank-and-file group within the National Tertiary Education Union, argues that regular and well-planned strikes are the only effective tool our side has.

Management has a suite of proposed attacks on our conditions. They want to make it easier to push through redundancies. They want to deploy AI, threatening job security, the quality of our jobs, and the education and services we provide. And they want us to trust that they’ll do so on an ethical basis with staff rights at heart.

They won’t commit to serious action on de-casualisation, instead proposing to introduce more teaching-focused roles that break the teaching-research nexus.

The union has a lot to win as well. We are seeking a 20 percent pay rise (notably, we initially voted for 25 percent, but this was quashed by our own national office). We want recognition that staff wages have gone backwards by tens of thousands since 2021 due to sub-inflation pay rises. We are still pressuring management to commit to enforceable targets for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander employment, improved disability rights, an academic workload allocation policy based on how much time the work actually takes, intellectual freedom, and an increase in severance pay for professional staff.

Alma Torlakovic is a member of the NTEU branch committee, the NTEU national council and is the NSW Socialists candidate for Granville in the March 2027 state election.

title: March for White Australia : August 30, 2026
content:
On August 30, M4WA supporters will again be reclaiming the streets for White Australia, ‘remigration’ and — of course — #FreezePeach.

The march takes place on the first anniversary of the previous march in Melbourne/Naarm and the subsequent, celebratory attack on Camp Sovereignty by local neo-Nazis belonging to Tom Sewell’s (now-proscribed) National Socialist Network. Over a dozen men were charged over that matter: Nathan Matthew Bull, Haymish Busscher, Blake Cathcart, Billy Michael Conheady, Jake Crockett, Zack Steven Dewaard, Augustus Coolie Hartigan, Jaeden Bernard Johnson, Timothy Holger Lutze, Michael Nelson, Michael Saarinen, Thomas Sewell, Ryan Williams and Yan Zakharin. Of these, Zakarin has been deported back to Ukraine, and earlier this month, ‘Jaeden Johnson, Zack Dewaard, Blake Cathcart and Timothy Lutze pleaded guilty to one charge each of violent disorder, with Johnson and Lutze also pleading guilty to committing an indictable offence while on bail’. Lutze failed to attend a court hearing on August 14 and it was subsequently reported that he was, in fact, dead. Cases against the others allegedly involved in the attack are otherwise making their way through the courts.

As for M4WA in 2026, while Bec Walker (now known as FightForAustralia) once led the charge from Sydney, on this occasion property developer scion Hugo Lennon (like Australia’s leading neo-Nazi website, also sponsored by Facebook) — having wrested control of their socials from Walker — has appointed himself the Sir Topham Hatt of the racist carnival. Joining him will be his frens in the (former) NSN, Matt Trihey and his NWA and, presumably, an unknown number of PHONy supporters and other right-wing bizarr0s.

Anyway, while Trans Queer Solidarity has announced a protest event, a Rock Against Racism gig has been organised at Camp Sovereignty on Sunday afternoon.
