author: Isaac Nellist
title: Lessons from One Nation’s Secret Harbour by-election win
content:
It wasn’t even close. Pauline Hanson’s One Nation won the August 29 Secret Harbour by-election in Western Australia with 38.9% of the primary vote, up from 8.43% in the March 2025 state election.

With preferences, it secured 57% of the two-party preferred vote. Labor's primary vote slumped to 24.3%, down from 46.5%. The Liberals came in third with 17%.

The Greens ran a strong campaign, targeting the cost of living and AUKUS, but their vote dipped slightly from 8.82% to 7.64%.

The hope of some Labor party strategists after the South Australian state election that the nationwide surge in support for One Nation would mostly eat away Liberal or National Party votes was smashed.

Labor's candidate was Georgia Tree, a former lobbyist for oil and gas giant Woodside who no longer lived in the electorate. This did not help her credibility but the size of the swing indicates that this was a secondary factor.

There was as much dirt swirling around the One Nation candidate, whose party is even more explicit in its support for the fossil fuel industry.

There has been a four-decade decline in the primary vote for both Labor and Coalition. The thumping wins by WA Labor between 2017 and 2025 temporarily disguised this reality.

While Labor’s parliamentary majorities are real, they were and did not represent a new generation of “rusted on” loyal voters. That no longer exists like it did in the past.

Instability is the new normal in Australian politics.

In this turmoil One Nation’s bubble could also pop. However, neither the volatility nor the surge in toxic racist, sexist and anti-LGBTIQ scapegoating will go away by themselves.

This ugly reality grows out of three interrelated phenomena. They need to be understood separately and in combination because they all contribute to explaining why so many have turned to One Nation, but they each vary in importance depending on the individual.

The first is four decades of neoliberalism implemented by Liberal and Labor. This means policies that favour the rich at the expense of working people such as privatisation, deregulation, contracting out, corporate tax cuts and subsidies to landlords.

Together these policies have led to the wages share of national income falling to record lows — even though Australian workers are more productive than ever — a loss in job security and now the ferocious damage done by the housing affordability crisis.

The statistics bear out the feeling that many Australians have that the system, the economy and politics, no longer works for them.

Second is the fact that implementing neo-liberalism depended on reducing the militancy and organisation of Australian workers.

In the US and Britain this was achieved by conservative governments unleashing full-frontal attacks on the unions in an attempt to smash them.

In Australia it was done by Labor but more drawn out, slowly strangling the traditions of self-organisation and industrial action by taming unions through the infamous Prices and Incomes Accord.

In the 1970s the majority of the Australian workforce had some experience of going on strike, of taking collective action with their workmates to make their own lives and the lives of others better.

Unless they’ve been lucky enough to connect with a vibrant community or social movement campaign, or been part of the recent upsurge in activism against the genocide in Gaza, most Australian workers have never been part of such collective action.

The vacuum is quickly filled by despair, individualism, scapegoating and “culture wars”; all of which erode social solidarity.

Third is the unrelenting campaign by the pro-capitalist parties and media over the last decades to deflect people’s anger and anxiety at refugees, Muslims and migrants in general.

The Labor Party has gone along with this, and most of the union movement acquiesced, doing terrible damage to working-class consciousness.

Labor is powerless to kill the monster it helped create, and does not have the will to do so. It’s determination to squash the Palestine solidarity movement is proof of that.

Of course racism in Australia didn’t begin with the assault on refugee rights or the ramblings of Pauline Hanson.

It has its origins in a colonial settler state based on the violent dispossession of Indigenous people and serving as a fortress for the British Empire, and now the US, in the Asia Pacific.

The world economy divides humanity into rich and poor. This system is both violent and requires …

author: Alexis Vassiley
title: Labor’s Secret Harbour by-election loss is ominous
content:
Less than eighteen months ago, Western Australian Corrective Services Minister Paul Papalia comfortably held the seat of Secret Harbour, in Perth’s southern suburbs, with a two-party preferred vote of 61.5 percent in the state election. The by-election on Saturday wasn’t even close. One Nation currently leads 57-43 on a two-party preferred basis with 75 percent of the vote counted.

ON candidate Luke Herdegen’s 39 percent primary vote represents a swing of more than 30 percent to the party since last year. Labor’s primary vote plummeted to less than 25 percent, for a negative swing of 22 percent.

Labor’s campaign was utterly tone deaf. Papalia, who retired last month, triggering the by-election, told the

West Australian

days before the election: ‘‘We live in the best state in the best country on planet Earth, and part of the reason for that is good, solid, responsible government”. Anthony Albanese flew to Perth, not to campaign in the election, but for a $10,000-a-head fundraising dinner in a mansion on a street nicknamed “millionaire’s row”.

The party’s candidate selection was no better. Georgia Tree, a government relations advisor to Woodside Energy, was parachuted into what was considered “safe” territory. She previously worked for Federal Resources Minister Madeline King. Tree tried to leverage her working-class roots, saying how important Medicare and TAFE were to her parents. But all she could muster was a pathetic $100 fuel payment for motorists as her answer to the cost-of-living crisis.

Labor threw its all at the campaign, spending more than $400,000 (of which $14,850 came from Woodside). The premier seemingly never left the candidate’s side, while government MPs from all across Perth doorknocked. Labor also spent millions on a pork-barrelling spree and promised to finally start work on a train station they first promised ten years ago. But it was to no avail.

Despite what WA Labour tells itself, voters are not happy. A Demos poll in late August asked respondents if the state government was doing a good or bad job managing particular issues. Its

best

 result was 0 percent for “net good job” (i.e. the same percentage thought it was doing a good and bad job) for education and schools. On the cost-of-living, net good job was negative 56 percent; for housing it was negative 57 percent.

Indeed, the health and education systems are in crisis. The housing situation is thrown into stark relief on Memorial Drive, in the neighbouring Rockingham electorate, where hundreds of homeless people sleep in tents and caravans. Yet funding can be found to build housing for 1,200 defence personnel from the US and UK. In fact, Labor governments are spending billions of dollars on nearby military facilities at HMAS Stirling and the Henderson industrial precinct.

Secret Harbour is one of the least diverse seats in the state. There are fewer immigrants than the state average; those there hail largely from the UK, New Zealand and South Africa. Largely working class, more people have vocational qualifications than university degrees.

Gym owner Herdegen’s pitch centred on infrastructure, the cost of living, crime, immigration and housing. He told voters that Labor had neglected the area for too long, and this was an opportunity to send a message. Herdegen’s campaign did not shy away from far-right talking points. One social media video, for instance, talked about “saving the family suburb”, blaming a “population explosion” for ruining the “suburban Australian dream”, featuring white faces and nostalgic music. The One Nation campaign also spent a huge amount.

The Liberals did badly, coming third with around 17 percent of the primary vote (a negative swing of nearly 8 percent. State Liberal leader Basil Zempilas provoked a stoush with the Liberal federal MP for Canning, Andrew Hastie (whose seat overlaps with Secret Harbour), by claiming that a One Nation win would actually be a Liberal “victory”.

The Greens vote held mostly steady at 7.5 percent. The party campaigned on Labor’s neglect of the area, the cost of living, housing and against the AUKUS security pact.

So this was a good night for the racist far-right bigots of One Nation. The orange wave is real. Prior to Secret Harbour, it remained to be seen if One Nation could actually win seats off Labor. They can, and “safe” ones at that. Labor had held Secret Harbour and its previous incarnations since 1989. Only in 2008 and 2025 did Labor candidate need preferences to …

author: Susan Price
title: Climate emergency: Nepal disaster is ‘showing us the future’
content:
While the whole world is shocked and horrified at the scenes of the catastrophic glacial floods and landslides in Nepal and Tibet, this should be an international wakeup call, said Indra Raj Bhattarai, a social justice and human rights advocate, conservation educator and researcher from Nepal.

Speaking from Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, Bhattarai told Green Left that despite several climate summits the international community has fallen far short of its targets for funding climate change frontline states such as Nepal.

“This is not only an issue of Nepal,” he said. “Nepal adds very little to the global greenhouse gas emissions and 46% of Nepal is forest.

“And it is not just Nepal that is affected. It goes to other countries also, because the river flows all the way to the ocean, past the boundaries of landlocked Nepal.”

Melting glaciers across the whole Hindu Kush Himalaya mountain system directly affect China, India, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Pakistan, Bhattarai explained.

“It affects these countries’ agriculture, the ecosystem and the economy of the whole region.

“Eventually the water from melting glaciers will raise the sea level and affect even more countries.

“We’ve talked about this problem for at least the past two decades in lots of international meetings. Day by day, our extreme weather patterns send us reminders.

“The devastating consequences are seen. The biodiversity is in decline, new diseases are emerging and lots of devastating effects remind us that this is the problem of the whole world.”

Bhattarai said that the international climate talks have focused on the “polluter pays” principle (PPP) which means that those responsible for environmental damage and greenhouse gas emissions should pay the cost of preventing, controlling and remedying impacts.

“What happened to PPP? Nepal actually increased its forested area by 10% in the last decade and a half, but we are facing the challenges arising from increased greenhouse emissions and forest clearing in other parts of the world…

“There’s a fund called the Green Climate Fund [which approved $36.1 million for Nepal in 2025] to reduce the risk of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and United Nations agencies are working on that, but Nepal still has no early warning system.

“That should be the first thing the fund is used for. If we had an early warning system, thousands of lives would have been saved.

“We still don’t know exactly how many people lost their lives but we can say that between 15,000 and 20,000 people have been directly affected.”

The Nepali government is struggling to deal with this catastrophe and the problem is made worse because there is not enough cooperation with China, Bhattarai told GL.

“We need real-time information sharing mechanisms between these two countries to deal with this disaster.

“One week after this flood swept through the Rasuwa and other valleys, there are some remote areas where they have not seen any government representatives or aid.

“While the Nepali and Chinese governments are doing their best to rescue the people buried in the hydroelectric dam tunnels, many other people in remote areas are still not getting emergency assistance, nor have there been efforts to rescue them.

“They urgently need food, medical help and temporary shelters. They need solar lights, communication equipment or mobile connections.”

Those who survived the flood but lost family members also face a very challenging time, Bhattarai said.

“They are moving from one place to another trying to identify their families among the dead bodies, and as a result suffer serious mental health problems, which are not addressed.”

There have been complaints about the emergency response by the new Nepali government, under Prime Minister Balendra Shah. However, Bhattari said that the PM was correct to call an all-party meeting to deal with the crisis.

“While all the party leaders agreed to cooperate, until now there is little cooperation between the federal, provincial and local governments.

“The provincial and local governments are in a better situation to understand the real problems in the field but they are controlled by the parties in opposition at the federal level. The federal ministers have little local connections.”

Bhattarai said the federal government should be distributing more of the international funds to the provincial and local governments.

“Our political leaders should realise that they need to put the people’s interest …

author: Jerome Small
title: Vic premier’s attack on independent unions is an attack on decent unionism
content:
Organisations that offer workers some choice over who represents their industrial interests should be in the same legal category as violent fascist gangs and listed terrorist organisations. This is the intended effect of

amendments

 to laws governing incorporated associations, introduced into the Victorian parliament in mid-August by new Premier Ben Carroll’s Labor government. 

The law threatens to wipe out the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU), which is a challenger to Labor’s largest affiliated union—the notoriously right-wing Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA). Much of the media coverage has presented Carroll’s appalling attack on RAFFWU as a straightforward factional payback, after the SDA-aligned faction within the Labor caucus supported Carroll when he rolled Jacinta Allen as premier of Victoria last month. 

Factional favours may well be a factor, but there’s more to it than that. 

As well as being a gift to the SDA leadership, Carroll’s move is part of a nationwide trend for Labor to crack down on any idea that workers should be entitled to seek representation from a union body not currently licensed by the state through the Fair Work Commission. 

Similar legislation

 to the current Victorian bill was passed in Queensland in 2022 under the Labor government of Annastacia Palaszczuk. And the

Australian Financial Review


reported

 in mid-August that Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth, a former SDA organiser, moved amendments to the national Labor platform at July’s national ALP conference “to bind the party to target ‘sham unions’”. According to the

AFR

: “The amendments say Labor will legislate to limit unregistered unions’ participation in industrial matters, including acting as bargaining representatives”.

Labor figures say that the main target of these moves are the so-called “Red” unions set up in recent years. These “Red” unions are indeed a crime against decent, principled unionism. Their main instigator is Graeme Haycroft, who has a long history in the Liberal National Party in Queensland and was a long-time, prominent member of the notorious 1980s union-busting think tank the

HR Nicholls Society

.

But the best remedy against right-wing unions preying on workers is political exposure, along with established unions demonstrating their superiority through organising strikes and industrial action that improve workers’ lives. This is clearly too much work to contemplate for most of today’s union leaders, and would run totally counter to their politics, which emphasises class collaboration rather than class combat. Much easier to just rely on Labor to wipe out any competitors through legal and bureaucratic methods.

It’s not just RAFFWU and the “Red” unions that are affected by Labor’s attacks. For a decade from 2015, the farm workers’ organising team of the United Workers Union conducted a series of effective—in fact,

outstanding

—organising drives among migrant workers on farms. These workers sometimes made use of the provisions in the Fair Work Act that allow workers to nominate independent bargaining agents to represent them at enterprise agreement negotiations. 

This enabled workers to get around the dictates of the Fair Work Commission, which enforces a legal monopoly on union coverage for most industries in Australia. In the case of farms, this state-sanctioned monopoly belonged to the Australian Workers Union, which had done zero organising on farms for decades and was utterly opposed to any other union doing this organising either. 

Removing the ability of workers to appoint an independent bargaining agent in these circumstances, which seems to be the intention of Rishworth’s proposed changes to national industrial laws, would pose a significant problem for workers in situations like this. Migrant farm workers would be able to secure decent representation only by overthrowing the entire national leadership of the AWU, one of the oldest and strongest bureaucratic machines within Australia’s union movement. 

There’s also the case of the

Independent Transport Union

, a breakaway from the Rail, Tram and Bus Union in Victoria. Unlike RAFFWU, the ITU didn’t start as a project of the left, but rather as a sectional breakaway representing train drivers. But regardless of its origins, the ITU has become an effective industrial force within V/Line, Victoria’s regional rail network. The ITU’s existence as an incorporated association is clearly …

title: Activists protest Murray Watt on Beetaloo gas
content:
Yesterday, fracked gas from the Beetaloo Basin was pumped into the NT electricity grid for the first time. The NT is also planning a big expansion of data centres which will be run in part on Beetaloo gas.

Around the country today, people took action to oppose the opening of Beetaloo and to highlight the disaster that ongoing fossil fuel extraction will be. This action was in Magan-djin/Brisbane outside federal environment minister Murray Watt's office.

Activists intended to present Watt with fracking fluid to show how dangerous it is, but he declined to meet with protesters.

title: Türkoğlu: The process is about restoring the value of labour
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Women’s Assembly Spokesperson Halide Türkoğlu and Deputy Co-Chair Yüksel Mutlu attended the 3rd Women’s Congress of the Confederation of Public Employees Trade Unions (KESK) in Ankara.


Türkoğlu said KESK’s struggle continued to “serve as a beacon” for them and added: “Every right we have won is the result of great struggles waged in the streets, workplaces, trade unions, public squares and every sphere of life. I therefore want to begin by commemorating with respect, longing and gratitude all our women comrades who lost their lives in the struggle for women’s freedom and equality.”


Türkoğlu said it had never been easy for women to expand the grounds of their struggle and continued: “The struggle for labour is women’s struggle for equality. The struggle for labour is a struggle for democracy. This is precisely where the significance of the congress we are holding today lies, as those carrying forward this just and honourable struggle. Every discussion that takes place and every decision that is made during this three-day congress will be decisive both for us and for our politics. We believe that the strong decisions emerging from here will strengthen not only KESK, but the struggle of all women and workers.”


Türkoğlu said the Peace and Democratic Society Process was also about “restoring the value of labour” and added: “We know that the Peace and Democratic Society Process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 February call, is not merely a political process. It is also about democratising social life, restoring the value of labour and achieving women’s freedom. We do not separate the women’s freedom struggle from the struggle for a democratic society. This is because we women have paid the heaviest price for war, poverty and insecurity. For this reason, we do not separate the struggle for peace from the struggle for labour.”


Türkoğlu said women would take the lead in building a democratic life and stressed: “We women no longer want merely to be those who pay the price; we want to be the founding subjects of peace, equality and democratic society. We firmly believe that together we will build a life in which women are equally represented in decision-making mechanisms, where there is no violence, exploitation or insecurity, and where peace and freedom prevail.”


Türkoğlu concluded by saying that organising labour was a responsibility shared by all: “It is the responsibility of all of us to organise the Peace and Democratic Society Process, take part in building this process and develop a form of labour organisation that reflects the spirit of the new era. With our belief that we will assume this responsibility together and build the Peace and Democratic Society Process, I once again salute your congress and wish you every success.”

title: Girne'deki gemi faciası sonrası Kıbrıslı sendikalardan Birleşik Metal-İş'e ziyaret
content:
Kıbrıs Türk Amme Memurları Sendikası (KTAMS) ve Kıbrıs İşçi ve Emekçi Sendikaları Federasyonu (KİEF) yöneticileri, Türkiye Devrimci İşçi Sendikaları Konfederasyonu’na (DİSK) bağlı Birleşik Metal İşçileri Sendikası’nı ziyaret etti. Bostancı’daki Birleşik Metal-İş Genel Merkezi’nde gerçekleştirilen görüşmede ekonomik kriz, hayat pahalılığı, sendikal mücadele, Türkiye-Kuzey Kıbrıs ilişkileri ve Girne açıklarında yaşanan gemi faciası ele alındı.

Ziyarette KTAMS ve KİEF Genel Başkanı Güvenç Bengihan ile KTAMS Genel Sekreteri Selman Yiğit yer aldı. Bengihan ve Yiğit, Birleşik Metal-İş Genel Başkanı ve DİSK Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Özkan Atar ile bir araya geldi. Görüşmede, iki ülkedeki emekçilerin ortak sorunları ve sendikal dayanışmanın geliştirilmesine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulunuldu.

Atar, Kıbrıslı işçiler ve emekçilerle geçmişten bugüne dayanışma içerisinde olduklarını belirterek, bu ilişkinin ortak mücadele temelinde sürdürüleceğini söyledi. Kıbrıs’taki sendikalarla Türkiye’de eğitim ve konferanslar gerçekleştirdiklerini aktaran Atar, işçi sınıfının uluslararası dayanışmasına dikkat çekti. “Kıbrıslı işçilerle, emekçilerle ve onların sendikal örgütleriyle de bugüne kadar olduğu gibi bugünden sonra da dayanışmamızı ve ortak mücadelemizi devam ettireceğiz” dedi.

Bengihan da Birleşik Metal-İş ile uzun yıllara dayanan dayanışma ilişkisine dikkat çekerek, sendikacılık açısından sendikayı bir okul olarak gördüklerini söyledi. Geçmiş yıllarda Kemal Türkler Tesisleri’nde gerçekleştirilen eğitim çalışmalarına değinen Bengihan, bu çalışmaların kendilerinin sendikal mücadele anlayışının gelişmesinde önemli rol oynadığını belirtti. Birleşik Metal-İş’in emek eksenli örgütlenme konusunda kendilerine yol gösterdiğini ifade eden Bengihan, sendikanın çözüm için önce masayı işaret ettiğini, ancak masada sonuç alınamadığında işçilerle birlikte sokakta mücadele ettiğini söyledi.

Türkiye’de ekonomik krizin emekçilerin alım gücünü her geçen gün düşürdüğünü belirten Atar, AKP iktidarının Orta Vadeli Program kapsamında uyguladığı ekonomi politikalarının işçiler başta olmak üzere emeklileri, kamu çalışanlarını, küçük esnafı ve köylüleri etkilediğini söyledi.

Asgari ücretin açlık sınırının altında kaldığını belirten Atar, “Bugün asgari ücret açlık sınırının sekiz bin liradan fazla altına düşmüş vaziyette. Türkiye’de yakın tarihimize bakacak olursak, hiç olmadığı kadar şiddetli bir yoksullaşma süreci yaşıyoruz” dedi.

Ekonomik krizin bedelinin emekçilere yüklenmesine karşı mücadele edilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Atar, asgari ücret başta olmak üzere tüm ücretlerin güncellenmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Atar, “Bütün ücretlerin hiç zaman kaybetmeksizin tekrar güncellenmesi, yükseltilmesi ve insanca yaşamaya yetecek hale gelmesi için öncelikle mücadele verilmesi gerekiyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

Bengihan ise Türkiye’deki hayat pahalılığının Kuzey Kıbrıs’a doğrudan yansıdığını belirterek, Türk lirasının değer kaybının adadaki emekçilerin alım gücünü gerilettiğini söyledi. “Türkiye’deki yaşanan hayat pahalılığı doğal olarak Kuzey Kıbrıs’a da yansıyor. Bize de ithal olarak enflasyon geliyor” diyen Bengihan, Türkiye’deki işçilerin yaşadığı sorunların benzerinin Kıbrıs’ta da yaşandığını ifade etti.

Kuzey Kıbrıs’ta asgari ücretin Temmuz ayında brüt 70 bin 886 liraya, net olarak yaklaşık 63 bin liraya yükseldiğini belirten Bengihan, ücretlerin rakamsal olarak artmasının yaşam koşullarının iyileştiği anlamına gelmediğini söyledi. “Rakamsal olarak büyüyor ama bizlerin alım gücü geriliyor. Alabileceğimiz hizmetlerin ve ürünlerin miktarı geriliyor” dedi.

KTAMS ve KİEF’in hesaplamalarına göre dört kişilik aile için açlık sınırının 45 bin 389 lira, yoksulluk sınırının ise 244 bin 818 lira olduğunu belirten Bengihan, asıl ölçütün ücretin rakamsal büyüklüğü değil, emekçilerin bu ücretle ne kadar temel ihtiyaç karşılayabildiği olduğunu söyledi. Kıbrıs İstatistik Kurumu’nun 13 aydır enflasyon hesaplama sepetinde değişiklik yapmadığını da aktaran Bengihan, mevcut verilerin hayat pahalılığını ne ölçüde yansıttığına sorguladı.

Kuzey Kıbrıs’taki hayat pahalılığında yalnızca Türkiye’deki enflasyonun değil, piyasadaki denetimsizliğin de etkili olduğunu belirten Bengihan, yüksek kâr oranlarına tepki gösterdi. “Bitmek bilmeyen açgözlü kâr hırsı var, denetim de yok, azami kâr marjı da yok. Denetim olmadığı için çok pahalı bir ülke durumuna geldik” dedi.

Bengihan, eğitim, sağlık ve barınma giderlerinin de emekçilerin bütçesi üzerindeki yükü artırdığını belirterek …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Top of the World": Remembering the Restaurant Workers Killed Atop World Trade Center in 9/11 Attack
content:
A new documentary titled

Top of the World

 tells the story of Windows on the World, the legendary restaurant atop the World Trade Center, through the eyes of its former employees. Windows on the World served guests for 25 years, until the morning of September 11, 2001, when it was destroyed in the attacks on the World Trade Center. Seventy-nine workers and 91 diners were killed.


We’re joined by

Top of the World

's co-directors, Julie Cohen and Betsy West, and by Sekou Siby, a former line cook at Windows on the World. Siby, who immigrated to the United States from the Ivory Coast in 1996, was originally scheduled to work on the morning of September 11, but a co-worker asked him to switch shifts. “He didn't make it,” says Siby, who later became an organizer and longtime leader at the Restaurant Opportunities Center (

ROC

), an advocacy group founded by Windows on the World workers to support each other in the aftermath of the attack.


“The extraordinary immigrant workforce of Windows [of the World] and what they collectively created is just a reminder of the contributions of immigrant New Yorkers to the restaurant world and to the culture of the city,” says Cohen. “We want people to remember not just the tragedy, but the real beauty and the specific stories of what was lost on that day.”


Top of the World

 premieres on

CNN

 Monday, September 7, 2026.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Meta Tests Robots That Could Replace Human Workers at Data Centres
content:
Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables and reset servers at data centres, sparking concerns among workers that they will soon be replaced. 


Whistleblowers told Wired

 the social media giant is working with several firms on robotics technology as its investment in AI infrastructure soars. 


In the face of

widespread opposition

 to

new data centres

, which drive up household bills, pollute groundwater and raise local temperatures,

some advocates

 have argued that they are worthwhile because they create local jobs.  


Tugger robots, which can move heavy racks around data centres, are already in use at Meta data centres in US states including Iowa and Virginia, according to those familiar with the projects. Inventory robots are also being used to inspect failures, although they reportedly struggle to get around corners. 


In Altoona, Iowa, morale among workers is low. One person familiar with staff group chats said the general sentiment was that they were “all going to be gone in a few years anyway because of the robots”. 


Meta engineers are assessing whether a robotic arm from Kinova Robotics can be trusted to turn electronic devices on and off. Another robot being tested to swap networking cables could fulfil up to 80% of some staffers’ workloads, according to one Meta data centre employee. 


“We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” the worker said. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.”


By 2023, Meta was already operating robots programmed to track inventory and independently plan their own routes,

engineers told

 the Open Compute Project. 


In a video published at the time, one senior staffer said that Meta’s robotic innovations would be shared “with the industry”. 


Meta spokesperson Francis Brennan said the company is training and hiring workers to operate its data centres. “We need more workers, not fewer,” he said.


But not all workers are convinced.


“

They no longer want people who can think independently, come up with creative solutions, or perform complex troubleshooting,” said one. “They want ‘smart hands,’ people who are just capable enough to follow AI instructions and not mess anything up.”

title: JUNG. DIGITAL. ORGANISIERT. Aufstieg und Fall der Jungnazi-Gruppe ‚Deutsche Jugend Voran‘
content:
Die erstarkende rechte Jugendbewegung, die sich überall bemerkbar macht, auf Social Media, im Kiez, bei CSDs, wirft viele Fragen auf: Wer sind diese jungen Neonazis? Wie sind sie organisiert? Was sind ihre ideologischen Ankerpunkte? Und vor allem: Was tun wir dagegen?


Diese Broschüre ist das Ergebnis antifaschistischer Recherche der letzten beiden Jahre. Der Fokus liegt auf Berliner Jungneonazigruppen und insbesondere der „Deutschen Jugend Voran“ (DJV). Auch wenn diese Struktur mittlerweile weniger präsent ist, war sie die erste Berliner Gruppe der rechten Jugendbewegung, die sich 2024 bundesweit formierte. An der DJV lässt sich das Phänomen beispielhaft erklären. Denn obwohl sich die Gruppenzusammensetzungen und Labels sich ständig verändern, bleibt das Kernproblem bestehen.


Unser Ziel ist es, Rechercheerkenntnisse und Strategiedebatten zu verschriftlichen, um sie möglichst vielen Antifas zugänglich zu machen und so Inspiration für antifaschistische Interventionen zu liefern.


Zu Beginn steht eine Chronik, die Aktivitäten von extrem rechten Jugendgruppen aus Berlin vom Juli 2024 bis Mai 2026 dokumentiert.


Daran schließt sich die Analyse der Struktur an, in der sich die Jungneonazis organisieren.


Das nächste Kapitel widmet sich der dahinterstehenden Ideologie und der Frage, warum die rechte Jugendbewegung gerade jetzt so präsent ist.


Darauf folgt ein kritischer Blick auf die staatliche Reaktion und den Gerichtsprozess gegen den DJV-Anführer Julian Milz.


Abschließend ziehen wir Bilanz, welche antifaschistischen Strategien in den letzten Jahren genutzt wurden und welche Handlungsmöglichkeiten sich uns bieten, um den Rechten entgegenzutreten.


Besprecht die Broschüre in euren Gruppen, bildet Banden und macht Pläne!

Il est plus que nécessaire aujourd'hui, à moins d'un an du cirque électoral habituel, de mettre en place des formes d'organisation collectives et autonomes : groupes d'autodéfense, comités de quartiers, assemblées locales mais aussi l'acquisition, par quelque moyen qui soi, de lieux et de moyens matériels. Face à ces formes d'organisation, la répression policière et judiciaire a rarement frappé aussi fort. Soyons solidaires de celleux qui s'y retrouvent confronté-es car iels n'ont pas leur place dans la logique capitaliste : sans-papier, fraudeur-se, voleur-se à l'étalage, cambrioleur-se et/ou tabasseur-se de faf etc. (quelques exemples)


Devant l'ampleur de la tâche à réaliser, quelques tags dans un quartier peuvent sembler dérisoire. Mais, nous y voyons 2 utilités. Premièrement, la présence à répétition sur plusieurs lieux de passages fréquentés peut interpeller les passant-es et pousser quelques personnes à s'informer sur ce sujet et ces affaires autrement que par les médias dominants. Deuxièmement, ce type d'opération peut être une première étape, un entraînement, une manière de gagner en confiance et en compétences en vue de réaliser d'autres actions plus ambitieuses : sabotage, attaques diverses etc.


En tout cas, nous pensons que c'est à la portée de beaucoup de personnes (attention aux caméras et aux voitures banalisées de flic la nuit) et nous préférerons toujours montrer notre solidarité ainsi plutôt qu'en repostant une story instagram avant de retourner à un train-train quotidien confortable.


Espérons que cette action puisse participer à soutenir Gino, Zaïd, Maja, Lina, les lyonnais-es et les autres. Des camarades.

title: Neuer Angriff auf die VVN-BdA und die Gemeinnützigkeit
content:
Neuer Angriff auf die VVN-BdA und die Gemeinnützigkeit


Die Bundesorganisation der Vereinigung der Verfolgten des Naziregimes – Bund der Antifaschistinnen und Antifaschisten (

VVN

-BdA) sieht sich einem Angriff auf ihre Gemeinnützigkeit gegenüber: Das Finanzamt Berlin hat eine außerordentliche Prüfung eingeleitet, weil es die antifaschistische Arbeit der Organisation als „unzulässige politische Betätigung“ einstuft. Ganz konkret verweist die Behörde auf die Bündniskampagnen gegen die AfD, an denen sich die Vereinigung beteiligt. Die

VVN

-BdA war nach der Befreiung vom

NS

-Faschismus von Überlebenden des

NS

-Terrors gegründet worden und engagiert sich bis heute gegen rechte Hetze und Krieg.

Bereits am 17. Juli 2026 schickte das Finanzamt für Körperschaften I Berlin der Bundesorganisation der

VVN

-BdA die Aufforderung, bis November vorzeitige Steuererklärungen der vergangenen drei Jahre einzureichen, da Zweifel an der Gemeinnützigkeit bestünden. Explizit benennt das Schreiben die von einem breiten Bündnis getragene Kampagne „Menschenwürde verteidigen – AfD-Verbot jetzt“. Die

VVN

-BdA fungiert als rechtlicher Träger des Gemeinschaftsprojekts und stellt auch das Spendenkonto zur Verfügung. Dass staatliches und gerichtliches Vorgehen gegen die faschistischen Umtriebe eingefordert wird, widerspricht dem Verständnis des Finanzamts von Gemeinnützigkeit. 

Ebenfalls ein Dorn im Auge der Behörden und der Rechtsaußen-Partei ist die Kampagne „Widersetzen“, die sich gegen Parteitage und andere Großveranstaltungen der AfD richtet. Durch massenhaften zivilen Ungehorsam und Blockaden konnten die rechten Versammlungen jeweils nur mit starker Verspätung und unter extremen Beeinträchtigungen stattfinden. Bereits kurz vor der vergangenen Großaktion von Widersetzen am 4. Juli 2026 in Erfurt hatten AfD-nahe Akteure gefordert, der

VVN

-BdA die Gemeinnützigkeit abzuerkennen, was in den Folgetagen von verschiedenen Medien aufgegriffen wurde und sich zu einer wahren Hetzkampagne entwickelte.

Mit dem Schreiben vom 17. Juli 2026 setzte das Finanzamt diese Forderung bereitwillig um und bedroht damit die älteste antifaschistische Organisation in ihrer finanziellen Handlungsfähigkeit. Das passiert nicht zum ersten Mal: Bereits 2019 hatte die Berliner Behörde der

VVN

-BdA die Gemeinnützigkeit aberkannt, musste dann aber wegen des breiten politischen Drucks und sogar internationaler Proteste einlenken. Nach der damaligen Schlappe hofft das Finanzamt wohl, sich beim aktuellen Vorstoß durchsetzen zu können.

„Es ist empörend, dass die staatlichen Behörden versuchen, über den Angriff auf die Gemeinnützigkeit antifaschistische Arbeit und zivilgesellschaftliches Engagement gegen rechte Hetze zu unterbinden oder zumindest kleinzuhalten. Ganz offensichtlich soll an der

VVN

-BdA ein abschreckendes Exempel statuiert werden, um auch andere oppositionelle Vereine und Organisationen mundtot zu machen“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. V. „Umso notwendiger ist es, gegen diesen Repressionsschlag mit breiter Solidarität und Massenprotesten vorzugehen. Wir stehen an der Seite der

VVN

-BdA. Antifaschismus muss gemeinnützig bleiben – Wir sind alle Antifa!“

 


bert

Pressemitteilung


Die

VVN

-BdA steht erneut im Visier des Berliner Finanzamts. Weil sie sich an Bündnissen und Protesten gegen die AfD beteiligt, droht der antifaschistischen Organisation der Verlust ihrer Gemeinnützigkeit.

title: World’s Largest Far Right Paramilitary Rallied in NYC. It Should Alarm Everyone.
content:
Five thousand people attended a rally in New York City led by the right-wing Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On February 20, 1939, the Madison Square Garden arena in New York City hosted a chilling spectacle. A portrait of George Washington hung at the center of the arena, flanked by U.S. flags and swastikas. Over 20,000 people packed the stands to hear Fritz Kuhn, leader of the German American Bund — one of the most prominent U.S.-based organizations aligned with the Third Reich — project his vision of a “white, Gentile-ruled United States.” Outside, 100,000 anti-Nazi protesters clashed with police on Eighth Avenue, determined to stop the legitimization of European fascism on U.S. soil.

Eighty-seven years later, global leaders in ethno-fascism and their sympathizers returned to Madison Square Garden.

On August 29, 2026, 5,000 people gathered at Madison Square Garden to hear Mohan Bhagwat, the sarsanghchalak (Supreme Leader) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). As the ideological parent of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the RSS is the world’s largest far right paramilitary organization, with an estimated 4 million members spread over 73,117 branches across India. Just as the Bund attempted to leverage the image of George Washington to legitimize Nazism in their rally of 1939, the RSS used this invite-only event — apparently attended by 180 religious leaders from 30 countries — to sanitize a century-old project of Hindu fascism. Obscuring its extremist agenda, the RSS cloaked the gathering in the rhetoric of liberal multiculturalism, branding it with the theme “Universal Oneness.”

In his 42-minute keynote, the septuagenarian Bhagwat played the part of a playful but discerning uncle, dispensing meandering aphorisms about an “innate, eternal oneness” that connects humanity and nature. Rooting these concepts in the Atman (soul) and India’s civilizational values, Bhagwat painted a picture of a nation that champions “unity in diversity.” In a jarring contrast to his movement’s actual record, he claimed that India chooses to tolerate its enemies rather than subjugate them — elevating the country as a global exemplar of enlightened governance.

While Bhagwat spoke inside, an interfaith and anti-caste coalition protested outside. It consisted of groups like SALAM (South Asian Left), Hindus for Human Rights, and the Indian American Muslim Council, along with members of some of the 66 organizations that signed on to a statement earlier this week condemning Bhagwat’s visit. Their speeches exposed the hypocrisy of Bhagwat’s claim to “unity in diversity,” demonstrating how the RSS and its massive network of Hindu supremacist partners — including nearly a thousand nonprofit organizations, cultural organizations, paramilitary groups, unions, and political parties, collectively known as the Sangh Parivar (or the Family of the Sangh) — routinely practice the exact opposite of what Bhagwat preaches.

Speakers pointed out how the RSS’s notion of unity is, in fact, exclusively reserved for Hindus — and only for those who are wealthy and upper-caste. Shree Baphna from SALAM talked about how Hindutva (or the Hindu supremacist movement) attempts to divert mass anger “away from those in power and towards those communities who are exploited and oppressed.”

When an Adivasi [Indigenous person] defends jal, jungle, zameen [water, forests and land] against mines, dams and corporations – Hindutva says, ‘forget your history – you are a vanvasi – a child of the Hindu nation.’ Shame!

Ritu Gupta from the nonprofit Hindus for Human Rights, noted that Mohan Bhagwat is here “pretending to spread the message of oneness.” But this is not the message Bhagwat’s supporters spread in India, Gupta retorted. “In India they say, ‘Hindus only – everybody else, get out!’ These Hindus who support the message of purging India of its minorities do not represent all Hindus. There could be no bigger hypocrisy than this!”

title: Памяти "Сократа"
content:
Сегодня мы вспоминаем нашего товарища Алексея "Сократа" Сутугу, он умер ровно 6 лет назад. Сократ был настоящим антифашистом, идейным бойцом. Его яркая харизма, желание всем помочь, всех защитить сделали его очень заметной фигурой в анархистском и антифашистском движении. За это его ненавидели власти и немало времени ему пришлось провести в неволе. Но даже этот опыт он сделал оружием в борьбе с властями. Канал "Antifascist Post Every Day" напоминает слова Сократа из его книги "Диалоги о тюрьме":

"Есть отработанная тема: если ты слышишь, что пытают зека и ты точно знаешь, что это не провокация мусорская, ты должен заступиться за этого зека, потому что, если мы будем друг за друга заступаться, будет нормально все у зеков, мусора не будут так жестить, а если мы будем попустительством заниматься, начнут всех пиздить, вымогать деньги. Это общее людское понятие, ты должен заступиться вплоть до того, чтобы вскрыться, вскрыть вены, чтобы остановить насилие. Если ты этого не сделаешь, и об этом узнает братва, другие зеки, тебе скажут, ты что охуел так поступать, ты поступил как непорядочный, каждый порядочный должен заступиться за другого зека"

При всей своей известности в антифашистских кругах, у Алексея не было звёздной болезни. Он всегда оставался надёжным товарищем. Жизнь "Сократа" была такой яркой, что продолжает светить и новому поколению антифашистов.

title: Der Server namens Paranoia: Verteidigt Autistici/Inventati vor dem 25.9.
content:
Seit fünfundzwanzig Jahren baut ein italienisches Hackerkollektiv eine Kommunikationsinfrastruktur auf, die Zensur, Überwachung und Polizeirazzien überstehen soll. Am 26. August stuften es die Vereinigten Staaten als terroristische Organisation ein. Am 25. September endet die Frist der Abwicklung.


Dieser Text ist eine Übersetzung von

«The Server Called Paranoia: Defend Autistici/Inventati Before September 25»

, vom 27. August 2026, von Sabot Media. Mit kurzem Kommentar und weiterführenden Ressourcen.


Es hätte eine dunkle und stürmische Nacht in einem italienischen Hacklab sein sollen.


Es war, ärgerlicherweise, ein schöner sonniger Sonntag.


Am 3. März 2001 versammelten sich rund zehn Personen im LOA Hacklab in Mailand um einen Computer, der aus ausrangierten Teilen zusammengebaut war. Eine Bank hatte ihnen einen alten Server zum symbolischen Preis von 15.000 Lire, etwa acht Dollar, verkauft. Sie bauten ihn mit ausgeschlachteten Komponenten, auch mit einer Festplatte von einem Heimcomputer, weiter aus. Niemand kam mit einem fertigen Bauplan. Softwarepakete wurden einzeln in Betracht gezogen. Jede Entscheidung wurde besprochen, bis alle einverstanden waren. Sie setzten bewusst die technisch am wenigsten erfahrene Person an die Tastatur. Der Prozess dauerte viel länger als nötig, weil Effizienz nicht das einzige Ziel war. Alle sollten verstehen, was sie bauten. An diesem Tag, erinnerte sich eine teilnehmende Person später, stellten sie fest: «A/I existiert jetzt.»


Sie nannten den Computer

Paranoia

. Im darauffolgenden Monat ging er online. Mit zwei Domains und zwei miteinander verflochtenen Geschichten: Autistici.org und Inventati.org. Fünfundzwanzig Jahre später, am 26. August 2026, stuften die Vereinigten Staaten Autistici/Inventati als Specially Designated Global Terrorist (ausgewiesene globale Terroreinheit) ein und setzten sie auf die Liste der Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (mit dieser SDN-Liste setzt die USA Sanktionen durch. Sie landet global in automatischen Screening-Listen und blockiert und erschwert Geschäfte).


Die Strecke zwischen diesen beiden Ereignissen – von einem recycelten Computer in einem Mailänder Hacklab zu den Mühlen des amerikanischen Sicherheitsstaates – ist die Geschichte eines Kollektivs, das ein Vierteljahrhundert damit verbrachte, auf einem gefährlichen Unterfangen zu beharren:


Personen sollten kommunizieren können, ohne sich zuvor Konzernen oder Regierungen zu unterwerfen.


Die unmittelbare Bedrohung hat jetzt ein Datum. Am 25. September läuft die Frist des US-Befehls aus. Institutionen müssen ihre Beziehungen zu A/I bis dann herunterfahren. Banken, Technologieunternehmen, Hosting-Anbieter und andere Institutionen werden angewiesen, verbleibende Beziehungen zu kappen. A/I baute seine Infrastruktur so, damit sie das Verschwinden eines Servers überlebt. Die Vereinigten Staaten versuchen nun, das Kollektiv wirtschaftlich und technologisch unberührbar zu machen.


Bleib dabei: Wir vertiefen, was A/I ist, zeichnen die Geschichte des autonomen Tech-Kollektivs nach und erkunden, was dieser neueste Angriff für Kollektiv und die breitere radikale Bewegung bedeuten könnte.


Vor A/I: Italiens Internet im Untergrund


Autistici/Inventati erschienen nicht aus dem Nichts. Seine Wurzeln liegen in mehr als einem Jahrzehnt italienischem autonomem Organizing, Piratenradio, Bulletin-Board-Systemen, besetzten sozialen Zentren, antikapitalistischen Bewegungen und Experimenten mit Computern als politischem Werkzeug. In den 1990er Jahren boten Netzwerke wie das European Counter Network und Isole nella Rete sozialen Bewegungen Online-Räume, als das Internet einem Grossteil der Öffentlichkeit noch unbekannt war. Italiens Hackmeetings brachten Programmierer*innen, Aktivist*innen, Künstler*innen und technologisch Neugierige in selbstverwalteten Räumen zusammen. Hacklabs ploppten in besetzten Sozialzentren auf, wo die Menschen Linux lernen, Netzwerke aufbauen und technisches Wissen als etwas anpacken konnten, das geteilt und nicht verkauft werden sollte. Die künftigen Mitglieder von A/I kamen aus verschiedenen Teilen dieser Welt. In Mailand verwendeten die mit dem LOA Hacklab verbundenen Personen den Namen

Autistici

, um ihre intensive Faszination für Technologie und ihren Wunsch, die darin verborgene Politik aufzudecken, zu beschreiben. In Florenz war das

Inventati

-Projekt mehr auf Kommunikation, Veröffentlichung und Bewegungsorganizing ausgerichtet. Zu den Projekten …

title: „Nazi Incels“: Kollegahs Alpha Gym nach Vandalismus beschädigt
content:
Kollegah

s Fitnessstudio „Alpha Gym“ hat anscheinend Besuch von Menschen bekommen, die dem Rapper und seinem Geschäftspartner Heidrich Kopelke eher weniger positiv gesonnen sind. So wurde die Fensterfront des Solinger Studios mit einem „

Nazi Incels

„-Graffiti bemalt. Der Polizei zufolge soll das Fitnessstudio zudem im Inneren beschädigt worden sein. Das

Solinger Tageblatt

 ist derweil an ein angebliches Bekennerschreiben gekommen.


„Alpha Gym“: Kollegahs Fitnessstudio wurde mit Graffiti bemalt


Im Rahmen der Tat soll das „Alpha Gym“ auch im Inneren einiges abbekommen haben. Das hat die Polizei dem Solinger Tageblatt gegenüber bestätigt. Im oben genannten Bekennerschreiben findet man dazu weitere Infos. So seien die Beschädigungen in den Innenräumen durch das Verteilen von Buttersäure verursacht worden.


In ihrem Schreiben machen die Verfasser übrigens auch Angaben zur Motivation hinter der Tat. Dort werden Kollegah und seinem Geschäftspartner nämlich Nähe zu „

ultrarechten Kreisen

“ vorgeworfen. Der Ton des Schreibens soll laut dem Solinger Tageblatt recht hämisch sein. So schreiben die Verfasser unter anderem Folgendes:


„Nicht nur die Fassade ist ziemlich schäbig, einige der Fenster (sind) beklebt und andere wiederum nicht. Außerdem merkten wir bei unserer Ankunft direkt einen unangenehmen Geruch. War das der Geruch einer fehlgeschlagenen Bosstransformation?“


Beendet wird das Schreiben, dessen Echtheit sich zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt nicht bestätigen lässt, mit der Nachricht: „

Antifa heißt Kampf.

“


Die Besitzer des Gyms haben laut Polizei übrigens eine Strafanzeige wegen Sachbeschädigung gestellt. Zudem haben die Behörden wohl das Schreiben an den Staatsschutz weitergeleitet.


Kollegah & Heidrich Kopelke: Kontakte ins rechtsextreme Milieu?


Unabhängig von der Echtheit des Schreibens machen schon die Graffiti auf der Fensterfront des Gyms recht deutlich, worum es bei der ganzen Sache geht.


Aller Wahrscheinlichkeit nach beziehen sich die Urheber der Sachbeschädigung dabei unter anderem auf die Kontakte von Heidrich Kopelke. Der Geschäftsmann soll laut einer Recherche der Süddeutschen Zeitung enge Verflechtungen zur rechtsextremen Szene und der Bekleidungsmarke Thor Steinar haben. Letztere gilt laut dem Verfassungsschutz Brandenburg als ein mögliches Erkennungsmerkmal für Personen der rechtsextremen Szene.

title: From Afghanistan to Kurdistan: Women resist together
content:
An event titled “Five Years of Resistance: Our Voices Remain Loud” was held in Jena, Germany on Friday to mark five years of Taliban rule in Afghanistan. The event focused on the resistance of Afghan women in Herat, Kabul, and Bamyan, their organizing efforts, and the question of how women around the world can fight together against patriarchal violence and oppression. The event was organized by Netzwerk gegen Feminizide (Network Against Femicides) Thüringen, Gemeinsam Kämpfen (Fighting Together), and Wisdom House – Free Education for Afghan Girls.


Participants watched a documentary about women’s resistance in Afghanistan. The film shows how women continue to organize, create spaces for education, and bring their protests into the public sphere despite massive repression by the Taliban. It made one point particularly clear: resistance does not begin only with the direct struggle against the Taliban. It begins earlier—at home, within families, wherever women are subjected to patriarchal violence and oppression.


Women are deprived of their rights, pushed out of public life, and continue to face severe violence. Suicides and femicides are part of a reality that persists. And while women in Afghanistan struggle for their freedom and their lives under these conditions, the German federal government cooperates with the Taliban and organizes deportations to Afghanistan.


Afterward, poems and statements by participants were read aloud, and artistic works by young women from Afghanistan were presented. Their perspectives made clear that resistance takes many forms: through art and education, organizing, public protest, and the everyday decision not to submit to patriarchal domination. The discussion that followed centered above all on one question: How can women around the world organize together to issue a collective challenge to global patriarchy?


The philosophy of “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom] played a central role in this discussion. It stands for the international networking of women’s organizations, self-organization in all areas of society, and the development of an autonomous, self-determined identity. Rather than waiting for existing social structures to grant them freedom, women should organize themselves and create their own spaces, structures, and political perspectives.


At the same time, the responsibility of men was also addressed. Many men shared the view that they often do not have enough courage to stand up against the Taliban, but also against patriarchal structures and violence within their own families. What is needed, therefore, are men who do more than simply express their solidarity—men who actively stand alongside women and challenge patriarchal relations both within themselves and together with other men.


It was also emphasized that the history of patriarchy must be understood collectively: “Patriarchy is not an immutable or natural state of affairs. It is a social order that emerged historically and can therefore also be overcome. The question is what kind of society we want to build in its place—and what role women will have within it. The values embodied by free and self-determined women must be placed at the center.”


Struggles across borders are connected


The importance of international solidarity was also highlighted by the participants, as women’s struggles take place under different conditions across the world, yet they are interconnected. Resistance should not be understood as a series of separate struggles. The revolution in Kurdistan, “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî,” the revolution in Iran and Rojhilat, the resistance of women in Abya Yala and Afghanistan, and the struggle against femicides in Germany and around the world are all part of the same struggle. The aim is to learn from one another and from different experiences and forms of organizing, to build international networks, and to make visible together that patriarchal violence is not an individual issue, but a societal and global problem.


One participant raised an important point: “Even if an event like this does not yet bring together 200 people, that does not mean the resistance is small. Every person present has consciously chosen to fight for freedom. Within that lies a spark of hope from which the next steps can emerge. It is not only about numbers, but about the significance of each individual’s courage to choose resistance anew every day.”

title: Rassismus, Sexismus und ein Klima der Angst bei der Basler Polizei – nun wissenschaftlich belegt
content:
Dossier


„

Was die unabhängige Personalbefragung der Kantonspolizei Basel-Stadt über die Zustände im Korps aussagt, ist katastrophal: eine Kultur der Angst, eine veraltete Macho-Kultur, ein totaler Vertrauensverlust. (…) Markus Schefer, der Professor für Staats- und Verwaltungsrecht an der Uni Basel ist die erste gewählte Telefonnummer von Journalist*innen, wenn es eine Debatte über das Vorgehen der Polizei bei Demos gibt – er war beauftragt worden, die schiefe Personallage der Polizei zu untersuchen. Unterstützt wurde er von Claudia Puglisi, einer Polizeidirektor*in aus Niedersachsen, die bei der Präsentation neben ihm sass – ihr besorgt wirkender Blick spiegelte die Drastik der Ergebnisse wider. Denn an heftig negativen Begrifflichkeiten mangelt es im 42-seitigen Dokument sicherlich nicht.  (…) Die Kritik konzentriert sich auf Polizeikommandant Martin Roth. Er ist medial angeschlagen, seit linke Politiker*innen im Frühjahr 2023 wegen des

Gummischrot-Einsatzes der Frauentags-Demo


 seinen

Rücktritt


 forderten

…“

Artikel von David Rutschmann vom 21. Juni 2024 in bajour


 („Kein Lodern, ein Flammen“) – u.a. wurden Polizistinnen wurden in «fi**bar» oder «unf**kbar» unterteilt… Siehe dazu mehr Infos:


Das Gummischrot war illegal: Das Basler Appellationsgericht rügt die Polizei wegen eines Einsatzes gegen den feministischen Kampftag 2023


„Jahrelang war es so selten wie eine Fasnacht im Sommer, dass Basler Gerichte der Basler Polizei Grenzen setzen. Das ändert sich glücklicherweise gerade (…). Schritt für Schritt weist die Justiz ein entfesseltes Korps in die Schranken. Das neuste Urteil des Appellationsgerichts, das der WOZ exklusiv vorliegt, ist diesbezüglich ein Meilenstein. Darin erklärt das Gericht das Abfeuern von Gummischrot in eine Menschengruppe, von der keine konkrete Gefahr ausgeht, als illegal. Einen Klassiker der Basler Demobekämpfung. (…) Beurteilt hat das Gericht den Polizeieinsatz gegen den feministischen Kampftag am 8. März 2023. Damals versammelten sich rund 250 Personen vor der Universität. Und wurden, als sie sich in Bewegung setzen wollten, eingekesselt. Kurz darauf begannen die Polizist:innen, mit Gummischrot auf die Demonstrant:innen zu feuern. Doch nur die ersten drei Salven, so das Appellationsgericht, waren verhältnismässig. Diese erfolgten, als sich der Demozug in Richtung der Polizeikette bewegte. Die weiteren Salven waren rechtswidrig. (…) [S]elbst wenn der Mindestabstand eingehalten worden wäre, so das Gericht, hätte das den Gummischroteinsatz nicht gerechtfertigt. Dieser sei rechtswidrig gewesen (…)  In den weiteren Punkten des Urteils zeigt sich dann allerdings, dass auch das Basler Appellationsgericht alten Gewohnheiten nachhängt und noch immer gerne die Argumentation der Polizei übernimmt: Bei der Personenkontrolle sollen Polizistinnen mehreren Demonstrant:innen in die Unterhosen gegriffen haben. Die Polizei bestreitet dies – und das Gericht stellt sich auf ihre Seite. Die objektive Beweislast liege bei den Kläger:innen. In der dritten wichtigen Frage des Urteils geht es um die Rechtmässigkeit des Polizeikessels. Mit einer abenteuerlichen Begründung wischt das Appellationsgericht ein Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs für Menschenrechte (EGMR) vom Tisch, das Anfang 2024 verlangte, dass ein solcher Kessel nicht ohne genau festgelegte Rahmenbedingungen möglich sei, etwa was die Dauer betreffe. In Basel ist das bloss rudimentär geregelt. Mehr sei auch nicht nötig, befindet das Gericht geradezu anmassend: «Diese für eine polizeiliche Technik wie die Einkesselung aussergewöhnlich hohen Anforderungen können für die Schweiz nicht verbindlich sein.» Es reiche aus, dass im Polizeigesetz allgemeines polizeiliches Handeln und Personenkontrollen geregelt seien – auch wenn der Kessel nicht explizit vorkommt. Constanze Seelmann, die die Demonstrant:innen rechtlich vertritt, wird in deren Auftrag den Entscheid ans Bundesgericht weiterziehen. «Das Appellationsgericht hat sich nicht richtig mit dem EGMR-Urteil befasst. Die Schweiz braucht aber ein Grundsatzurteil, ob und falls ja, unter welchen Umständen ein Polizeikessel zulässig ist.» (…) Wie leichtfertig in Basel eingekesselt wird, zeigte sich an der Palästina-Solidemo vergangenen Samstag. (…) Die Demonstrant:innen mussten bis zu zehn Stunden im Kessel ausharren. Dazu ging die Polizei mit Schäferhunden und Pfefferspray auf Personen los, die sich nicht rechtzeitig aus dem gesperrten Perimeter entfernten oder entfernen konnten. Immerhin …

title: İHD 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu: Sandığa darbe, sokağa yumruk
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

İnsan Hakları Derneği’nin (İHD) basından ve açık kaynaklardan derlediği bilgilerle hazırladığı 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç geride kalsa da birçok temel alanda insan hakları ihlallerinin tüm ağırlıyla varlığını sürdürdüğünü ortaya koydu. Raporda, “barış ortamını besleyip güçlendirecek yeterli demokratik adımların atılmaması, üstelik her türlü toplumsal tepkiyi yargı kılıcı ve kolluk sopasıyla bastırmayı düstur edinen yönetim anlayışının devam etmesi yine pek çok temel hakkın ihlaline yol açtı” tespitinde bulunuldu.

Rapora göre, 2025 yılında en çok hak ihlali tespit edilen iller sırasıyla İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Bursa, Van, Antalya, Diyarbakır, Mersin, Kocaeli ve Şırnak oldu. Nüfusa oranla en sık hak ihlali tespit edilen illerin başını ise Tunceli (Dersim) çekti. Onu sırasıyla Erzincan, Bolu, Kırşehir, Şırnak, Van, Ankara, İstanbul, Elazığ ve Iğdır takip etti.

Rapora göre, yaşam hakkına yönelik ihlaller sonucu en az 2.749 kişi hayatını kaybetti, en az 1.112 kişi yaralandı. Yaşam hakkı ihlallerinde başı iş cinayetleri çekti. 2025 yılında en az 2.105 kişi iş cinayetleri sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Böylece 2016-2015 yılları arasında, 10 yılda iş cinayetleri sonucu ölen kişi sayısı 20.009 kişiye ulaştı. 2025’in ekonomik kriz ve MESEM vb. uygulamalarla çocuk işçiliğinde yaşanan kitleselleşmenin sonuçlarına da dikkat çekilen raporda, 26’sı 14 yaş ve altı, en az 94 çocuğun iş cinayetlerinde hayatını kaybettiği aktarıldı.

Rapora göre, Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın “Aile Yılı” ilan ettiği 2025 yılında, kadınlar ve çocuklar yine erkek şiddetinin hedefi oldular. Her gün en az bir kadın ya da çocuk erkek şiddeti sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Kadınlar en çok iktidarca konumlandırıldıkları “evde” şiddete maruz kalırken, bu şiddetin faili de yine eski/yeni eşler, partnerler ile baba, kardeş, damat gibi erkek aile fertleriydi.

Raporda, İHD’nin 1991 yılından bu yana yaptığı çalışmalara dayanılarak, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç nedeniyle en az 36.479 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği aktarıldı. İHD’nin verilerine göre, 25 yıllık bu süreçte 27.025 kişinin doğrudan operasyon ve çatışmalarda, 9.454 kişinin ise çatışmalı süreçle bağlantılı diğer saldırı ve yaşam hakkı ihlalleri sonucu hayatını kaybetti.

Rapora 2025 yılında, en az 159 kişi resmi ihmal ve denetimsizlik sonucu hayatını kaybetti. Deprem, sel vb. doğa olayları sonucu en az 1 kişi öldü, en az 180 kişi yaralandı. Bolu’da otel yangınında 34’ü çocuk, toplam 78 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Orman yangınlarında 10 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Kolluk güçlerine ait araçların karıştığı kazalar sonucu 20’si asker, 7’si mülteci, 1’i çocuk en az 29 kişi yaşamını yitirdi.

Ayrıca, kolluk güçlerinin silah kullanma yetkisini ihlal etmesi sonucu en az 3 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 5 kişi yaralandı.

2025 yılında politik nedenler ya da ırkçı, ayrımcı, fobik saiklerle gerçekleştirilen en az 43 fiziksel ya da silahlı saldırı basına yansıdı. Bu saldırılarla en az 148 kişi doğrudan hedef alınırken, bu saldırılarda en az 15 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 52 kişi yaralandı.

En az 9 gazeteci saldırıya uğradı. Hakan Tosun hayatını kaybetti. Dönemin CHP Genel Bşk. Özgür Özel fiziksel saldırıya uğradı. IŞİD ile ilişkili 2 saldırıda, en az 6 polis ve 6 silahlı örgüt militanı yaşamını yitirdi. En az 5 fobik saldırı tespit edildi. 1 trans kadın öldürüldü. 8 ırkçı saldırıda en az 14 kişi yaralandı. 12 yaşındaki mülteci çocuk evinde uğradığı saldırı sonucu öldürüldü. Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı saldırıya uğradı.

2025 yılında en az 1842 kişi işkence ve diğer kötü muamele niteliğindeki uygulamalara maruz kaldı.

Ankara’da gözaltında işkence gördüğü iddia edilen Musa Nargüner, tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi. 1’i geri gönderme merkezlerinde en az 90 kişi resmi gözaltı yerlerinde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. 1493’ü toplantı ve gösterilere yönelik kolluk müdahalelerinde olmak üzere, en az 1592 kişi resmi gözaltı yerleri dışında işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. En az 185 mahpus hapishanelerde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz bırakıldı.

2024 yerel seçimlerinden 2025 yılı sonuna kadar 27 belediye başkanı görevden uzaklaştırıldı, 13 belediyeye kayyum atandı. 16 belediye başkanı tutuklandı.

author: Equality Now
title: Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer
content:
3rd September 2026


Commemorating and celebrating Gloria Steinem: The life and legacy of a feminist trailblazer


9 min read


The world has lost an extraordinary champion for equality, and Equality Now has lost a beloved friend, mentor and member of our global family.


Gloria Steinem, the pioneering writer, feminist organiser and political activist, passed away at her New York City home on September 2, 2026, at age 92. For more than half a century, she helped shine a light on women’s rights and gave a voice to generations of women’s beliefs around what was possible for themselves and for each other. 


For Equality Now, Gloria’s loss is deeply personal. Our organisation was founded in her home and she stood alongside us from our earliest days, sharing her voice, wisdom, time and encouragement with extraordinary generosity. She was curious about women around the world, shaped especially by her formative years in India post-college.


“Gloria believed in the beauty of shared power. She used her own powerful voice to make space for millions of women’s voices and generations have stepped into their agency because she did. Her legacy is not only the world she shaped but is embedded in all of us who believe in that vision and continue to strive to achieve it,” said

Mona Sinha

, Chief Executive Officer of Equality Now.


“The world has lost one of its best, and I have lost someone who has been a north star in my own life. I first met Gloria when I was a student at Smith College but was blessed to come to know the woman behind her words and activism. What stays with me is her unconditional love of her chosen family, her extraordinary generosity of spirit, her infectious laugh and her curiosity and zest for women’s lives. For someone whose voice carried so much influence, Gloria had the remarkable ability to make space for everyone. 


“She listened to everyone who came to her Talking Circles. She genuinely wanted to hear your thoughts, your experiences and what you were excited to learn. She had this amazing ability to make everyone feel that their stories, their voices and their ideas mattered, which they did. While I will miss her enormously, I know she walks beside us in every movement she has inspired, in women who have stood up for change and the friendships she has nurtured. Each one of us feels a little braver because she embodied what courage looks like.”


Gloria Steinem’s enduring support for Equality Now and women’s rights


Gloria’s involvement with Equality Now as an active supporter of its mission spans the organisation’s entire 34-year history. She played an integral role as a founding member of Equality Now’s Advisory Board in 1992, served on the Board of Directors from 2010 to 2016, in addition to being a Trustee of Equality Now’s UK entity between 2005 and 2019.


At the United Nations, Gloria publicly supported Equality Now’s ongoing 

Words and Deeds

 campaign, which for almost three decades has highlighted sex discriminatory laws around the world and called for legal reform.


She stood with us against Big Apple Oriental Tours, a New York company promoting sex tourism in Asia, helping press authorities to act in a campaign that ultimately led to legal action against the company and strengthened the case for tougher anti-trafficking laws. 


For over 50 years, Gloria fought to strengthen legal protections for women and girls in the US by championing the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA), which would amend the US Constitution to guarantee equal rights under the law, irrespective of sex. In recent years, she worked alongside Equality Now and the ERA Coalition, helping build pressure on the Biden administration to recognise the ERA.

President Biden declared the ERA the law of the land

 in January 2025.


She was also a longstanding co-chair of Equality Now’s annual Make Equality Reality Gala,  helping the organisation to raise much-needed resources to protect and promote the rights of women and girls globally. In recognition of her tireless work to make equality a reality for everyone, Equality Now honoured Gloria for her lifelong commitment at the 2014

Make Equality Reality Gala

. 


A remarkable life


Born on March 25, 1934, Gloria’s life was a testament to her unwavering commitment to advancing gender equality and in the power of people coming together to create change.


In the 1960s, she made her mark as a journalist covering women’s rights and other social issues. She went on to become one of …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Inukjuak man accused of murder was ordered to not contact victim
content:
The Inukjuak man charged with first-degree murder for the death of his partner Elisabeth Qumak had been under a court order to not contact her when she was found dead inside a home in the community. 


Police

found

 the 41-year-old woman with stab wounds on Aug. 24, after Charlie Palliser arrived at the community’s police station to report he had committed a crime. She was pronounced dead at a local health centre.


The 45-year-old already faced charges for a break and enter and assault at Qumak’s home on July 17, court documents reveal. He was released on July 22 with conditions, including that he refrain from contacting her.


The Nunavik Police Service declined to comment on what happened on July 17, saying the investigation has since been handed over to provincial police in Quebec.


When reached by Nunatsiaq News, Quebec police also declined to comment.


Palliser had 

also given a curfew and was expected to attend social services meetings as well as activities organized by non-profit Saqijuq at least twice a month.


According to its website, the organization provides “alternatives to incarceration” by “promoting healthy lifestyles, strengthening cultural connections, and rehabilitating individuals.” It offers activities such as hunting, fishing and camping and workshops revolving around Inuit values and traditions. 


Nunatsiaq News asked Saqijuq if Palliser took part in any of their programs but has yet to hear back.


A Montreal-based coalition

of feminists against domestic violence

 has so far recorded 17 suspected

femicides in the province since the beginning of this year.


The figure is higher than what’s commonly reported in the media because the group monitors gender-based violence in situations that exclude romantic relationships, general co-ordinator Julie Antoine said in an interview. 


“It often happens that men are under no contact orders after a separation that they ultimately end up committing a femicide. Either the crime happens when the woman announces she wants to leave him, or the crime happens happens after an order is issued,” she said.


In about half of these 17 cases, she said, the group

 confirmed that the accused had previously been charged with a violent crime. 


“The state is falling in its role of protecting women, and it’s evident when you see that a high percentage of individuals involved in femicide cases were already known to the justice system,” Antoine said.


Palliser’s next court appearance is scheduled for Dec. 14.

author: Saneze Tshayana, Ana Stevenson, and Monica G. Fernandes
title: Wathint’ abafazi 70 years on
content:
The year 2026 marks the 70

th

 anniversary of the 1956

Women’s March

 against extending the

dompas

 to the black women of South Africa. Every August, the commemoration of Women’s Month highlights the inheritances and

unfinished legacies

 of women’s anti-apartheid resistance. This Women’s Month, it is timely to reflect on the legacies of women’s activism in South Africa over 70 years and more.


FEDSAW members in anti-Apartheid meeting


Organised by the

Federation of South African Women

 (FEDSAW), the 1956 Women’s March was a multiracial mass demonstration against pass laws. An estimated 20,000 women descended on Pretoria’s Union Buildings, presenting 14,000 petitions to

Prime Minister J.G. Strijdom

. Established in 1954, FEDSAW’s leadership, under luminaries such as

Lilian Ngoyi

,

Helen Joseph

,

Rahima Moosa

, and

Sophia Williams

, was particularly significant.


Previous women’s organising had arisen within the increasingly strict racial boundaries of the colonial and apartheid state. In 1913,

Charlotte Mannya Maxeke

 had led the

women’s anti-pass campaign

 in Bloemfontein, in the then Orange Free State. This led to the establishment of the

Bantu Women’s League

, which later became the

African National Congress

(ANC)

Women’s League

 in 1948. Similarly, the

Black Sash

, established in 1955, was an organisation of white women, bringing English-speaking women together with a smaller group of Afrikaans-speaking women. Alongside FEDSAW, these anti-apartheid resistance organisations were represented at the Women’s March.


The freedom song ‘

Wathint’ abafazi

, Strijdom!’, with the words ‘

Wathint’ abafazi, wathint’ imbokodo, uzu kufa!

’ (‘You strike a woman, you strike a rock, you will be crushed!’), featured at the 1956 protest. The

political slogan

 ‘

Wathint’ abafazi, wathint’ imbokodo

’ would become one of the liberation movement’s most enduring phrases, ricocheting across its posters and popular culture over the next four decades.


Yet, the slogan’s continued ubiquity into the twenty-first century belies the unevenness with which women’s activism has been recorded and remembered. Often invoked in popular memory, women’s activism has too often been marginalised against a celebration of men’s leadership, armed struggle, and formal political institutions.


A 2025

Special Issue

 of the

South African Historical Journal

, edited by Monica G. Fernandes and Ana Stevenson, centres women’s fight against apartheid. Spotlighting individuals and organisations, authors explore Ngoyi’s

urban roots

 and Williams’ formative experiences in the

youth movement

; uncover lesser known figures such as

Vesta Smith

 and

Joyce Piliso-Seroke

; consider Jewish social scientists Hilda Kuper and Ellen Hellmann’s

relationship

 with  scholar-activists of colour Fatima Meer and Regina Gelana Twala; revisit

Black internationalism

, the

Black Sash

, and the

ANC Women’s Section

; and critique

post-1994 literature

 about women’s experiences in the struggle.


This 70

th

 anniversary also offers a timely opportunity to consider women’s continuing activism towards realising the rights guaranteed in the 1996

Constitution

, 30 years later. Thanks to the efforts of various women’s groups as South Africa democratised, gender rights were enshrined in the final Constitution: in the

Bill of Rights

, gender is named as one of a slew of identifiers in anti-discriminatory legislation. However, the guarantees of gender equality have not gone unopposed, seen in South Africa most tellingly through the perniciously

high rates

 of men’s abuse of women, an enduring and insidious issue, more than 30 years into this democracy.


Legally, according to this Constitution, the status of South African women should be indisputable, protected as they are by gender-specific legislation against discrimination. Paradoxically, however, the ubiquity of men’s abuse of women, particularly in the context of intimate partner relationships, shatters any visions of constitutional equality.


Despite multiple

Presidential Summits

 dedicated to gendered violence, the drafting of the

National Strategic Plan on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide

 in 2020, and the establishment of the

Gender-Based Violence and Femicide (GBVF) Response Fund

, high rates of gendered violence continue to plague twenty-first century South Africa. This is the legacy of the historical and continuing disregard of women’s activism: where …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Rosario: movilización contra los femicidios y en reclamo de la emergencia en violencia de género
content:
Las organizaciones decidieron movilizarse luego de que se conocieran tres femicidios en 15 días.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Escuchar el reporte de Darío Uliassi desde Aire Libre Radio Comunitaria.


Concentraron este miércoles a las 17 frente a la Municipalidad de Rosario y finalizaron con un acto en la puerta de la sede de Gobernación de la provincia en la ciudad.


De la movilización participaron organizaciones feministas, sociales y políticas que se expresaron en contra de la violencia machista y reclamaron justicia por los femicidios.


En la provincia de Santa Fe se registraron más de 30 femicidios en lo que va del año. Además, se contabilizaron 10 víctimas más que en el mismo período del año pasado.


“Paren de matarnos” fue la consigna que encabezó la movilización donde las organizaciones advirtieron por la suba de casos, que se profundizan con el desmantelamiento de las políticas de género en los distintos niveles del Estado.


En declaraciones a Aire Libre, Gabriela Sosa, referente del movimiento feminista Mujeres por la Matria Latinoamericana (Mumalá), exigió la sanción de una ley provincial que declare la emergencia en violencia de género y que se cumpla la ordenanza local que declaró la emergencia hace un tiempo.


“Hemos presentado proyectos para que se declare la emergencia en violencia de género en Santa Fe y también que se pueda aplicar aquella ordenanza de hace varios años que ya declaraba la emergencia en Rosario y que disponía de recursos que siguen estando pendientes”.


Foto: Aire Libre- Rosario


Sosa también denunció las consecuencias del desmantelamiento de políticas públicas: “Esta quita de recursos, a la par de los discursos de odios, comienzan a impactar que las mujeres cada vez denunciamos menos, un 9% de la víctimas habían denunciado a su agresor anteriormente”.


Y agregó: “Por supuesto faltan campañas de prevención, faltan que los medios de comunicación tengan pautas de los estados municipales, provinciales y nacionales para informar de qué hacer”.

https://agencia.farco.org.ar/2026/08/27/rosario-movilizacion-contra-los-femicidios-y-en-reclamo-de-la-emergencia-en-violencia-de-genero/
