title: Punk-Violin vs Market: Paul Geigerzähler о сквотах, крахе надежд 89-го и нигилизме к законам
content:
Авторская рубрика legal illegal scheißegal и ее ведущий Артур Гранд снова вещают на youtube-канале проекта No Future из глубины немецкого андеграунда.

«В этом выпуске мы отправляемся на улицы берлинского Фридрихсхайна — на легендарную Ригаер штрассе (Rigaer Straße), где каждый свободный метр отвоеван у джентрификации и полиции, — поясняет No Future. — Наш проводник — Paul Geigerzähler: панк-скрипач, сквотер с 30-летним стажем, активист синдикалистского профсоюза FAU и человек с уникальной идентичностью, соединяющей саксонские бунтарские традиции и сорбские (славянские) корни.

Мы не будем обсуждать сухую теорию. Этот выпуск — глубокое погружение в то, как выжить, сохранить свободу и не сойти с ума в мире тотального контроля.»

— Упущенный момент 1989-го: почему крушение Берлинской стены и конец ГДР для многих стали не началом свободы, а моментом, когда уникальный шанс на свободный, низовой социализм был продан за западные супермаркеты и превращение человека в товар.

— Практика FAU против системного болота: как работает анархо-синдикализм сегодня. Почему реальная борьба за права рабочих и мигрантов — это не абстрактные лозунги, а прямой саботаж капиталистического рынка труда.

— Сквоты и коллективный разум: как устроена жизнь в современных берлинских хаус-проектах, почему их жителям плевать на безумный рост цен на аренду и как бывшие бунтари уживаются с церковными общинами, помогающими беженцам.

00:00:00 — Berlin’s Burning: Легенда Ригерстрассе и дух сквоттинга. Вводная часть про знаменитый сквот Rigaer 94 и анархистскую альтернативу капитализму.

00:02:32 — Короткий политический манифест. Бескомпромиссное высказывание на улицах Берлина против диктатуры и авторитаризма.

00:03:15 — Пауль Нагель: практик анархизма против пустой болтовни. 30 лет сквоттерства, борьба за права мигрантов и панк на скрипке.

00:08:25 — Анархо-синдикализм в действии: как FAU борется за права трудящихся. Прямое действие, отказ от «дерьмовой работы» и рабочее самоуправление.

00:18:55 — Правый поворот и кризис демократического фасада. Почему системные левые провалились, а капитализм превратил политику в шоу.

00:23:30 — Blues Mass: прогрессивная церковь и сопротивление в ГДР. Как церковные площадки укрывали панков при диктатуре и беженцев сегодня.

00:27:06 — Сорбы: панк и колониальное прошлое Саксонии. Борьба за идентичность славянского меньшинства и музыкальный перформанс Пауля.

00:39:25 — ГДР vs Капитализм: как нас лишили эмансипации и превратили в товар. Как надежды 1989 года разбились о поглощение Востока западным рынком.

00:46:52 — Низовая взаимопомощь: немецкий педантизм на службе анархии. Как устроен уличный пункт обмена вещами и порядок в анархо-проектах.

00:48:46 — От сквота к хаус-проекту: как защитить свое жилье от спекулянтов. Опыт легализации и борьбы кооперативов против джентрификации.

title: Burak Başer’i hatırlıyor musunuz?
content:
Esenyurt KYK Erkek Öğrenci Yurdu'ndan ücret gecikmesi gerekçesiyle çıkarılan Burak Başer, 7 Kasım 2022'de barınma hakkı için yurt önünde oturma eylemine başladı. Başer'in başlattığı eylem, birçok öğrencinin yaşadığı barınma sorununu dile getirmesine neden oldu.


“Yurtta kalmak istiyorum” dedi, 10 yıl ceza aldı: Burak Başer Dosyası Yargıtay’da


11 Şubat 2026


Başer, eyleminin altıncı haftasında, 15 Aralık 2022'de gözaltına alındı ve dört gün sonra tutuklandı. Başer, cezaevindeyken açtığı davayı kazandı. İdare Mahkemesi, Başer'i haklı buldu ve 8 Kasım 2023'te tahliye oldu. Tahliyesinin ardından okuluna dönen Başer, 6 Şubat 2024'te tekrar tutuklandı.


Yeniden tutuklanan Başer’e “örgüt üyeliği” ve “örgüte finansman” suçlamalarıyla 10 yıl 6 ay hapis cezası verildi. Karar istinafta onandı, dosya Yargıtay aşamasında.


Başer halen Kocaeli Kandıra Cezaevi’nde (resmi adıyla Kocaeli 1 No’lu F Tipi Cezaevi) tutuluyor. 19 yaşında cezaevine giren Başer’in, eğer Yargıtay cezasını onarsa 29 yaşında tahliye olacak.


Dosyada “örgüte finansman” suçlamasına dayanak olarak, cezaevindeki bir mahpusa gönderilen iki ayrı 200 TL’lik (toplam 400 TL) para transferi gösterildi. Savcılık, bu ödemeleri örgütsel bağ kapsamında değerlendirdi. İddianamede, Başer’in yeşil gömlek giydiği fotoğrafın “savaşçı kanaati” işaret ettiği öne sürüldü.


Fotoğraf: ANKA


Tutuklu öğrenci Başer’den davaya çağrı: Gelin bir de benden dinleyin


16 Eylül 2025


Başer'den mektup...


İki yıldan fazla süredir cezaevinde olan Burak Başer, bianet'e gönderdiği mektubunda Akbelen'de, Ankara'da öğretmenler ve madencilerin hakları için verdiği mücadeleyi hatırlatıyor.


Başer'in mektubu...


Bugün Anadolu’nun dört bir yanında hak ve adalet mücadelesi sürüyor. Akbelen’de, Ordu Perşembe Yaylası'nda, Varto’da, Rize Pazar’da köylüler, Ankara’da öğretmenler ve madenciler, kuyu tiplerinde ve diğer hapishanelerde tutsaklar direniyor.


Akbelen halkı diyordu bize; "Bu zeytinlik yasası çıkarsa Anadolu dağları emperyalistler için delik deşik edilecek." Bugün bunu yaşıyoruz.


Madenciler diyordu bize; "Yerin yedi kat altında ter akıtıyoruz. Patronlar dökülen alın terimizden, kanımızdan kasalarını dolduruyorlar. Bu da yetmezmiş gibi hakkımızı isteyince işe gitmedik diye dava açılıyor."


Kuyu tiplerinde tutsaklar haykırıyor; "Kuyularda bizi diri diri mezara gömmelerine izin vermeyeceğiz."


İçeriden dışarıya direniş dalgası dövüyor duvarları. Ve direnişlerimiz, birliğimiz kazanmamızı sağlayacak gücümüzdür. Bugün Marmara 6 No’lu L Tipi Hapishanesi’nde arkadaşlarımız kilitlendikleri 8 metrekarede en temel haklar için direniyorlar. Tacettin Eral Şahin, Can Dursun, Hasan Basri Yıldız, Emircan Yazı, Cemil Kurt ve Engin Ateş süresiz açlık grevindedir. Ayrıca Sincan Kadın Kapalı Hapishanesi’nde suçlu kimliği uygulamasına karşı da Gözde Tolga süresiz açlık grevindedir.


Hz. Ali yıllar önce "Görmek istemeyen göze ışık ne yapsın?" demiştir. Egemenler bizi görmek istemiyor. Ancak halkın tüm kesimlerinin bir araya gelerek yaydığı ışığı zalimler bile görmezden gelemez. Bir yerde bir çığlık yükseliyorsa oradan ne oluyor diye sormalıyız. Çünkü o çığlık yalnızca kendi gelecekleri için atılan bir çığlık değildir. Bir ülkenin çığlığıdır.


Arkadaşlarımızın açlık grevi direnişi bu çığlığın bir parçasıdır. Sizden isteğimiz bu çığlığı duymanız ve duyurmanızdır.


Çalışmalarınızda başarılar diliyoruz, kolay gelsin.

title: Protest against geothermal power plant project ends 124th day
content:
The vigil launched by the Youth Assembly of the Gimgim (Varto) Ecology Platform against the Geothermal Power Plant (JES) project in Xwarik village is ongoing.


A banner reading “The people of Varto do not want a geothermal power plant. Do not touch my water, my soil” was hung at the vigil site as the protest entered its 124th day.


Visiting the vigil site, New Party Istanbul MP Evrim Rızvanoğlu said the concerns of the people of Gimgim regarding the project were justified. Rızvanoğlu also criticised the decision that an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was “not required” for the project.


Gimgim Ecology Platform member Çayan Dursun said the struggle against the geothermal power plant project had been ongoing since January 22, and that the tent vigil had continued since May 3.


Dursun said they were also pursuing the struggle through legal channels and stressed the importance of bringing the issue before Parliament. “We will win; there is no second option. We do not accept anything carried out without the consent of the people,” he said.


Following the statements, the delegation met with citizens maintaining the tent vigil and exchanged views on the process.

author: Clare Hymer
title: Green Peer Refuses to Pay Full Thames Water Bill to Protest Sewage Pollution
content:
A Green party peer is refusing to pay her full Thames Water bill in protest at the supplier’s pollution record.


Writing in the Guardian

, Jenny Jones – a long-time campaigner against sewage pollution and the privatised water industry – said she has stopped paying part of her bill whilst the company pollutes Britain’s rivers and coastlines.


She wrote to Thames Water to explain she was happy to pay the part of the bill related to her water supply, but not to the part for dealing with sewage. The firm replied saying it doesn’t split bills in that way, and followed up with “a threatening letter and a vastly increased bill with penalty charges,” Jones said. 


She also called for the water industry to be brought back into public ownership.


She cited a 2025 Guardian report that found

serious pollution incidents by English water companies had increased by 60%

 the previous year, with Thames Water being the worst offender. 


“I decided that if the government wouldn’t act, I could at least do my part and not pay for this travesty,” Jones said. 


“Nothing will change until these companies go officially bankrupt and the quickest way of ensuring that happens is if people stop paying their bills. 


“A few decades ago millions of people did exactly that with the poll tax and the government backed down. (I was taken to court over that.) So why not use the same non-payment tactic to end water privatisation?”


Jones said there had also been mention of bailiffs, and she was prepared to face legal action.


“I will calmly read all the threatening letters and await the court case against me,” she said. “I have drawn a line in the sand. And I hope to win this particular battle,” she said. 


Jones’ solo protest echoes the

Don’t Pay campaign

 in 2022, which saw

more than 100,000 people

 sign up to stop paying their energy bills. It was described by energy firm E.ON as an

“existential threat”

 to the sector.

author: Unknown
title: Accessibilité dans les transports : les jeunes déficients visuels appellent à une mobilisation nationale le samedi 19 septembre
content:
Deux personnes aveugles sont mortes ces derniers mois après être tombées sur les voies du métro, à Paris puis à Lyon. Ces drames mettent en lumière les conséquences concrètes d'un manque d'accessibilité des transports : une perte d'autonomie, mais aussi une exposition à des situations de danger qui pourraient être évitées.


C'est pourquoi le collectif de jeunes citoyens aveugles et malvoyants pour l'accessibilité des transports appelle à une mobilisation nationale le samedi 19 septembre 2026 à 13h00, place d'Italie devant la Mairie du 13

e

 arrondissement, à Paris.


«

 

L'accessibilité ne doit pas être considérée comme un confort ou comme une politique réservée au handicap : elle permet concrètement à chacun de se déplacer de manière plus sûre

 

», estime Benjamin Rosan, l'organisateur du mouvement.


Cette mobilisation inédite s'inscrit dans la continuité de la première marche blanche organisée à Paris en hommage à André-Germain Dingome au mois de janvier, après son décès dans le métro de Paris. Réunis à Denfert-Rochereau pour lui rendre hommage, le collectif a souhaité faire de cette mobilisation un point de départ pour porter une revendication plus large : l'accessibilité des transports ne peut plus être traitée comme une question secondaire.


Le samedi 19 septembre 2026 à 13h00, place d'Italie, devant la mairie du 13

e

 arrondissement de Paris, le collectif appelle à un rassemblement pour demander des mesures concrètes en faveur de transports sécurisés. Cette mobilisation ne concerne pas uniquement Paris ou les grandes métropoles : il demande une véritable politique nationale, qui prenne également en compte les territoires ruraux et périurbains, où l'absence de solutions de transport accessibles peut entraîner des conséquences majeures sur l'autonomie et la vie quotidienne.


Des avancées, mais un combat qui doit continuer :


En 2023, une pétition intitulée «

 

Pour un métro parlant, dès maintenant

 

» avait recueilli près de 11 000 signatures pour demander la vocalisation du métro parisien. Cette mobilisation a contribué à faire avancer le sujet : lancement de l'application «

 

Compagnon Train

 

», permettant d'annoncer vocalement les stations sur plusieurs lignes, et déploiement progressif de solutions de sonorisation dans les anciennes rames. Ces avancées montrent qu'une mobilisation collective peut produire des résultats. Elles doivent désormais être poursuivies et étendues à l'ensemble des réseaux de transport.


Un plan national, avec des engagements vérifiables


Le collectif demande concrètement au Gouvernement de mettre en place un plan national pluriannuel pour l'accessibilité des transports comprenant notamment :


 un état des lieux public de l'accessibilité des réseaux de transport sur l'ensemble du territoire

 

;

 un calendrier de mise en accessibilité à court, moyen et long terme

 

;

 des financements clairement identifiés

 

;

 un responsable désigné pour chaque engagement

 

;

 la mise en accessibilité des stations, gares et arrêts, mais également des correspondances et des cheminements

 

;

 des «

 

informations voyageurs

 

» accessibles visuellement et auditivement

 

;

 le maintien en fonctionnement des équipements indispensables à l'accessibilité et des solutions de remplacement en cas de panne

 

;

 des solutions de transport accessibles dans les territoires ruraux et périurbains

 

;

 l'association systématique des personnes en situation de handicap à la conception, aux tests et au suivi des aménagements.


«

 

Nous ne voulons plus de nouvelles annonces sans calendrier. Nous demandons des dates, des moyens et des résultats

 

!

 

», annonce Samantha Lefebvre, porte-parole du collectif.


Du handicap à l'intérêt général :


Si la mobilisation est née d'une réalité vécue par des jeunes déficients visuels, ses revendications dépassent largement le seul handicap visuel. Une station accessible est également plus facile à utiliser pour une personne âgée, un parent avec une poussette, une personne enceinte, une personne temporairement blessée ou un voyageur se déplaçant avec des bagages.


Dans les territoires ruraux et périurbains, l'enjeu est encore plus important. Lorsqu'une personne qui ne peut pas conduire ne dispose pas d'un transport accessible, ce sont potentiellement ses études, son emploi, son accès aux soins et sa capacité à maintenir des liens avec ses proches qui sont remis en cause.

Benjamin Rosan — Organisateur — 06 36 66 …

author: anred
title: Lanzan campaña por el sobreseimiento de 19 manifestantes llevados a juicio por participar del «Jujeñazo»
content:
Represión en Jujuy ante el rechazo a la reforma constitucional – Foto: Guillermo Castro


A tres años del «Jujeñazo», 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio en una causa que comenzará el 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el 6 de noviembre. Organizaciones de derechos humanos, sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un llamamiento nacional para exigir su absolución y sobreseimiento y denunciar un nuevo avance de la criminalización de la protesta social. «No puede haber una Justicia para quienes lucharon y otra para quienes ejercían el poder y dieron órdenes ilegítimas», remarca el llamamiento, que reclama además investigar e imputar a los funcionarios implicados en la represión. «Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios» fue la consigna que sintetizó el «Jujeñazo» de junio de 2023, una masiva movilización que reunió el reclamo de docentes y estatales por salarios con la defensa de los territorios de las comunidades originarias y el rechazo a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales, y que tuvo como respuesta una brutal represión que dejó más de cien personas detenidas, numerosas heridas y manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones.

Por ANRed.


A tres años del «Jujeñazo», 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio

, en una causa cuyo debate comenzará el próximo

lunes 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el viernes 6 de noviembre

. Ante esta situación, organismos de derechos humanos, organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un

 llamamiento nacional para exigir el sobreseimiento y la absolución

 de quienes son perseguidos judicialmente, y cuyo petitorio se puede

firmar aquí

.


La conssigna «

Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios

» fue la consigna que sintetizó las jornadas de

junio de 2023

, cuando la

lucha de docentes y trabajadores estatales por salarios confluyó con la resistencia de las comunidades originarias en defensa de sus territorios y con el rechazo de organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales

. Según el llamamiento, aquella movilización «arrancó uno de los aumentos salariales más importantes para los estatales jujeños y puso en jaque al gobierno provincial».


Imagen: Originarios.ar


La respuesta del gobierno de Morales en ese momento fue una

fuerte represión,

recuerda el documento del llamamiento: «

una brutal represión, con detenidos, numerosos heridos y manifestantes que sufrieron gravísimas lesiones, entre ellas pérdida de visión. Mas de 100 detenciones que luego derivaron en libertades y sobreseimientos».

 Aquel año, organizaciones de derechos humanos y organismos antirrepresivos también documentaron

detenciones irregulares, el uso desproporcionado de la fuerza y lesiones graves

 durante aquellos operativos.


La persecución judicial, sin embargo, continuó después de la represión porque, tres años más tarde, 1

9 personas que participaron de aquellas protestas son llevadas hoy a juicio

. El proceso está atravesado, denuncian desde el llamamiento, por «

graves cuestionamientos de las defensas respecto del derecho de defensa, el debido proceso y la imparcialidad judicial»

. Además, se cuestiona el modo en que fue fijada la audiencia: «el 21 de agosto de 2026 fue rechazado el pedido de no fijar audiencia y apenas seis días después, con quejas en trámite, el 27 de agosto, se notificó un debate de enorme magnitud concentrado en diez jornadas».


«¿Cómo piensa Morales devolverle la vista a nuestros hermanos? ¿El objetivo es enceguecer a todo el pueblo de Jujuy?»


Mientras se acelera el proceso contra quienes participaron de la movilización, las organizaciones reclaman que la Justicia avance sobre quienes ordenaron la represión: «

seguimos reclamando que se investiguen las responsabilidades políticas y penales por la represión de junio de 2023

, que dejó manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones, y que

se avance también en la causa de Caspalá, donde se debate sobre el territorio de la Comunidad Originaria y la corrupción de los funcionarios del gobierno provincial»

. Así, la campaña por el sobreseimiento de quienes participaron de la pueblada del «Jujeñazo» vuelve así a inscribirse en una disputa más amplia por

el territorio, los recursos naturales y el derecho a protestar

.


Asimimos, el juicio que comenzará en octubre no es solamente el capítulo …

title: PUNK - From Mosh Pits to Protests
content:
Author : PUNK Title : From Mosh Pits to Protests Subtitle : Investigating how the Punk Community Motivates Punks to Participate in Social Movements. Date : May 1, 2026
From Mosh Pits to Protests: Investigating how the Punk Community Motivates Punks to Participate in Social Movements. PUNK (May 1, 2026)
Contents [[#_Toc228532953][Section 1: Introduction. 3]] [[#_Toc228532954][Purpose. 3]] [[#_Toc228532955][A Brief History of Punk-Rock Subculture. 4]] [[#_Toc228532956][Positionality Statement 18]] [[#_Toc228532957][Section 2: Literature Review.. 19]] [[#_Toc228532958][Communities. 20]] [[#_Toc228532959][Resistance. 23]] [[#_Toc228532960][Social Movements. 25]] [[#_Toc228532961][Emotional Habitus. 26]] [[#_Toc228532962][Narrative. 27]] [[#_Toc228532963][Section 3: Theoretical Framework. 29]] [[#_Toc228532964][Definitions. 29]] [[#_Toc228532965][Punk Rock. 29]] [[#_Toc228532966][Punk Shows. 30]] [[#_Toc228532967][Moral Shock. 31]] [[#_Toc228532968][Moral Panic. 31]] [[#_Toc228532969][Analytical Lens. 32]] [[#_Toc228532970][Section 4: Methods. 33]] [[#_Toc228532971][Music. 33]] [[#_Toc228532972][Written & Oral 34]] [[#_Toc228532973][Visual 35]] [[#_Toc228532974][Section 5: Findings. 36]] [[#_Toc228532975][Resistance to Social Norms. 36]] [[#_Toc228532976][DIY Culture. 39]] [[#_Toc228532977][Resistance to State Coercion. 46]] [[#_Toc228532978][Guardianship. 51]] [[#_Toc228532979][Resistance to Inequality. 55]] [[#_Toc228532980][Participation in Social Movements. 58]] [[#_Toc228532981][Section 6: Conclusion. 62]] [[#_Toc228532982][Appendix 1. 63]] [[#_Toc228532983][Bibliography. 72]] * Section 1: Introduction Purpose There is a significant gap within the literature pertaining to Punks (as individuals) and the Punk-Rock music subculture. Despite the thematic overlaps of the Punk-Rock subculture with social movements literature regarding what drives political participation (Passy 2020; Polletta 2025; Tilly and Tarrow 2015; Woods 2003) and the literature about the emotionality of protests and social movements (Gould 2009; Kingston and Ferry 2008; Jasper 1998; Blackington 2024) academia has largely either purposefully or implicitly ignored Punk-Rock as a topic of analysis. Additionally, there is significant literature on the power of music and more broadly art as a political force (Goldman 1910;1914; Orwell 2016; Ziv 2019; Vance and Potash 2022; Ward 2020), yet, despite being a music-based subculture, Punk Rock is excluded from that literature. The literature gap is even more interesting when considering Hip-Hop music, which has existed temporally for approximately as long as Punk [1] and yet Hip-Hop as it relates to social movements has received significantly more analysis in the literature (Chang 2005; Kitwana 2003; Rose 1994). There lies the primary goal of this thesis project; to begin filling that gap in the analysis and bring Punks into the discussion. The secondary goal of this thesis project is to attempt to break the stereotypes associated with the Punk community as chaotic, violent, and emotional. As a political scientist and a Punk, I argue it is important to bring this politically relevant subculture into the discussion because not including Punks only limits analysis of social movements where Punks are present. Punks are people whose political feeling (Gould 2009) manifests as anger, frustration, and dissatisfaction with society because the status quo is constantly challenging their values. The Punk community’s emotional habitus reflects their political feeling (Gould 2009). I argue that Punks (as individuals) are motivated to participate in social movements by a constant state of moral panic [2] , which is maintained by the Punk community and engagement with Punk Rock music. The following content of this thesis includes in this section a brief historical analysis of the Punk-Rock subculture to illustrate the semi-cohesive set of values that Punks ascribe to, followed by a positionality statement laying out how I fit into this discussion as a Punk myself. Section 2 will be a literature review. Section 3 will lay out the theoretical framework for this thesis. Section 4 of this thesis will include the methods section, focusing on the narrative of Punk Rock music and on visual evidence of Punks participating in social movements. Section 5 …

title: Rusya: Almanya'nın eylemlerine sert karşılık verilecek
content:
Rusya Dışişleri Bakanlığından yapılan açıklamada, Almanya'nın, Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda patlayıcı yüklü İHA bulunduğu gerekçesiyle Rusya'ya karşı bazı tedbirler aldığı anımsatıldı.

Bu nedenle Almanya'nın Moskova Büyükelçiliği Maslahatgüzarı Bernd Finke'nin bakanlığa çağrıldığı kaydedilen açıklamada, Rus tarafının kendisine yöneltilen suçlamaları reddettiği belirtildi.

Açıklamada, Berlin'in ikili ilişkilerin tamamen bozulması yönünde adım attığı vurgulanarak, "Berlin, Rusya-Almanya ilişkilerindeki durumu gerginleştirmeyi amaçlayan provokasyona bilinçli şekilde başvurdu. Almanya yönetiminin eylemlerine sert karşılık verilecek." ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Almanya'daki Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda 4 Ağustos'ta Ukrayna'ya ait bir nakliye uçağının yakınında patlayıcı düzeneği içerdiği değerlendirilen İHA bulunmuştu.

ABD istihbaratı, bulunan patlayıcı yüklü İHA'nın özelliklerinin, Rus askeri istihbaratına "özgü" olduğunu iddia etmişti.

Almanya hükümeti, dün, olayla ilgili soruşturmada elde edilen bulguların Rusya'yı sorumlu gösterdiğini belirterek, bir dizi tedbir açıklamıştı.

Karar gereği, Rusya'nın Bonn Başkonsolosluğu 18 Eylül itibarıyla kapatılacak, Berlin'deki Rus Evi ile ilgili sözleşme feshedilecek, Rus vatandaşlarına yönelik giriş kontrolleri sıkılaştırılacak ve Rusya'nın sözde gölge filosuna yönelik baskı artırılacak.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Stand Up for Multifaith Democracy": U.S. Activists, Lawmakers Protest India's RSS & Hindu Supremacy
content:
Demonstrators gathered outside Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday to protest against the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, a far-right Indian paramilitary Hindu nationalist organization with close ties to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The leader of the

RSS

, Mohan Bhagwat, was holding a rally inside the arena to launch a global speaking tour marking the 100th anniversary of the

RSS

.


The RSS’s “explicitly stated mission, its purpose, is to create a Hindu Rashtra, a Hindu nation — to take the India that is a secular and inclusive democracy and transform it into a country that is just for Hindus, where Muslims, Christians, Sikhs and other minorities are basically erased,” says Sunita Viswanath, co-founder of Hindus for Human Rights Action. ”

RSS

 affiliates, these Hindu right-wing organizations, exist in growing numbers in the diaspora, especially in America.”


“In 1939, [Madison Square Garden] hosted a Nazi rally with swastikas hung from the banners around a portrait of George Washington. They said they wouldn’t do something like that again, and yet here they were hosting Mohan Bhagwat, spouting a similar fascist ideology,” says Brad Lander, a Democratic nominee for Congress from New York City, who joined Saturday’s protest.

author: Ivan Mayabi
title: Kenya’s Kairos After the #Occupy Churches Protests
content:
In 2024, a wave of youth-led protests in Kenya, which organizers and commentators came to call “Occupy Churches”, directed itself not at the state but at the country’s most visible religious institutions – its megachurches, its prosperity preachers, the whole apparatus of what scholars call the “

neo-Pentecostal political economy

“. And the question I keep circling is whether this movement is best understood as a crisis

for

 Kenyan Christianity or as, in some sense, an event

within

 it – i.e. not an attack from outside the tradition but an argument the tradition is having, urgently and in public, with itself.


This educated, digitally connected youth demographic had identified religious institutions as central pillars sustaining the oppressive political order. Youth activists asserted that

church leaders had become complicit in state oppression

 by accepting money from corrupt politicians, surrendering sacred altars to political actors, and maintaining silence in a time of severe economic distress. 


The political economy of extractive ministry and elite patronage


Religious authority in Kenya, and across much of the continent, has for decades functioned less as a moral counterweight to power than as its most reliable subcontractor. The alliance is old and almost structurally inevitable – a state that cannot always be trusted to deliver services will always find it convenient to borrow legitimacy from an institution that promises something even the state cannot: salvation, certainty, a story of individual transformation that, however politically convenient for elites, is also, for the person living it, a genuine and often quite beautiful thing. Pentecostal and Charismatic movements provide essential social networks, existential security, and personal empowerment in urban environments plagued by severe inequality and state neglect. Through

emphasis on personal transformation, moral discipline, and individual efficacy,

 churches equip believers with practical survival strategies to navigate economic precarity. 


However, most of these movements operate under a “

Prosperity Gospel

” theology, a framework that interprets material wealth and physical well-being as direct indicators of divine favour unlocked through financial contributions. Originating from international Pentecostal currents and adapting to indigenous spiritual frameworks,

prosperity theology centres on seed-sowing economics

. In this transactional framework, congregants are urged to yield financial offerings to church proprietors to activate supernatural returns.

Where institutional financial records remain opaque and unregulated, extractive ministry thrives

. Capital generated from millions of socio-economically marginalized adherents is accumulated tax-free by religious elites who showcase luxury assets and extravagant personal lifestyles. This accumulation model operates through a psychological apparatus that spiritualizes structural poverty, framing systemic economic failures as personal spiritual deficits resulting from insufficient faith or inadequate financial giving.


The financial imperatives of extractive religious institutions create a structural convergence with the political class. Political figures have

routinely leveraged the pulpit

 to secure political legitimacy, purchase moral sanitization, and gain access to voting blocs. In exchange for substantial cash donations to church building funds and public fundraisers, politicians are granted access to church platforms during weekend services. From these sacred altars, political elites advance electoral agendas, defend unpopular policies, and evade accountability for corruption and governance failures.


This dynamic was

prominently demonstrated

 in Kenya during the consolidation of President William Ruto’s administration. Tracing his political trajectory from youth evangelism in the North Rift Evangelistic Team to his presidential campaigns, Ruto deployed Pentecostal language and networks to build a powerful political coalition. Framed as a spiritual battle of the poor “hustlers” against elite dynasties, his political strategy relied heavily on church prayer rallies, frequent endorsements by evangelical prelates, and public declarations that his electoral triumph was a divine mandate. Following his election, this

Pentecostalization of statecraft

 was institutionalized through regular interdenominational prayer services inside the State House, diplomatic prayer …

author: Unknown
title: Rencontres anticarcérales du 17 au 27 septembre à Avignon
content:
La prison est-elle vraiment la réponse ?


Et si on imaginait autre chose ?


📅 Du 17 au 27 septembre 2026 📍 Avignon


Le collectif Crève la Taule 84 propose une série de rencontres, discussions et événements pour questionner la prison, ses effets et la société qui la produit.


Que vous soyez proches de personnes incarcérées, déjà engagé·es sur ces questions, ou simplement curieux·ses d'en savoir plus, venez découvrir d'autres façons de penser la justice, les violences, la punition et le vivre-ensemble.


Parce que derrière les murs, il y a des vies, des familles et des questions qui nous concernent toutes et tous.


affiche2


prog


Dans le Vaucluse, Crève la taule 84 lutte contre la prison et contre la société qui l'engendre. Né il y a plus de vingt ans lors de la construction de la prison du Pontet, le collectif s'est remobilisé face au projet d'une nouvelle prison à Entraigues-sur-la-Sorgue.


Il soutient les proches de prisonnier·es, notamment à travers l'émission V'la la Gamelle sur Radio Aïoli, et organise des temps de réflexion sur l'abolition des prisons.


En France, la population détenue a augmenté de 139 % depuis 1980, atteignant 86 100 personnes en janvier 2026. Surpopulation, insalubrité, violences, maladies et suicides marquent le quotidien carcéral.


Malgré les condamnations répétées de la France par la justice européenne, l'État continue de construire des prisons et de durcir sa politique pénale. La prison punit, désocialise, détruit des liens et frappe en priorité les personnes les plus précaires et marginalisées.


Loin de réduire les violences, l'enfermement peut les aggraver et favoriser la récidive. Alors pourquoi continuons-nous à croire qu'il nous protège ?


Parce que l'insécurité est devenue un outil politique : on désigne des menaces, on construit des ennemis et on présente la punition comme une évidence. On transforme ainsi des problèmes sociaux en responsabilités individuelles.


Crève la taule 84 refuse cette logique. Nous ne voulons pas répondre à la haine par la cage, la matraque et l'humiliation, mais par la solidarité, l'organisation et les idées.


Nous sommes abolitionnistes parce que nous refusons la domination et la violence institutionnelle. L'abolition n'est pas un rêve : c'est la nécessité d'imaginer et de construire d'autres façons de prévenir les violences, de réparer les torts et de vivre ensemble.


La prison est inutile et néfaste.


L'insécurité imaginaire.


La révolution possible.


L'abolition nécessaire.


crevelataule84@riseup.net

content:

Le jeudi 14 mai, 8 personnes bloquent un pont névralgique de Valence avec une banderole

A l'avenir on zieutera sur la table si y'a pas une caméra qui est déjà en train de filmer avant de s'assoir pour une audition.

Par la suite,

 Si ce service mystère prend la peine d'utiliser le conditionnel dans son

A partir de là, en plus des numéros abritaires initiaux (

Après 36h de

GAV

 et avant le déferrement du vendredi soir, 1 personne (faussement) reconnue par les renseignements et la 7

e

 personne silencieuse donnent finalement leurs vraies identités

. Le parquet requiert le placement en détention provisoire des 8 interpellés (pour une banderole), et la Juge de la Détention et des Libertés le suit pour les 5 qui n'ont pas confirmé leur identité et place en contrôle judiciaire les 3 autres (couvre feu, interdiction de paraitre à Valence où certaines travaillent,etc).

 Les 5 passeront 3 nuits en maison d'arrêt avant leur comparution immédiate (

author: Sav Jonsa
title: Manitoba officers charged in just 2% of all police-involved deaths since 2015
content:
This is the first part in a series focused on the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba. Stay tuned for part two.


The police watchdog responsible for investigating all officer-involved deaths in Manitoba has never met its mandate of accountability, transparency and independence, says a man who helped establish it more than a decade ago.


A months-long IJF [Investigative Journalism Foundation] probe into its history found the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba, or IIU, has charged Manitoba police officers in only two per cent of all police-involved deaths since becoming active in 2015. As well, the IIU hasn’t publicly released annual reports for the last three fiscal years, its website is often inaccessible to the public and the IIU has been operating without a permanent civilian director since late 2024.


The information is frustrating for Robert Taman, who believed police accountability was headed in the “right direction” when he first helped establish the IIU in the early 2010s. It was created by the province after

police botched the 2005 investigation into his wife Crystal’s death

 in a crash with an off-duty officer.


Crystal Taman, a 40-year-old Métis woman and mother of three children, was known as the ‘heart of the family.’ Photo: Taman Inquiry.


Now 11 years since its launch, Taman saidys he sees a lack of transparency and independence at the IIU, which is “completely against what it was meant to be.”


“I don’t think they’ve ever met their mandate,” said Taman. “I believe that everybody’s intentions are correct and they’re all trying to do the right thing, but in the end it’s like they get to a certain point and they can’t go any further.”


Taman’s skepticism of the IIU has also been shared by many

Indigenous community members and advocacy organizations

 in Manitoba after the IIU declined charging officers in several death investigations of First Nations people, notably in the cases of

Eishia Hudson

, 16,

Janine Walker

, 23,

James Wood

, 35,

John Ettawakapow

, 54,

Tammy Bateman

, 39, and

Elias Whitehead

, 37, to name just a few.


Whitehead died after his arrest in 2023 by the Winnipeg Police Service, who were responding to a call about a man “acting erratically in traffic” near the city’s downtown.


Whitehead was unarmed.


The

IIU’s final report for his death investigation

 states that during his arrest, officers punched Whitehead approximately 23 times in the head and body and delivered three knee strikes to his body. The autopsy found his cause of death to be “subdual and prone restraint (by police officers) complicating cocaine intoxication and cardiomegaly (enlarged heart).”


His common-law wife, Jody Beardy, told the IJF that officers not being charged in his death “didn’t make sense.”


“The IIU … I don’t know what their point is when they do not hold [police] responsible for what they did, what they do,” said Beardy, who had to wait more than two years after Whitehead’s death to learn no charges would be laid through the investigation.


Elias Whitehead is pictured here with his common-law wife, Jody Beardy. She posted several photos of Whitehead soon after he died in police-custody, saying that her ‘heart is completely broken’ and that she now has to ‘live in this world alone without the love of my life!’ Photo courtesy Jody Beardy.


According to its website, the IIU’s mandate ensures accountability, independence, objectivity, high investigative standards, timeliness, thoroughness and transparency in its investigations. Police must notify the IIU whenever there is an incident it may need to investigate. They do not take public complaints.


The IJF examined about 1,000 publicly available IIU documents, including news releases, annual reports and final reports, to find trends in their investigations, which include all death, serious injury and criminal allegations against officers for every police service in Manitoba including the RCMP, municipal police and First Nations police forces.


Since annual reports summarizing IIU investigations were not available for the last three years, the IJF had to pull data from close to 350 individual news releases from April 2023 onward.


There may be information not shared publicly by the IIU that the IJF was unable to record.


The IJF’s research found police officers have been charged in only two out of roughly 100 concluded death investigations since the IIU’s inception, according to published annual reports and news …

title: Συγκέντρωση για τη δίκη των βασανιστών του Β. Μάγγου, Παρασκευή 4/9, στις 09.00, στα Δικαστήρια Καρδίτσας
content:
“Στις 4 Σεπτέμβρη, στις 09.00, αναμένεται να συνεχιστεί στο μικτό ορκωτό εφετείο Καρδίτσας η δίκη των 6 ένστολων βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου σε βαθμό κακουργήματος […] Θα ακολουθήσει η κατάθεση 6 ακόμη μαρτύρων κατηγορίας των βασανιστών του Βασίλη, η εξέταση γιατρών καθώς και μαρτύρων υπεράσπισης, στην πλειοψηφία τους αστυνομικών, συναδέλφων των κατηγορούμενων βασανιστών.[…] Οι επόμενες δικάσιμες ορίστηκαν για τις 7, 10 και 17 Σεπτέμβρη […] Όλες/οι την Παρασκευή 04/09 στις 09:00 στα δικαστήρια της Καρδίτσας.”


Καλέσματα:


Δίκτυο αλληλεγγύης και αγώνα Καρδίτσας – Για υγεία, ζωή και ελευθερία


ΟΛΟΙ ΚΑΙ ΟΛΕΣ ΣΤΙΣ ΣΥΓΚΕΝΤΡΩΣΕΙΣ:


• ΚΕΝΤΡΙΚΗ ΠΛΑΤΕΙΑ, 2 ΣΕΠΤΕΜΒΡΗ, 20:00


• ΔΙΚΑΣΤΗΡΙΑ ΚΑΡΔΙΤΣΑΣ, 4 ΣΕΠΤΕΜΒΡΗ, 09:00


ΝΑ ΚΑΤΑΔΙΚΑΣΤΟΥΝ ΟΙ 6 ΒΑΣΑΝΙΣΤΕΣ ΤΟΥ Β. ΜΑΓΓΟΥ


Στις 4 Σεπτέμβρη αναμένεται να συνεχιστεί στο μικτό ορκωτό εφετείο Καρδίτσας η δίκη των 6 μπάτσων βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου σε βαθμό κακουργήματος.


Στις 13 Ιούνη 2020, στη μεγάλη κινητοποίηση ενάντια στην καύση σκουπιδιών στο εργοστάσιο της ΑΓΕΤ-Lafarge, η αστυνομία εξαπέλυσε μια από τις πιο βίαιες επιχειρήσεις καταστολής, τραυματίζοντας δεκάδες ανθρώπους και στοχοποιώντας το κίνημα που απαιτούσε καθαρό αέρα και αξιοπρέπεια για την πόλη του Βόλου. Στο ίδιο ακριβώς πλαίσιο, την επόμενη μέρα, εξελίχθηκε ο δολοφονικός βασανισμός του αγωνιστή Βασίλη Μάγγου, έξω από τα δικαστήρια Βόλου και στη συνέχεια μέσα στο κολαστήριο της Ασφάλειας Μαγνησίας. Είναι ξεκάθαρο ότι ο βασανισμός και εν τέλει η κρατική δολοφονία του Βασίλη, ενός ανθρώπου που στοχοποιήθηκε επειδή στάθηκε αλύγιστος απέναντι στα συμφέροντα κράτους και επενδυτών, αποτελούν τις πιο ακραίες εκφάνσεις ενός συστημικού σχεδίου καταστολής. Ένα σχέδιο που αποσκοπεί στην υπονόμευση και τη διάλυση των κοινωνικών και ταξικών αντιστάσεων, ώστε να διευκολυνθεί η επιβολή καταστροφικών επενδυτικών σχεδίων και αντικοινωνικών πολιτικών σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα. Η δικαστική μάχη που δίνεται στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο Καρδίτσας αποτελεί πλέον ένα κεντρικό πεδίο αναμέτρησης του κινήματος με τους μηχανισμούς της συγκάλυψης.


Στις 17 Ιουλίου διεξήχθη η τελευταία δικάσιμος για το καλοκαίρι όσον αφορά τη δίκη των έξι αστυνομικών που κατηγορούνται για βασανιστήρια σε βαθμό κακουργήματος. Οι επόμενες δικάσιμες έχουν οριστεί για τις 4, 7, 10 και 17 Σεπτέμβρη. Στο επόμενο διάστημα αναμένεται η κατάθεση ακόμη έξι μαρτύρων κατηγορίας και η εξέταση γιατρών, ενώ θα ακολουθήσουν οι μάρτυρες υπεράσπισης, στην πλειοψηφία τους συνάδελφοι των κατηγορούμενων ένστολων. Παράλληλα, στις 16 Σεπτέμβρη έχει οριστεί το εφετείο για τους τρεις αστυνομικούς της ΟΠΚΕ που καταδικάστηκαν σε βαθμό πλημμελήματος τον Φλεβάρη του 2025. Μέσα στη δικαστική αίθουσα, η πλευρά της υπεράσπισης των αστυνομικών έχει επιστρατεύσει την πιο χυδαία και προκλητική στάση, επιβεβαιώνοντας τον ρόλο της ως μηχανισμός ξεπλύματος της κρατικής βίας. Οι συνήγοροι των βασανιστών επιτίθενται αναίσχυντα στη μνήμη του ίδιου του Βασίλη, επιχειρώντας να αντιστρέψουν την πραγματικότητα, να τον συκοφαντήσουν μετά θάνατον και να μετατρέψουν το θύμα σε θύτη. Η στάση τους απέναντι στους χαροκαμένους γονείς, είναι γεμάτη ασέβεια, ειρωνεία και προσπάθεια ψυχολογικής εξόντωσης, προσβάλλοντας καθημερινά το πένθος και την αξιοπρέπειά τους. Ταυτόχρονα, οι δικηγόροι των αστυνομικών επιδεικνύουν μια απαράδεκτη και πιεστική συμπεριφορά απέναντι στην ίδια την έδρα, επιχειρώντας να τρομοκρατήσουν το δικαστήριο, να καθυστερήσουν τη διαδικασία με δικονομικά τερτίπια και να επιβάλουν ένα καθεστώς ιδιότυπης ασυλίας για τους πελάτες τους. Αυτή η μεθόδευση έρχεται σε συνέχεια της προκλητικής απόφασης του δικαστηρίου τον Απρίλιο του 2026, το οποίο απέρριψε το αίτημα της οικογένειας για παράσταση προς υποστήριξη της κατηγορίας με το πρόσχημα ότι ο Βασίλης, εξαιτίας των βαρύτατων τραυμάτων του, δεν πρόλαβε να καταθέσει μήνυση πριν πεθάνει. Παρά τα συντριπτικά στοιχεία από μαρτυρίες, ιατρικά ευρήματα και τρεις εκθέσεις του Συνηγόρου του Πολίτη, το κράτος επιχειρεί να αφήσει την οικογένεια χωρίς «φωνή» μέσα στην αίθουσα. Στις 7.4.2026 η εισαγγελέας Πρωτοδικών Καρδίτσας ανέγνωσε το κατηγορητήριο, περιγράφοντας με ανατριχιαστικές λεπτομέρειες πώς οι κατηγορούμενοι υπέβαλαν σε βασανιστήρια τον Βασίλη ενώ ήταν ακινητοποιημένος και δεμένος πισθάγκωνα, πώς προσέβαλαν την ανθρώπινη αξιοπρέπειά του με ομοφοβικά σχόλια, πώς του αρνήθηκαν νερό και ιατρική περίθαλψη, οδηγώντας τον σε καθεστώς παράνομης κατακράτησης.


Η υπόθεση του βασανισμού και της κρατικής δολοφονίας του Βασίλη Μάγγου δεν είναι μια ατομική …

author: Sabot Media
title: A Network Called Resistance: An Interview with Autistici/Inventati
content:
Originally Published 8/31/26 – 3:23PM PST


Updated Institutional Responses 8/31/26 – 6:35PM PST


Updated Banca Etica Statement 9/01/26 – 3:02AM PST


Editor’s note


This interview was conducted in writing with Autistici/Inventati following its August 26, 2026 designation by the United States under Executive Order 13224.


Sabot Media is an independent publication. We are not affiliated with A/I, do not represent the collective and did not conduct this interview at its direction. We are not fundraising for A/I, transmitting donations, providing technical or other services, mirroring its infrastructure, operating replacement services or archiving Noblogs material.


The interview has been edited only for spelling, punctuation, formatting and clarity. Any substantive condensation or reordering is identified. Links and brief explanatory context added by the editors appear in brackets. A/I was given the opportunity to review its own words for factual accuracy; it did not exercise editorial control over our introduction, reporting, questions or conclusions.


Statements by A/I represent the collective’s position. Claims concerning third parties are attributed accordingly and should not be read as independently verified unless our accompanying reporting says otherwise.


We sent separate questions to Public Interest Registry, Banca Etica, PayPal, The US Treasury Department and The US State Department. Their responses, where received, and their status as of publication appear below and will be updated as needed.


Interview with Autistici/Inventati


Immediate response and consequences


1. When and how did A/I first learn about the U.S. designation, and how did the collective initially respond?


A/I response:


We first learned about the designation via a tweet on Marco Rubio’s X account. We then did a bit of digging on the Treasury and State Department websites and eventually found the official announcements. The first thing we did was write a short statement to counter the allegations and start spreading it as widely as possible.


Then we had to check whether we had any assets in the United States, and we set about moving everything to different jurisdictions. We did not think PIR would act so swiftly, so we focused on domain registrars—we still had some things with a U.S.-based registrar—and PayPal. Apart from that, we thought we would be rather safe.


Then we had to answer hundreds of emails and interview requests, set up a coordinated response plan, and find lawyers as well as a press office. None of this proved quick to do, and we are still trying to juggle everything.


2. Since the designation, what consequences have already materialized—financially, technologically, institutionally or socially?


A/I response:


Our PayPal account has been closed for good, and we have been notified about it. To explain its decision, PayPal mentioned the designation of A/I by the U.S. authorities in the email it sent two days after terminating our account.


Autistici.org is also gone for good, and nobody felt the need to notify us. Our bank account is still active at the moment, but today is Sunday, August 30, and bank offices in Italy are closed. We sent an official legal warning to the bank not to close the account, and we have a call with the bank and our lawyers on Monday, August 31. We will see whether it has decided to reconsider its decision.


3. Have you seen banks, technology companies, hosting providers or other institutions over-comply by taking actions beyond what the sanctions clearly require?


Yes. Banca Etica’s reported decision to close our account illustrates how de-risking operates. The United States did not need to issue a direct order to the bank, and it has not been established that Italian law requires the relationship to be terminated. The bank can decide that maintaining the relationship creates too much legal, financial or reputational risk because our OFAC entry carries a secondary-sanctions warning.


We believe something similar occurred with our domain, although the exact chain of responsibility has not yet been publicly established. We attribute the intervention to PIR, but PIR has not publicly stated why it acted or whether OFAC instructed it to do so.


This is one of the central dangers of the designation. The United States does not need to order every company individually to abandon us. It can create enough uncertainty and fear that institutions impose the isolation themselves.

author: Betty Gedlu
title: Court Rules Against Citizen Journalists in DMCA Takedown Case—EFF Will Appeal
content:
A federal court in Massachusetts has ruled that copyright holders can issue online takedown notices based on a subjective belief of copyright infringement, even when that belief is unreasonable and self-serving. The case was brought by our client, Channel 781 News, after takedown notices temporarily shut down the citizen journalism group's YouTube channel. We think the court set the bar far too low for copyright takedowns, and we plan to appeal.

Channel 781 is a group of independent, volunteer journalists who report on local affairs in Waltham, Massachusetts. That includes posting short, newsworthy excerpts from recordings of city government meetings produced by Waltham Community Access Corporation (WCAC), the city's public access television station.

In September 2023, WCAC sent three copyright takedown notices to YouTube targeting fifteen of Channel 781's videos. YouTube removed the videos and, under its three-strikes policy, temporarily disabled Channel 781's entire account—just days before a local election.

Represented by EFF and Brown Rudnick LLP, Channel 781 sued WCAC under Section 512(f) of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), which provides a remedy when a copyright holder knowingly makes material misrepresentations in a takedown notice.

Fair use is the legal right to use copyrighted material without permission, when doing so serves purposes like criticism, commentary, or creating something new. Fair use is not copyright infringement, and courts have recognized that copyright holders must consider fair use before using the DMCA's powerful notice-and-takedown process.

In this case, Channel 781 argued that WCAC accused it of copyright infringement without making a good-faith assessment of whether its videos were fair use.

The evidence showed that WCAC's analysis was seriously deficient. The court noted that Chris Wangler, the WCAC employee who sent the notices, didn’t consider several facts relevant to fair use. For instance, Channel 781 used relatively small portions of WCAC's recordings, and the underlying recordings were factual public meetings, not a creative work. WCAC also gave little or no weight to whether Channel 781's use harmed any market for the recordings.

There’s also strong evidence that WCAC had motivations unrelated to copyright. WCAC objected to its footage being used to criticize local officials and advance political viewpoints. And WCAC sent the takedown notices during a local election, shortly after Channel 781 posted a campaign statement by Waltham's mayor that WCAC had mistakenly made available online.

Despite this evidence, the court concluded that WCAC had a subjective good-faith belief that Channel 781's videos were infringing. We disagree.

Channel 781 argued that a copyright holder’s belief that material is infringing must be both genuinely held and objectively reasonable. WCAC argued that a subjective good-faith belief is good enough. Unfortunately, the court agreed with WCAC.

The court emphasized that Wangler had read up on fair use, watched a short YouTube video explaining the doctrine, and distinguished between videos he thought might qualify as fair use and those he believed did not. That was enough, the court concluded, to establish subjective good faith—even though Wangler’s analysis ignored important facts relevant to fair use. As the court put it, Section 512(f) does not require “a perfect or even reasonable fair use analysis.”

That is an alarmingly low bar for copyright holders seeking to remove someone else’s speech from the internet. A DMCA takedown can cause lawful speech to disappear almost immediately. As Channel 781 experienced, multiple notices can even result in an entire channel being disabled.

If a copyright holder can avoid liability despite a cursory, incomplete, and objectively unreasonable analysis that ignores important facts—even when there’s evidence that the copyright holder wanted to suppress critical speech—the obligation to consider fair use risks becoming little more than a box-checking exercise. That interpretation threatens to strip Section 512(f) of much of its force.

Even accepting the court’s subjective standard, WCAC's cursory consideration of fair use should not have been enough. WCAC disregarded important fair use considerations, and the record included statements suggesting that it believed people generally needed permission to reuse its footage—an understanding at odds with fair use. author: Brian Dolinar
title: It’s Not Just Flock. Police Can’t Be Trusted With Our Data.
content:
An Illinois State Police database available online listed personal information, including Social Security numbers.

An Illinois State Police database available online listed personal information, including Social Security numbers.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A growing movement has been campaigning against surveillance cameras from companies like Flock Safety, which allow local police to gather mass surveillance data, often citing the possibility of misuse of that data. But for years police have steadily been building a digital infrastructure with personal information on people with criminal backgrounds in the name of public safety — and often without proper digital security

Since 2020, the state police in Illinois have maintained a publicly accessible online map of 30,000 people that it has labeled as “offenders” in 685 nursing homes across the state. The map included the first and last names, dates of birth, home addresses, phone numbers, FBI numbers, and Social Security numbers of people listed. These are elderly people who are vulnerable to scammers. It’s not stated what they have been convicted of. They may have a drug charge from decades ago before marijuana was legalized in Illinois, but their past still follows them.

Matt Chapman, a researcher with the Chicago-based Lucy Parsons Labs, stumbled across the map when he was researching license plate readers maintained by the Illinois State Police (ISP). “Anybody can find this,” Chapman told Truthout. “Anybody can use this for nefarious purposes.”

“Why do these agencies have all this information?” Chapman questioned. “Why are they not protecting it? It really speaks to the lack of care that Illinois State Police have for the information of sensitive folks — the people they’re supposedly supposed to protect.”

As police build an increasingly sophisticated surveillance apparatus, they have been shown to be poor stewards of the mass amounts of information they collect on the public. Police have also wrongly entered people into gang databases. In 2020, a scandal erupted in Los Angeles after cops there falsified records in a gang database, which led to the suspension of several officers with the city’s police department. Last year, Kilmar Abrego Garcia was sent to CECOT, the mega-prison in El Salvador, after Immigration and Customs Enforcement accessed information from a disgraced Maryland cop who put him into a gang database linking him to M-13 for wearing a hoodie and Chicago Bulls baseball cap.

In 2021, Protocol, a company owned by BI Incorporated (a subsidiary of the private prison builder GEO Group), which supplies the Cook County Sheriff’s Office with electronic monitors, leaked the personal information of thousands of people across Chicago wearing the devices, what expert James Kilgore calls “ankle shackles.” Chapman, who also uncovered this data leak, said it included “an enormous amount of private information,” such as names, email and home addresses, and the “detailed movement schedules” of people on these digital tracking devices.

“Any scammer could have an absolute field day with this data.”

States have been expanding the use of registries to track individuals — most commonly people convicted of sexual offenses, but also those found guilty of murder, arson, methamphetamine production, and other crimes. In Kansas City, a multi-jurisdictional police operation recently rounded up nearly 100 people on the state sex offender registry who were living within 1,000 feet of a school, which is a violation. Police claimed they were protecting children heading back to school. Thirty years after they were first established, research shows there is little proof that registries make people safer.

Last year, a company that sells an app to monitor the phones of people convicted of sex offenses had the information publicly leaked in what a hacker called “one of the easiest” breaches they had ever done.

The map of 30,000 names, which the Illinois State Police took down after being notified about it by Truthout, was an interactive map of nursing homes across the state. author: EDRi
title: EDRi stands in solidarity with Autistici/Inventati after “terrorist” designation by the US government
content:
The United States government has designated the Italian non-profit organisation Autistici/Inventati as a "Specially Designated Global Terrorist" for providing digital infrastructure to supposedly “violent far-left militants.” This targeting of A/I is also an attack on independent internet infrastructure, fundamental rights of multiple collectives, safe and secure communications, democratic anti-authoritarian organising and the democratic integrity of the EU.

On 26 August, the United States government designated the Italian non-profit organisation Autistici/Inventati (A/I) as a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” for providing digital infrastructure to supposedly “violent far-left militants.” This targeting of A/I is also an attack on independent internet infrastructure, fundamental rights of multiple collectives, safe and secure communications, democratic anti-authoritarian organising and the democratic integrity of the EU.

As the largest digital rights network in Europe, EDRi stands in full solidarity with Autistici/Inventati.

A/I is a volunteer-run collective that has been operating from Italy since 2001, providing services like email, mailing lists, hosting blog, and other services related to privacy and anonymity to associations, community groups and people across Europe and worldwide. Importantly, it is an anti-fascist, anti-racist, anti-sexist and anti-militarist organisation opposed to capitalism and authoritarianism, and they only host projects that are compatible with these principles.

A/I’s services are decentralised, not-for-profit, and offer security from surveillance of law enforcement and state overreach. This safe and secure communications infrastructure is a critical alternative to Big Tech platforms and used widely for anti-fascist organising and grassroots social movements, which are already under pressure due to rising authoritarianism globally.

The impact of the designation was felt immediately: A/I’s website is not longer accessible because the US-based Public Interest Registry disabled their domain “autistici.org”. Paypal has seized their account, and the Italian ‘Banca Etica’ might, out of fear of secondary sanctions, close their account, despite the bank’s commitment to human rights.

The obligation imposed on US companies to sever all economic ties with A/I also risks having consequences far beyond the United States. Non-US banks and financial institutions are likely to terminate their relationships with A/I out of concern about potential US secondary sanctions or other regulatory risks. As a result, A/I could effectively become an outcast, losing access to essential services and facing significant difficulties in carrying out its day-to-day operations.

The effect of this designation will not be limited to A/I or those directly using their infrastructure. It speaks to an escalation of massive, institutional attacks on safe and secure communication, alternatives to for-profit Big Tech platforms, democratic organising, and more, which will be felt by the digital rights community and the wider civil society.

Concretely, the US attack against A/I threatens:

The freedoms of expression, information, assembly and association: A/I’s services are used by a multitude of collectives, campaigners, trade unionists, journalists, researchers, many of whom chose A/I because their work was unsafe or shunned on commercial platforms. Currently, A/I hosts 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists, and 10,000 blogs. Not only does attempting to cut off their communications and archives, without due process, undermines Articles 7, 11 and 12 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights, it also puts at risk the important work being done by thousands of organisations and collectives. The target is clearly not just A/I but the wider ecosystem and community they support. These users will not be sanctioned directly but the association with A/I will affect how banks scrutinise their payments, how ‘risky’ they are deemed by researchers and journalists, how ‘suspicious’ they come across while crossing borders – a broad chilling effect delivered through one targeted designation. If independent and secure providers like A/I continue to be attacked, collectives and organisations might be forced to move to commercial Big Tech platforms, exposing them to supercharged levels of surveillance and censorship.

title: Rachel-Rose O’Leary - Lunarpunk and the Dark Side of the Cycle
content:
Author

: Rachel-Rose O’Leary

Title

: Lunarpunk and the Dark Side of the Cycle

Date

: 2022

Source

: Retrieved on 8

th

 July 2026 from

https://heterarchy.fyi/cs/texty/lunarpunk-dark-side-of-the-cycle


 Forward


 A lunarpunk manifesto disguised as market analysis. The essay argues that solarpunk’s optimism and transparency are structural fragilities — when regulatory pressure mounts, transparent systems expose their users and collapse. anonymous-communication and encryption are not optional extras but the precondition for crypto’s antifragility.


 Science fiction is a speculative exercise. By speculating on possible futures, sci-fi expands the space of possibilities. Crypto is an extreme kind of sci-fi because as well as offering a vision of the future it also provides the tools to make that future possible.


 Crypto is currently energized by a sci-fi called solarpunk. Evolved from cyberpunk, solarpunk is a utopian vision of the future characterized by its optimism. For solarpunks, the future is bright. Solarpunk casts away the dystopian shadows of cyberpunk and illuminates a world beyond the chaotic horizon.


 In Ethereum, solarpunk hackers are creating transparent infrastructures for funding public goods. The imaginary here is simple: decentralization and transparency will lead to a fairer and more just world. Web 3 is creating a new path for humanity, which old institutions will inevitably follow.


 Solarpunk is crypto’s conscious mind. It is bright, self-confident, and future-oriented. Yet the counterpart to solarpunk faith is lunarpunk skepticism. Lunarpunks are the solar shadow-self. They are the unconscious of this cycle. While “solarpunks join DAOs” (Dylan-Ennis), lunarpunks are preparing for war, and building privacy-enhanced tooling to protect their communities.


 Lunarpunk first came into being as a subset of solarpunk. It has always preferred encryption over the plaintext paradigm offered by Ethereum. Overtime, the tensions created by solarpunk tendencies have only multiplied. Lunarpunk is forced to break away from the solarpunk legacy and assert its own.


Lunarpunk squad


 In the lunarpunk imaginary, a conflict between crypto and existing power structures is essentially preprogrammed. Regulation forces crypto underground. Anonymity proliferates. In the interstellar darkness, freshly radicalized crypto factions create a new kind of democratic society.


 This conflict is repressed in solarpunk psychology. The lunar cycle is rejected as a bearish nightmare. Its foundational conflict: nation-state’s banning crypto — is called FUD because it produces fear, the kind of fear that compels people to grab their money and run.


 As the supercycle segments, solarpunk repression is mounting. The optimism of solarpunk has become synonymous with bull market cycles, while pessimism is associated with the bear. Lunarpunk offers something beyond this simple oscillation. It is a moment of insight between market cycles, a glitch in the hologram where the source code shines through. Solarpunk fragility


 Fragile is something that breaks when shaken. Antifragile is something that absorbs shocks and becomes stronger.


 The fate of antifragility follows a convex curve, while fragility is concave.


Fragile vs antifragile


 The antifragility of crypto has been repeatedly emphasized. Yet crypto today exists on a fragility spectrum. The extent of its resilience will only be demonstrated when under sufficient external pressure. If crypto’s defenses hold, convexity is its fate. Otherwise we will see a race to the bottom, concave-style.


 Consider the following. Crypto’s core innovation is a diptych — it empowers users while diffusing its attack surface (in equal proportion). User empowerment is negatively correlated with fragility; the more empowered a user base, the more antifragile a network becomes.


Empowerment and antifragility


 User-empowerment and system-antifragility are in positive feedback with each other. But this cycle also runs in reverse. In a transparent system, users are exposed. If the external environment turns hostile, this information can be weaponized against them. Faced with persecution, users will opt-out, triggering a descent into fragility.


Fragility


 The solarpunk mindset is essentially optimistic. Transparency in solarpunk systems is the spirit of optimism projected outward. By building transparent systems, the solarpunk says: I have faith that the law won’t turn against me …

author: Lillian Kollross
title: Helpful or Hurtful? The Growing Privacy Debate Over Meta Glasses
content:
As AI becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life, smart glasses have emerged as one of the newest technologies raising questions about privacy and consent. This week, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) reportedly banned employees from wearing Meta smart glasses over privacy concerns.

Dubbed “pervert glasses,” Meta glasses are wearable computers, allowing users to take photos and videos, access artificial intelligence, and use other digital features without holding a phone. But unlike a traditional camera, smart glasses can make it difficult for others to know when they are being recorded.

Those concerns have become particularly apparent in incidents involving women. In California, a doctor was caught wearing Meta glasses while examining a female patient who had recently undergone a breast lift. In another incident, a TikToker used Meta glasses to film himself harassing comedian Diane Morgan while she was filming on the Hollywood Walk of Fame for her fictional documentary series Cunk on Earth.

Videos recorded with smart glasses have also become increasingly common on social media, including content in which users approach, flirt with, or harass strangers without their knowledge or consent. Instagram promised to crack down and remove these kinds of harmful videos, but no such action has been taken.

The backlash has extended beyond social media. Influencers who publicly post footage recorded with smart glasses have faced criticism and hate comments. When cyclist influencer Oliver Hooson posted a biking video filmed using Meta glasses, he lost dozens of followers and was called a “perv” in his comment section.

Even Meta’s high-profile celebrity partnerships have drawn attention to the controversy. Reality TV star Kylie Jenner recently partnered with Meta to promote a line of smart glasses, prompting criticism from users concerned about the technology’s potential for surveillance.

The British advocacy group Everyone Hates Elon went further, creating fake advertisements with an X-ray skeleton of Jenner with the slogan, “We’re Always Watching.” The same advocacy group also took shots at Meta with an ad that featured a photo of child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein wearing Meta glasses with the text “Glasses for people who don’t do consent.”

Courts and governments are beginning to respond as well. Last month, the New York State Court System banned smart glasses. A month later, England and Wales followed suit and also banned all smart glasses from their courts. In Germany, an advocacy group has also filed a criminal complaint against Meta related to the glasses.

This came after Meta filed a patent application for AI-powered facial recognition software for their smart glasses. The software would automatically capture people’s faces and convert them into biometric data without their consent.

At the same time, smart glasses have meaningful benefits that should not be overlooked. For those who are blind or visually impaired, the glasses help with reading, identifying objects, and accessing information from the internet. When users visit a new country or start a conversation with someone who speaks a different language, the glasses include a live translation feature.

While these features are beneficial to some, the perverts and creeps of the world are ruining it for the rest of us. As AI becomes a larger part of our daily lives, we must find a way to protect the privacy and safety of women and girls.

author: groundxero
title: The Next Election May be Our Last
content:
Donald Trump is determined to subvert the midterms. All that can save us, if he succeeds, is a national strike.


 


CHRIS HEDGES


Aug 31, 2026


 


The Trump White House has put into place a series of mechanisms to fix or invalidate the midterm elections. Congress will not save us. The courts will not save us. Our only hope — should the election be rigged or stolen — is nationwide strikes. Our only hope is to cripple the machinery of commerce and government, although this militancy will be met with savage state repression.


 


Otherwise, we are doomed. There will be no exit.


 


If the measures advocated by the Trump administration are implemented, 

emergency powers

 will be invoked to assert unprecedented federal control over voting. Federal agents will seize election materials. They have already 

seized

 ballots from previous elections.


 


The U.S. Postal Service will only send ballots to those 

included

 on federally approved eligibility lists drawn from state voter rolls. These rolls, subject to citizenship checks, will 

deny

 election-mail services entirely in states that 

refuse

 the administration’s demands for voter data.


 


Trump-

backed

 mid-decade 

gerrymandering

 has already dismantled Democratic-held districts and created new ones for the Republican.


 


Federal ID and citizenship-document requirements will disenfranchise 

millions

 of eligible voters, including lower-income Americans who lack access to the required documents and married women whose current names do not match those on their citizenship records.


 


Federal troops and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) — with $113.5 billion in additional funding 

allocated

 by Congress through September 2029 — will be deployed to or near polling stations which have a traditional Democratic Party majority. Those branded as “anti-capitalist” and “anti-Christian” or charged with belonging to 

antifa

 will be intimidated or blocked from voting.


 


The Republican majority in the House — regardless of the vote — will use its authority to certify election results to retain power, gaming the Electoral College and refusing to seat newly elected members of the opposition.


 


Overseeing the massive election fraud will be 

loyalists

 seeded by the Trump administration across state and federal election offices.


 


Trump — who attempted to overturn the 2020 election results and said he would 

refuse

 to accept the outcome of the 2024 election if he lost — 

ruminates

 about defying the Constitution in order to serve a third term. He has also floated the idea of canceling the upcoming election, 

telling

 Reuters “when you think of it, we shouldn’t even have an election.”


 


When Volodymyr Zelensky — whose presidential term 

ended

 in May 2024 — informed Trump that elections would not be held in Ukraine because of the war, Trump

 

responded, “So you’re saying, during the war you can’t have elections…So, let me just say, three and a half years from now, so you mean if we happen to be in a war with somebody, no more elections? Oh, that’s good.”


 


Trump

 

told

 The New York Times in January he 

regretted

 not directing the National Guard to seize voting machines after the 2020 election. Trump not only wants to

 

abolish

 mail-in ballots – Democrats vote by mail in higher numbers than Republicans – but voting machines and tabulators which allow election boards to post results on election night.


 


Trump laid the groundwork for federal interference in his national address in July on election fraud, 

charging

 that the elections are dangerously exposed to “hacking, exploitation, and foreign interference.”


 


This assault has been decades in the making. It did not begin with Trump.


 


I warned about the Christian nationalist movement and its latent fascism in my book “

The only proper tasks for the federal government, they believe, are tax collection, war and domestic security.


 


These goals are laid out in numbing technical detail in 

Project 2025

.
