author: winter oak
title: An A-Z of the modern mega-racket
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


Art

 of the modern variety is concerned less with aesthetics than with accumulation. When the cabal owns the art critics, the media and the cultural institutions, artificial value can be ascribed to works endowed with neither beauty nor meaning. Their only meaning is in the making and laundering of money and, indeed, the deliberate destruction of meaning.


Banking

 is at the rotten core of the modern mega-racket. Creating money out of thin air and then lending it out at interest brings long-term control over society. This allows the racketeers to manufacture the “demand” for development, expansion, infrastructure, war and post-war reconstruction, which all require still further loans, still further usurious extraction of wealth from the host population. Usury is no longer regarded as an evil because the usurers, through their usury, have gradually gained control of governments, media, publishing houses, educational institutions and organised religions.


Culture

 from below is organically alive, but culture from above is a dead thing imposed on peoples to shape them according to the demands of the system. Before it can take hold of a population, this artificial culture has to destroy the rooted variety, declaring it defunct or dangerous. Modern culture is thus anti-culture, used as a tool of imperialist conquest and domination.


Development

 is a deliberately bland term describing the systematic pillage and exploitation of a people and its land in order to transfer its wealth into the hands of the imperial racketeers. Their control of government and institutions allows them to enshrine their theft in law as a fundamental, permanent and incontrovertible social and economic good.


Education

 is the formatting of young people’s minds so that their thinking corresponds to the requirements of the ruling gang. They must be trained to be able to perform certain tasks, sorted and sifted to find how they can best be exploited, trained to obedience and conformity, brainwashed with the gang’s version of history and reality and, crucially, accustomed to the unnatural and freedom-denying rhythms of slave life.


Food

 is used as a tool of control by the racket. A people with no land cannot feed itself and becomes dependent on the system for its food. To access this food, it has to work for the racket and earn its money. Those who grow the food for these exploited and landless wage-slaves are obliged to do so by high levels of taxation from the racketeers’ state, which forces them to work harder to produce surplus food simply in order to survive.


Growth

, in the financial sense, is the cancerous expansion of the parasitical tumour sucking the lifeblood out of humankind and our world, powered by the banking scam and taking the physical form of development. Real growth is about life, while economic growth spells death.


Health

 in a modern context refers to a lucrative business sector which profits from the unhealthy lifestyles, poor industrial diets, polluted environments and child-like dependent mentalities of most modern people. It also creates further demand for its products and services by means of those very products and services, which produce secondary and tertiary problems requiring more and more treatment.


Investment

 is a euphemistic term suggesting that it is positive and socially helpful to put money into something with the aim of later making a considerable profit. This profit does not come from nowhere, but is extracted from society by those who already have the money to invest. Investment is thus a disguised form of theft, robbing the majority to make the rich still richer.


Jobs

 are the slave roles that modern men and women are generally required to accept in order to be able to live and eat in a world which is no longer free but effectively owned by the racketeers. Whenever some new industrial abomination is launched in order to make more money, the gang announces that it must be a good thing because it will create more jobs – in other words, more lucrative exploitation of dispossessed, disempowered and landless human beings.


Kingdoms

, in the modern world, are just the same as republics, since behind the facades of monarchical or democratic control lies one and the same criminal gang, which in fact sees itself as the real and all-powerful global king. Nobody is allowed to criticise or mock this monarch or to question the lies with which he …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: City of Iqaluit recycling proposal sitting in limbo with Department of Finance
content:
Work to re-establish a beverage recycling program in Iqaluit seems to have stalled with the Nunavut government, after the city presented territorial officials with a feasibility study earlier this year.


Iqaluit residents lost the program in July 2025 after local business Northern Collectables discontinued the service. Iqaluit city council

passed a motion

 in December, asking administration to embark on a feasibility study for the municipality to take over the program.


The study analyzed adding a reverse vending machine and other container deposit options for the city, along with cost estimates.


The city then met with territorial officials, said city spokesperson Geoffrey Byrne, but can’t move forward without financial support.


“Council has been clear that any such program would need to be cost-neutral to the municipality,” he said in an email.


Nunatsiaq News asked the Finance Department what came of these talks but only received a statement from spokesperson Hala Duale that the department

“does not have plans to reintroduce a refundable container deposit program at this time.”


Derek Allerton, an Iqaluit resident who says he collected approximately 14,000 cans off the streets in the past year, said the Government of Nunavut’s response is frustrating.


“Tens of thousands of alcohol aluminum beverage cans litter the streets of Iqaluit, and millions of aluminum cans are going to landfill,” he said.


Some of these cans have made it to a fundraising bin managed by Aqsarniit middle school’s environmental club, which

started

 a beverage drop off this spring with help from the Department of Environment. But the club only accepts non-alcoholic beverage containers.


“In my personal experience, one in four cans littering the city are pop cans, and the rest are alcohol beverage cans,” Allerton said, adding the

 most popular brands he sees littering the streets are Molson Dry, Budweiser and Molson Canadian. 


The environmental club’s initiative is far from a solution, Allerton said. For many, it’s too far out of the way.


“There’s a lot of pop consumed in the city, so I think there could be easily multiple drop-off points for pop cans to be recycled,” Allerton said.


He added he was previously feeling hopeful 

about the prospects of the territorial government resolving the issue after Premier John Main wrote to him in June to assure him the city and territory were “actively working together” to resume a “successful long-term program.”


“The Government of Nunavut (GN) has received a proposal from the City of Iqaluit with several different program options and there is a group which has been meeting regularly to develop a city-led program,” Main wrote to Allerton in a letter dated June 22.


“As of today, there is no confirmed funding model or program structure, because the parties are still analyzing the different program options with their respective funding needs,” the premier wrote.


“We are committed to continuing our work with the city to develop a program with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.”


Main also shared with Allerton that the territory’s liquor commission is no longer collecting a waste management fee on alcoholic beverages until a “new solution” can be found.


Nunatsiaq News has reached out to the premier’s office to clarify his position on the funding of a new recycling program for the city but did not immediately hear back.


Nunavut’s Finance Department did not respond to follow up questions regarding whether it is committed to funding a program at some point in the future.

author: Unknown
title: 9,000-year-old mining workshop unearthed in Ergani
content:
Excavations carried out at Kotaberçem (Çayönü Mound) in the Ergani district of Amed (Diyarbakır) have uncovered a mining workshop of approximately 5 square meters, dating to 6900–6800 BCE. Raw and processed pieces of malachite, as well as copper objects, were found at the site. The excavations, wrote Mezopotamya Agency (MA), were led by Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University, and identified at least six postholes around the workshop, which was uncovered in the western part of the settlement, as well as a stone-paved work area at its center.


The postholes possibly indicate that the production area may have been covered with a canopy or shelter. Raw and semi-processed malachite, processed malachite samples, copper beads, and various copper objects were found in the workshop. Including finds from the center of the workshop and its immediate surroundings, the number of malachite and copper fragments identified across the wider excavation area has reportedly reached approximately 42.


Shedding light on the history of mining


The discovery of raw materials, semi-processed pieces, and finished products in the same area indicates that mining activities were carried out in an organized manner within a designated work area. Earlier evidence of the use of copper and malachite at Kotaberçem dates back as far as 9100 BCE. The new discovery is said to demonstrate that the region’s mining tradition developed and continued for approximately 2,000 years.


Located within the Ergani and Tigris River Basin, Kotaberçem is among the important settlements of the Neolithic period, with finds providing evidence of the development of settled life, agriculture, and animal husbandry.

author: Frederich Kirsten and Mduduzi Biyase
title: Why Lesotho’s remittance ‘safety net’ was never really its own, and why it is failing again in 2026
content:
Lesotho is two years into a national state of disaster: US tariffs have gutted its garment factories, unemployment has passed 30%, and its main trade lifeline is guaranteed for less than a year. To understand how the mountain kingdom keeps ending up here, start almost forty years earlier.In 1987, something extraordinary happened in this small kingdom, completely surrounded by South Africa. Money sent home by Basotho men working in South African gold mines reached

236% of Lesotho’s entire GDP

. Not 23%. Not 60%. More than double the value of everything the country itself produced in a year. Today, that figure sits at around a fifth of GDP. The money didn’t slow down gradually. It collapsed, and it has never recovered. To understand why, you have to understand what that money actually was.


A mountain village in Lesotho.


Why one country’s economy ran on someone else’s mines


For over a century, Lesotho had almost no domestic industry of its own. What it had instead was proximity: a small, mountainous, landlocked territory sitting right next to the richest goldfields on Earth. South African mining houses needed enormous numbers of workers willing to do dangerous, underground labour for low pay, and they built an entire recruitment system to draw men from Lesotho, in their hundreds of thousands, to fill that need.


This wasn’t diversification. It was concentration. An entire national economy came to depend not on a sector but on the hiring decisions of one industry, in one neighbouring country, that Lesotho had no ownership of and no influence over. The arrangement generated enormous sums of money. But it meant Lesotho’s prosperity was never really Lesotho’s to control. It belonged to the price of gold, the depth and cost of South African ore bodies, and the mining houses’ own calculations about profitability: decisions made in boardrooms far from Lesotho.


Why the mines emptied out


South Africa’s gold mining industry has been declining for decades. Ore grades have thinned, extraction has moved ever deeper and more expensive, and profitability has steadily eroded. Industry data shows gold mine employment falling from around

536,000 workers in the late 1980s to roughly 94,000 in 2023, a loss of more than 440,000 jobs

. What is far less well understood is when that decline first showed up on the ground in Lesotho. That is what our research set out to trace.


The illusion of insurance


Here is the idea we set out to test, in ongoing research that is not yet peer-reviewed: a common assumption in development economics holds that remittances act like insurance for vulnerable countries. When disaster strikes at home, such as a drought or a bad harvest, the theory goes, migrant workers send extra money to cushion their families. It appears again and again in World Bank reports and climate-adaptation policy documents. If it were true anywhere, it should have been true in Lesotho. So we tested it every way we could think of: immediate effects and delayed ones, good mining years and bad, average years and the very worst.


So far, we have found nothing. At no point did Lesotho’s own climate conditions appear to move the money flowing into the country. This work is ongoing. But that absence is the whole point. Real insurance responds to your shocks: your drought, your bad year. What Lesotho had was money that moved in response to conditions entirely outside its own borders. That isn’t insurance. It’s exposure to a risk you don’t control, wearing the appearance of a safety net.


What the sequence suggests, and what it does not prove


Our analysis cannot show that the mining industry’s decline directly caused Lesotho’s remittance collapse. Establishing causation from national data alone is genuinely difficult, and we want to be honest about that limit. What we can show is a sequence, dated using statistical tools that detect when a long-running trend breaks.


Net migration out of Lesotho reversed course in

1986

: families were already pulling back from the mines before anything else in the data moved. Just two years later, in

1988

, around the same time mine employment across the industry peaked before its long decline, Lesotho’s remittances began their long, uninterrupted fall. It would be a full decade, until

1998

, before international aid to Lesotho showed any measurable shift. That was also the year of Lesotho’s post-election crisis and SADC intervention, so donors may have been answering the political …

Shein und Co.: Frankreich erhebt Sondergebühr für Wegwerfmode


„

Zwölf Euro Abgabe pro Jacke, neun Euro für eine Jeans, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt: Frankreich will die Verbreitung von Billigmode mit Strafzahlungen einschränken. In den kommenden Jahren sollen sie noch weiter angehoben werden.


Eine Billigjacke eines Onlinehändlers wie Shein oder Temu kostet in Frankreich künftig bis zu zwölf Euro mehr. Die Regierung veröffentlichte am Freitag im Amtsblatt die neuen Regeln, die die Verbreitung sogenannter Wegwerfmode einschränken sollen und ab dem 1. September gelten. Im laufenden Jahr werden demnach auch 50 Cent für Unterhosen oder Socken, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt und neun Euro für Jeans fällig, die bestimmten Kriterien entsprechen. Frankreich wolle auf diese Weise gegen ein Geschäftsmodell vorgehen, »das darauf beruht, dass ein Kleidungsstück in Rekordzeit von der Ladenfläche in die Mülltonne wandert«, schrieb der Umweltstaatssekretär Mathieu Lefèvre im Onlinedienst X.


»Die schädlichen Auswirkungen der Ultra-Fast-Fashion auf unsere Umwelt und unsere Wirtschaft sind bekannt und dokumentiert«, fügte er hinzu. Die Kriterien sind so formuliert, dass sie in erster Linie asiatische Onlinehändler wie Shein und Temu treffen, nicht aber Ketten wie Zara, H&M oder Uniqlo, die in Frankreich Arbeitsplätze bieten. Entscheidend ist die Menge der Modelle, die auf den Markt gebracht werden, und deren Preis im Verhältnis zu einer Reparatur.


Anstieg programmiert


Die Strafzahlungen sollen bis 2030 ansteigen und dann etwa zwei Euro für Unterhosen und 19,50 Euro für eine Jacke erreichen. Das Geld soll in einen Fonds fließen, mit dem vorbildliche Unternehmen unterstützt werden sollen. Dazu sind bislang keine Details bekannt

…“

Mode und Interior inspirieren sich nicht immer nur im Guten. Nach Fast Fashion ist auch Fast Interior zum Problem geworden. author: Nayanika Guha
title: Yup’ik Immersion School Program in Alaska Opens Doors to Cultural Connection
content:
Other Indigenous groups are looking to the K-8 language immersion program in Anchorage, Alaska, as an inspiring model.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Growing up in Bethel, Alaska, Amber Arnaqulluk Shields spoke Yup’ik from a very young age. Whenever she wasn’t in school, her parents sent her to their ancestral home in Toksook Bay to spend time with grandparents who spoke no English.

Speaking Yu’pik at home had always been a priority for her family, and so when Shields had her kids, whom she is raising in Anchorage, Alaska, she wanted to give them the same access to her culture and family connections. Her son Kangrilnguq, a rising fifth grader who is the eldest of her three children, was raised speaking Yup’ik.

“We only speak Yup’ik in the house to our kids. My son actually didn’t really know much English by the time he was in kindergarten,” Shields told Truthout.

However, she started noticing that Kangrilnguq would shy away from playing with other kids at the park and not want to meet any other kids outside the family. She recalls a time when she was helping her relatives move, and there was a child her son’s age there whom she was encouraging him to play with, but he refused and ran away to hide in their truck. “I was like, ‘Hmm, I wonder why he’s not paying with the kids.’ And I asked that little girl [in Yup’ik], ‘Hey, could you go into the back of my truck and help me get that bag out?’ And he jumped out of the truck, and he asked me, ‘Does she understand? She speaks Yup’ik?’” That’s when he started playing with her, and when it clicked for Shields that he wasn’t playing with other kids because they weren’t understanding each other.

As a result, when Shields learned about the Yup’ik immersion program at College Gate Elementary School in Anchorage, it was a natural choice for her to send her children there. Her son started the program as a kindergartener in 2022, “and my hope was that he’ll be able to understand his teachers, and his teachers would be able to understand him,” Shields said.

The program at College Gate started in 2018, with support from a federal grant, to reinvigorate Indigenous languages. Each year since its inception, the school has successfully added a grade to the program, and the Anchorage school system is now adding an 8th grade class to the program at Wendler Middle School, with plans to add high school grades next year, too.

“Kids are fully immersed with the target language for half the day, and then they get their reading and math for the other half with an English partner teacher,” explained Darrell Berntsen, the principal at College Gate Elementary. “And so that happens daily, where they’re with one teacher for the start of the day, and then they move to another teacher to end the day.”

It’s not just the language that is taught, Berntsen said — the culture is taught also. “So it has really changed the culture of my school … and our school has kind of adopted their culture because we act like a big village here at the school.”

The program at College Gate started in 2018, with support from a federal grant, to reinvigorate Indigenous languages.

According to Shields, this has been especially important for her family, and her son specifically. Their family engages in many Yup’ik subsistence practices “even though we’re in Anchorage,” Shields explained, and now her son is “able to feel normal, I guess, because there’s other kids that do subsistence.” In the Yup’ik immersion program, he can also regularly interact with Yup’ik elders who teach in the program. She recalls a time when their family was going to Bethel and had plans to go ptarmigan hunting, and Kangrilnguq promised to bring a bird back as gift for his teacher. Another time, she recalls he wanted to go fishing so that he could bring back fish for his teachers. “He’s like, ‘she’s an elder, and I want to give her fish.’ So we were able to still practice giving to elders that way, and he really appreciates being able to understand his teachers, his teachers being able to understand him and who he is and where he comes from.”

Berntsen, who is Alutiiq from Kodiak Island, said he hopes that the school’s Yup’ik immersion program will have a lasting effect on the city, and “that they’ll be able to kind of revive the language and have more Indigenous speakers here in Anchorage.” In 2018, Anchorage Daily News …

author: Andrés
title: Contra el extractivismo y el despojo territorial, las Warmis marchan al Congreso
content:
Este jueves al mediodía, mujeres de pueblos originarios de Jujuy se movilizan desde Plaza Miserere hacia el Congreso de la Nación para exigir el cese del saqueo minero. Por ANRed.


Las Warmis del Kollasuyu marcharán durante la mañana del jueves 03 de septiembre por la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Provenientes de la Puna, la Quebrada y los Valles jujeños, las mujeres originarias trasladan su reclamo para presentar un petitorio formal ante el Congreso de la Nación, frente a la falta de respuestas por parte de la Dirección Provincial de Minería, la Dirección de Recursos Hídricos y el Ministerio de Ambiente de Jujuy, tras la Caminata de Mujeres del 2025.


Tal como adelantaron en su comunicado a la prensa, bajo el lema “Caminatas de Mujeres en defensa de la Pachamama 2026”, las voceras comunitarias exponen en esta jornada la contaminación que afecta a la Laguna de Pozuelos por el impacto de la actividad minera. “Exigimos el cese de la contaminación de nuestros territorios y el respeto a nuestros derechos como Pueblos Originarios”, señalaron en el documento.


Iniciada el 3 de agosto en Rinconada (Jujuy), la movilización al Congreso marca el cierre de la «Segunda Caminata de Warmis». Tras recorrer unos 2.000 kilómetros a pie durante todo el mes, con una reciente escala en Rosario, las manifestantes trasladan sus demandas a Buenos Aires. Denuncian la contaminación de la Laguna de Pozuelos y exigen la intervención de las autoridades nacionales ante la falta de respuestas del gobierno provincial.


Apuntan específicamente contra los daños generados por la Mina Pan de Azúcar, la Mina Pirquitas y la Mina Chinchillas. A este escenario se le suma la amenaza de desalojo que pesa sobre decenas de comunidades de sus tierras ancestrales debido al avance de pedimentos mineros a lo largo de toda la cuenca.


Las organizaciones exponen la violación del derecho a la Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada, consagrado en el Convenio 169 de la OIT, así como el incumplimiento del Acuerdo de Escazú (Ley 27.566) en materia de acceso a la información y justicia ambiental.


A través del petitorio que entregarán, las comunidades interpelan directamente al Poder Legislativo. Quieren: “saber si las comunidades originarias somos tratadas verdaderamente como sujetos de derecho colectivo» Y además, sostienen que: «cuestionamos el favorecimiento del extractivismo por encima del bienestar de las comunidades”.


La postura de las defensoras de la tierra es clara, y así lo dieron a conocer en su comunicado a los medios: «Las mujeres de la Puna, Quebrada y Valles no permitiremos que continúe la fragmentación de nuestras comunidades ni la destrucción de nuestros territorios ancestrales. Exigimos el derecho a permanecer y desarrollarnos en paz en nuestra tierra».

author: admin
title: Keep It In The Ground August Report
content:
Tamarack Sulfide Copper Mine Meeting – Blaine, MN (August 14, 2026)

A public meeting on the proposed Tamarack sulfide copper mine was held in Blaine, Minnesota. Upon entering, attendees were greeted by eight tables staffed by mining company representatives, positioned next to a tray of lemon-and-cucumber water, cookies, and baked goods. The testimonies, however, were powerful and sobering. A miner from the Iron Range spoke about how cleanup from mining operations conducted fifty years ago is still incomplete, even though that era was considered when they “did it right.” Representatives from the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe tribal administration testified that the proposed mine sits within two miles of their Minnomem (sp?) ricing beds, presenting an existential threat to the tribe’s land, water, and long-term survivability. Environmental advocates spoke about the track record of mining companies, noting that promises of responsible mining consistently fall short when measured against the devastation of contaminated water, spills, and Superfund sites left unattended for generations.

Northern Arapaho Chairman Opposes Bridger Pipeline (August 18, 2026)

Chairman Keenan Groesbeck of the Northern Arapaho Business Council issued a public statement of opposition to the Bridger Pipeline and expressed support for the Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes. The proposed crude oil pipeline crosses the Canadian border into Montana and Wyoming, traversing treaty lands and the Fort Peck Indian Reservation. The Northern Arapaho stand in solidarity with the Fort Peck Tribes in their opposition, and it is a welcome display of intertribal unity.

Red Stone Movement Meeting Pipestone, MN (August 18, 2026)

The Brave Heart Society, Indigenous Protector Movement, Indigenous Environmental Network, NDN Collective, Minnesota Environmental Affairs Council, the Chairman of the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe, and others gathered in Pipestone, Minnesota for the Red Stone Movement meeting. The day began with prayers and ceremony at the Sundance grounds. The united message from the group was clear: the survey process for the proposed Magellan pipeline was not conducted correctly, remains incomplete, inadequate, and unacceptable. The movement is calling on regulators to deny the pipeline permit.

Minnesota PUC Pipestone Comment Period Accepted Until September 11, 2026

The Minnesota Public Utilities Commission initial public comment period regarding the Magellan pipeline closed on August 21.

However, reply and final comments will be accepted until September 11. To leave a comment, email the PUC at consumer.puc@state.mn.us, referencing Docket 23-109.

Tribal leaders, Elders, and grassroots defenders are urging even more protectors and the public to comment in OPPOSITION to the Magellan/OneOK pipeline options proposed. The first permit was rescinded when it appeared the opposition was fierce, when 25,000 in opposition flowed in from across the country. Oceti Sakowin Native people and supporters expect that number will be exceeded with this extended deadline. These numbers reflect the sacred nature of the Sacred Site of the Pipestone Quarry, held in reverence and practice by thousands for centuries.

Online: https://mn.gov/puc/consumers/public-comments

Email: consumer.puc@state.mn.us – Reference Docket 23-109

Consumer Affairs Office Minnesota Public Utilities Commission

Governor Walz Signs BWCA Mining Ban Executive Order (August 18, 2026)

Governor Tim Walz signed an executive order banning copper-nickel mining in the Rainy River Headwaters Watershed. The ban preserves vast areas of some of the most pristine and widely used wilderness in Minnesota. Anyone who has canoed, camped, or walked through the Boundary Waters knows it is a life-changing and life-affirming experience that provides a spiritual connection to the natural world. The order effectively canceled the Twin Metals proposed mining project near Ely, Minnesota, and the Bois Forte Reservation.

Trump Administration Opens 62,000 Acres of Superior National Forest (August 19, 2026)

In what appears to be direct retaliation for Governor Walz’s mining ban, the Trump administration opened 62,000 acres of the Superior National Forest to potential mining and development. It is unclear how planned out this move was, but the timing suggests it was a response to the governor’s efforts to protect the area.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Una ciudad con menos árboles y más extractivismo urbano
content:
Por Natalia Concina


La docente y química María Angélica Di Giacomo comenzó en 2010 a enviar notas al Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires denunciando que observaba podas indiscriminadas. También contactó a periodistas que cubrían temáticas porteñas, pero durante dos años esas acciones no tuvieron eco. “Un día pasé frente a un árbol que estaban podando y me senté sola a llorar. Me di cuenta que para cambiar algo iba a tener que juntarme con otras personas y abrí un grupo de Facebook al que le puse ‘Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles”. Inmediatamente empezó a sumarse gente”, recuerda Di Giacomo a Tierra Viva.


Y continúa: “Nuestra primera actividad callejera fue cuando sacaron los árboles de la Avenida 9 de Julio para construir el Metrobús. No logramos frenar la remoción, pero fue un punto de inflexión porque comenzamos a tener contacto con quienes defienden el arbolado y el patrimonio natural y cultural de la ciudad”.


Desde entonces el grupo no paró de crecer. La poda tampoco.


El miedo a otros seres vivos


“El árbol no necesita ser podado, no le reporta ningún beneficio. Esta idea de que si le cortas ramas crece con más fuerza es un mito —explica Di Giacomo— La poda se hace por necesidad humana y debería reducirse a la más mínima expresión. Por ejemplo, la poda de refaldado, para que los peatones puedan caminar por la vereda y los autos pasar por la calle, o si tapa un semáforo; en cambio, si tapa una luminaria, ésta podría cambiarse de lugar”.


Sin embargo, desde la organización advierten que en las ciudades existe una percepción del árbol como riesgoso y la poda es vista como una solución: “Muchas personas prefieren los árboles mutilados porque los ven más prolijos. Existe un afán de control sobre la naturaleza y muchos miedos”, dice.


La mujer, que profesionalmente decidió no hacer carrera de investigadora para dedicarse a la docencia, afirma que uno de esos miedos es “a los otros seres vivos”: “Puede ser desde el muchacho que duerme en la puerta del edificio, hasta las abejas, los murciélagos, las palomas o los pajaritos porque les cagan el auto, las cucarachas, las ratas…todo lo vivo da miedo”.


Y agrega: “El otro factor que veo, que es mucho más grave, es que hay una imagen de que la ciudad es un domo. No se sabe de dónde viene el agua, a lo sumo se preocupan si llega el humo de algún incendio desde Rosario o de los humedales del Paraná. Pero no hay noción de que estamos formando parte de un sistema mucho más grande”.


Foto: Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles


Conocer para proteger


Guillermina Bruschi llegó a Basta de Mutilar Nuestros Árboles en 2019 cuando intentaron sacar árboles centenarios en el Barrio Nazca, al oeste de la ciudad, ubicado dentro de los límites de Villa Santa Rita: seis manzanas con edificaciones de más de cien años que en lugar de calles tiene pasajes angostos, un oasis en medio de la ciudad más ruidosa del país.


“En ese camino de defender estos árboles conocimos a María Angélica. Ella nos orientó sobre qué podíamos hacer como vecinos y logramos salvarlos”, cuenta Bruschi.


Con el impulso de ese proceso organizativo, después de la pandemia las y los vecinos retomaron una demanda histórica de Santa Rita: tener una plaza. “El primer documento de pedido de una plaza está en un diario de 1927. No sabemos por qué no se hizo, porque cada uno de estos barrios se hacía con una plaza y con una biblioteca”, relata. Después de varios años de movilización, la lucha tuvo un final feliz: en abril de 2025 se inauguró oficialmente este espacio público para el barrio.


Bruschi reconoce que en estos siete años descubrió muchas cosas que van más allá del arbolado. “Si consideramos que hay

20.000 personas muriendo en Europa por el calor extremo

, uno pensaría que los gobiernos tendrían como prioridad en la agenda la infraestructura verde y sucede exactamente lo contrario”, dice Guillermina, quien describe que en los últimos 20 años, se hicieron

40 millones de metros cuadrados de construcciones

 nuevas.


E indica que “eso significa que, además del calentamiento global, en la ciudad tenemos más hormigón y más cemento que años atrás que retienen más la temperatura y provoca lo que se llama el

efecto ‘isla de calor’

 que implica entre uno y seis grados más que en un entorno urbano donde hay menos cemento y hormigón”.

crisis ambiental

title: La Caminata de Warmis llegó a Rosario en defensa de la Pachamama
content:
Durante agosto, mes de la Pachamama, mujeres de comunidades originarias de la Puna jujeña emprendieron una extensa caminata desde la zona de Laguna de Pozuelos hacia Buenos Aires para visibilizar la lucha en defensa del agua, de la tierra y de los territorios ancestrales frente al avance de actividades extractivas.

La Caminata de Warmis en Rosario al Monumento a la Bandera. Fotos: Noelia Naporichi


La movilización conocida como Caminata de Warmis – Mujeres del Kollasuyu en defensa de la Pachamama (en Instagram:

@caminata.warmis

), partió el 3 de agosto desde Rinconada, Jujuy, a 3.500 metros sobre el nivel del mar, y viene atravesando distintas localidades donde mantienen encuentros con comunidades. Lo hicieron primero en su propia provincia, luego Salta, Tucumán, Santiago del Estero, Córdoba, y el pasado jueves las Warmis llegaron a la ciudad de Rosario, provincia de Santa Fe. Allí se encuentran antes de continuar su camino a la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, donde buscarán ser recibidas por legisladores y realizar actividades en el marco del Día Internacional de la Mujer Originaria, que se conmemora el 5 de septiembre en homenaje a Bartolina Sisa.


La Caminata recorre distintos territorios para visibilizar las luchas y resistencias que sostienen mujeres indígenas y comunidades frente a las amenazas sobre la Pachamama, los bienes comunes y los territorios ancestrales.


Las comunidades rechazan el avance de la explotación de los bienes naturales, la contaminación de las cuencas de agua dulce y el uso indiscriminado de los bienes comunes naturales en las cuatro regiones de la provincia de Jujuy: Puna, Quebrada, Valles y Yungas. La segunda caminata busca sensibilizar sobre la pérdida de la biodiversidad y denunciar las violaciones a los derechos de los pueblos indígenas.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/warmis_rosario_caminata_monumento_001.mp4


La Caminata de Warmis en Rosario. Video: Noelia Naporichi


A través de esta acción colectiva, las Warmis buscan poner en agenda sus demandas, fortalecer los vínculos entre comunidades y hacer escuchar una voz que nace de los territorios y de la organización comunitaria y popular.


Contra la minería contaminante


En Rosario realizaron el viernes a la mañana una conferencia de prensa y por la tarde, marcharon al Monumento a la Bandera y al Parque Nacional de la Bandera, donde realizaron un encuentro y una sahumada, ceremonia de agradecimiento a la Pachamama. También se reunieron con la comunidad de los barrios Qom (toba) y representantes de otros pueblos que se encuentran habitando la ciudad.


Conferencia de prensa de las Warmis ante la Municipalidad de Rosario. Foto: Noelia Naporichi


A la conferencia de prensa asistieron pocos medios. Entre ellos, estuvieron el periodista Claudio de Luca, de Aire Libre Radio Comunitaria, y la comunicadora qom Noelia Naporichi de Abya Yala Antiimperialista, autora de las fotos y videos de esta nota. Agradecemos a ambos por compartir su producción periodística con Indymedia Argentina.


Florencia Solís. Foto: Noelia Naporichi


“Queremos contarles que las Warmis venimos desde Rinconada, el último rincón de la patria, de la provincia de Jujuy, la cual estamos caminando en el marco del mes de agosto, en defensa de la Pachamama, para defender nuestra Pacha y decirles que estamos aquí …

author: Unknown
title: Zayıflama iğneleri tehlikeli mi? Bilim ne diyor, sağlıkçılar ne öneriyor?
content:
Kilo kaybı sağlayan ilaçlar, obezite tedavisinde önemli bir seçenek haline geldi. Ancak “zayıflama iğnesi” olarak bilinen bu ilaçlar masum birer kilo verme ürünü değil. Bilimsel çalışmalar etkili olduklarını gösterirken, ciddi yan etkiler ve yanlış kullanım riskleri de bulunuyor. İlaçların hekim değerlendirmesi ve yaşam tarzı değişiklikleriyle birlikte kullanılmasının ise önemi büyük.

Son yıllarda sosyal medyanın da etkisiyle kilo vermek isteyenlerin gündemine giren GLP-1 temelli ilaçlar, aslında başlangıçta özellikle tip 2 diyabetin tedavisinde kullanılan ilaçlar arasında yer alıyordu. Semaglutid ve tirzepatid gibi etken maddeler iştahı azaltıyor, tokluk hissini artırıyor ve kan şekeri düzenlenmesine yardımcı oluyor. Bu etkiler, obezite tedavisinde de kullanılmalarının önünü açtı.

Ancak bu ilaçları “hızlı kilo verme iğnesi” olarak görmek önemli bir yanılgı. Dünya Sağlık Örgütü (DSÖ), 2025'te yayımladığı kılavuzda semaglutid, tirzepatid ve liraglutid gibi GLP-1 ilaçlarının yetişkinlerde obezitenin uzun süreli tedavisinde kullanılabileceğini koşullu olarak önerdi. DSÖ, bunun yanında uzun dönem güvenlilik, tedavinin bırakılması sonrası ne olacağı, maliyet ve sağlık sistemlerinin bu tedavilere hazırlığı konusunda belirsizlikler bulunduğuna dikkat çekti.

Evet. Bu ilaçların kilo kaybı konusunda güçlü bilimsel kanıtları bulunuyor. Özellikle semaglutid ve tirzepatid, iştah ve enerji alımı üzerinde etkili olarak kişilerin daha az yemek yemesine yardımcı olabiliyor. Ancak alınan sonuç kişiden kişiye değişiyor ve ilaçların etkisi, tedavinin süresi ve kişinin yaşam tarzıyla yakından ilişkili.

Bu nedenle sağlık otoriteleri ilaçları diyet ve fiziksel aktivitenin alternatifi olarak değil, obezitenin kapsamlı tedavisinin bir parçası olarak değerlendiriyor. DSÖ de GLP-1 ilaçları kullanan obezitesi olan yetişkinlere yapılandırılmış sağlıklı beslenme ve fiziksel aktivite programlarının eşlik etmesini öneriyor.

Doğru hastada, uygun dozda ve hekim gözetiminde kullanıldığında bu ilaçların yararları ve riskleri klinik olarak değerlendirilmiş durumda. Ancak ciddi yan etki potansiyelleri nedeniyle gelişigüzel kullanılmaları güvenli değil.

En sık karşılaşılan sorunlar arasında bulantı, kusma, ishal, kabızlık, karın ağrısı, hazımsızlık gibi şikâyetler bulunuyor.

Bunların yanı sıra ilaçların resmi güvenlik bilgilerinde pankreatit, safra kesesi hastalıkları, böbrek hasarı ve ciddi gastrointestinal reaksiyonlar gibi daha önemli riskler de yer alıyor. Bazı hastalarda kan şekeri düşüklüğü ve diyabetik retinopati komplikasyonları da önem taşıyor.

Bu nedenle “yan etkisi sadece biraz mide bulantısı” şeklindeki yaklaşım doğru değil.

İlaçların etkili olabilmesi kadar doğru dozda kullanılması da önemli. Özellikle doktor kontrolü dışında kullanılan ürünlerde doz hataları ciddi problemlere yol açabiliyor. ABD Gıda ve İlaç Dairesi (FDA), onaysız veya bileşik olarak hazırlanan semaglutid ürünlerinde yanlış doz kullanımına bağlı olarak hastaneye yatış gerektiren vakalar bildirildiğini açıkladı.

Bildirilen sorunlar arasında şiddetli bulantı ve kusma, karın ağrısı, susuz kalma, pankreatit ve safra taşı bulunuyor.

Uzmanların en önemli uyarılarından biri de ilacın nereden temin edildiği. FDA, onaylanmamış semaglutid ve tirzepatid ürünlerinin güvenlilik, etkinlik ve kalite açısından piyasaya çıkmadan önce kurumun değerlendirmesinden geçmediğini belirtiyor.

Daha da önemlisi, kurum sahte semaglutid ve tirzepatid ürünleri tespit edildiğini; bazı ürünlerin etiketlerinde gerçekte bulunmayan eczanelerin isimlerinin dahi kullanılabildiğini bildiriyor.

Bu nedenle sosyal medya üzerinden, internet sitelerinden veya doktor değerlendirmesi olmadan satılan ürünler ile ruhsatlı ilaçların aynı şey olmadığı unutulmamalı.

Bu ilaçların temel kullanım alanı obezite veya belirli koşullarla aşırı kiloluluk gibi tıbbi durumların tedavisi. Sırf birkaç kilo vermek isteyen sağlıklı bir kişinin sosyal medyada gördüğü bir ilaçla kendi kendine tedaviye başlaması doğru değil. Tedavi kararı verilirken kişinin kilosunun yanı sıra boyu, vücut kitle indeksi, eşlik eden hastalıkları, kullandığı ilaçlar, beslenme alışkanlıkları ve diğer sağlık koşulları birlikte değerlendirilmeli.

Ayrıca gebelik söz konusu olduğunda GLP-1 tedavileri kullanılmamalı; DSÖ'nün obezite kılavuzu da hamile kadınları kapsam dışında bırakıyor.

Burada da önemli bir ayrıntı var. GLP-1 ilaçlarının iştah üzerindeki etkisi tedavi sürdüğü sürece devam eder. Tedavi bırakıldığında iştahın yeniden artması ve …

Lights, Camera, Action – Immediate Steps

To answer the question of why the December 4th execution of UHC CEO Brian Thompson happened seems easy. Denials, price gouging, and the health insurance industry at large. However, as one unravels the outpouring of stories and symbolism in its wake, one finds it difficult to wrestle into a specific activist program. The questions one runs into are so urgent, but so foundational, that they resist easy answers.

Who lives and who dies? Who is healed and who is hurt? Who takes resources and who loses them?

There are no quick fixes to this system’s problems. Even if you personally have good insurance coverage and good health, you have seen loved ones struggle to afford or access lifesaving care. You have seen the downstream effects of for-profit healthcare in rising costs, closed hospitals, under-staffing, wait times, bureaucratic obfuscation. You have seen people lose everything to cover cancer care, forced to choose between rescue inhalers and rent, while c-suites get rich off the blood in the streets. It is impossible to avoid the growing realization that there are no quick fixes to this system’s problems because this system is the problem.

This is a part of the reason the events of December 4th resonated across the globe. While the “united states” is particularly bad in this regard, paying substantially more for worse care, other countries still struggle. “britain” has such lengthy wait lists for gender affirming care that the system forces trans people out of the country. “canada” may have universal healthcare that makes public hospitals and clinics available, but even still, has increasingly privatized some care, leading to 17.5% of the population to significant medical debt,[1] and the healthcare regime also pushes disabled people toward assisted suicide programs.[2] In Cuba, healthcare is free but US sanctions manufacture health scarcity by blocking the flow of technologies and medications both to punish Cuba for fighting western imperial capitalism and as propaganda against free healthcare.[3]

Within the “united states”, attempts to revise policies for better health outcomes have met little success.4 This is because such attempts do not fundamentally change the power dynamic at play, so insurance companies and hospital corporations continue raising prices, deciding what care gets covered, and limiting available services regardless of what laws are passed or revoked. Reform is not the solution when the system kills for profit.

We do not want to simply renegotiate the terms of a hostage scenario. We want the power to no longer be hostages.

author: Briana Torres
title: Planned Parenthood’s Funding Ban Ended — But Money Isn’t Flowing in Every State
content:
Standard federal Medicaid reimbursement should have automatically resumed in about three dozen states.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Last year’s federal ban on using Medicaid to pay Planned Parenthood might have ended, but its funding has not automatically resumed nationwide.

On July 4, 2025, President Donald Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” barred federal Medicaid reimbursements for one year to nonprofit family planning organizations that both provide abortions and received more than $800,000 in Medicaid reimbursements between October 2022 and September 2023.

The Hyde Amendment already prohibits Medicaid coverage of abortion with rare exceptions; the 2025 provision blocked reimbursement for other preventive care services Medicaid normally covers, like contraception, cancer screenings, STI testing and treatment, and annual exams.

The law never named Planned Parenthood. However, its criteria were so narrow that, as the organization argued in court, they seemed written to target the reproductive health-care giant. Only two other family-planning chains — Maine Family Planning and Health Imperatives, in Massachusetts — lost their funding.

Officially, these organizations can once again bill Medicaid for covered services. But when I scanned the states to see the status of Planned Parenthood’s federal funding, I found a more complicated budgetary reality. Its affiliate clinics have resumed billing for Medicaid-covered reproductive health-care services in many places — but in other states, GOP lawmakers are finding new ways to starve it of cash.

After a year-long hiatus, standard federal Medicaid reimbursement should have automatically resumed in about three dozen states, based on a June 2026 report by the health policy research nonprofit KFF. These include the 11 Democrat-led states that spent their own funds to keep affected clinics open — among them California, Connecticut, Illinois, and Maine.

My research shows that Medicaid payments are also up and running in Republican-run Ohio and purple Pennsylvania, among other states.

Just because something should automatically happen, however, doesn’t mean it will.

A handful of states had already blocked Planned Parenthood’s participation in Medicaid programs before the federal government did — some for over a decade. Texas, Arkansas, Mississippi, Missouri, and South Carolina — all Republican strongholds — fall into this category.

Despite some litigation over their Planned Parenthood exclusions, neither the federal ban nor its expiration changed the status quo in these places. Prior to July 2025, Medicaid patients in these states could not use their coverage at any Planned Parenthood clinic for any service — not birth control, cancer screenings, STI testing, or annual OB-GYN exams. And they still can’t.

Planned Parenthood’s status in Iowa is more legally complicated.

In 2017, Iowa withdrew from the federally matched family-planning program and created a state-funded alternative — one that explicitly excludes abortion providers, though the Iowa Planned Parenthood clinics still appear to participate in Medicaid.

But multiple other states have seen their own, similar exclusion laws tied up in court. The Supreme Court’s 2025 decision in Medina v. Planned Parenthood South Atlantic, which held that Medicaid patients cannot sue states in federal court to see the provider of their choice, may bolster these exclusion efforts.

Medicaid’s “free choice of provider” provision generally allows Medicaid patients to receive care from any qualified provider willing to treat them, including Planned Parenthood. Medina did not change the law, but it removed the possibility of federal litigation to enforce it. This eliminated one of the principal ways patients had enforced this provision.

As a result, when a state excludes Planned Parenthood from Medicaid, it’s now harder for patients to challenge that decision. That has created the opportunity for states to revive exclusion laws previously blocked by federal courts.

For example, after Medina, Indiana moved to vacate a 2013 court injunction on its 2011 law excluding the organization from the state’s Medicaid program. The district court granted that request in July 2026. Planned Parenthood has appealed, but it remains suspended from Indiana’s Medicaid program until the Seventh Circuit rules.

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: EXPLAINER: Why mental health professionals want DepEd’s live shooter drill deferred
content:
Simulation drill during the National Safe Schools Summit and Safety Drill at the Manila Science High School last July 15, 2026. (Photo from the DepEd Facebook page)

Psychiatrists and child mental health specialists insist that preparedness and psychological well-being should not be treated as competing priorities.

MANILA — The Department of Education’s (DepEd) plans to conduct a nationwide simultaneous school safety drill for active attack incidents has drawn concern from mental health professionals, who warned that hyper-realistic active shooter simulations may cause psychological harm to learners while offering little evidence that they improve school safety.

In a joint statement released on August 22, the Philippine Psychiatric Association (PPA) and the Philippine Society for Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (PSCAP) called for the deferment of any simulation of a live shooter attack drill, saying school preparedness must remain trauma-informed and evidence-based.

The two organizations stressed that they support efforts to make schools safe and resilient but argued that the methods used to prepare students and school personnel matter as much as the goal itself.

The statement came in response to a DepEd memorandum dated August 12 directing schools nationwide to conduct a nationwide simultaneous school safety drill for active attack incidents.

The PPA and the PSCAP said active attack simulations differ significantly from routine drills for earthquakes, fires, and other emergencies.

The groups said schools regularly conduct disaster preparedness exercises because these activities teach practical responses to real emergencies without exposing learners to graphic or highly realistic depictions of violence.

They argued that live shooter simulations introduce a different level of psychological risk because they often recreate violent scenarios that place participants in situations resembling actual attacks.

According to the groups, these exercises can expose children and adolescents to fear, uncertainty, and distress that may linger long after the drill ends.

Mental health professionals based their position on studies and recommendations from medical, educational, and safety organizations.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine reported in 2025 that available evidence remains insufficient to conclude that active shooter simulations improve safety outcomes.

The report also advised schools against using high-intensity drills and deceptive practices.

The PPA and the PSCAP cited a large-scale study published in 2021 that analyzed 54 million social media posts from 114 schools in the United States.

Researchers found a 42 percent increase in language associated with stress and anxiety after shooter drills.

The same study documented a 39 percent increase in language associated with depression.

Researchers found that these effects remained evident for at least 90 days after the exercises.

The organizations also cited a 2020 policy statement from the American Academy of Pediatrics, which cautioned against involving children and adolescents in high-intensity crisis simulations.

The academy said schools should never rely on deception when conducting emergency preparedness exercises involving young people.

The groups also referenced guidance released this year by the National Association of School Psychologists, the National Association of School Resource Officers, the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, and Safe and Sound Schools.

The guidance recommended banning hyper-realistic simulations, requiring advance notice before drills, and involving school mental health professionals in planning and implementation.

Mental health experts said children process fear and traumatic experiences differently from adults.

The PPA and the PSCAP warned that realistic simulations can trigger strong emotional reactions among learners, especially those who have previously experienced violence, abuse, displacement, disasters, or other traumatic events.

The organizations noted that some learners may also have disabilities, sensory-processing needs, or mental health conditions that make them more vulnerable to distress during highly immersive drills.

Mental health professionals argued that schools should avoid preparedness measures that inadvertently create psychological harm while attempting to prevent physical harm.

The groups emphasized that protecting learners requires balancing …

La brochure trouve d'autant plus son sens dans le contexte actuel de fascisation et d'eugénisme grandissant. Qu'on pense à la gestion de la pandémie de Covid-19 mais aussi plus récemment aux épisodes caniculaires répétés (durant lesquels les personnes psychiatrisées ou médicamentées sont plus particulièrement victimes) ou encore plus idirectement à la loi «

 

fin de vie

La psychiatrie est aussi utilisée comme outil de surveillance et de répression depuis maintenant une bonne dizaine d'année, avec une accélération impressionante depuis les mandats Macron. Dès 2018, un nouveau fichier, Hopsyweb, est créé afin de recenser les données relatives aux personnes faisant l'objet de soins psychiatriques sans consentement (internements sur demande d'un tiers, d'un juge, du préfet...)

Le tout, sous-entendant évidemment que les forces répressives prennent en compte la psychiatrie et le "trouble mental" soit comme un facteur aggravant de la soi-disant "radicalisation" voire comme menace en soi à prévenir. Ces listes de personnes psychiatrisées rappellent évidemment les mouvements fascistes historiques et l'implication des corporations médicales dans ces derniers, notamment à travers le mouvement eugéniste, qu'on retrouve des Etats-Unis à l'Europe dès les années 1920, soutenu par de nombreuses fondations capitalistes

title: Hastalar için tedavi ortamı hayati önemde
content:
İzmir – Kanser hastalarının tedavisinde kullanılan kemoterapi ve port uygulama odalarındaki fiziki ve teknik eksiklikler hem hastaların hem de sağlık emekçilerinin sağlığını tehdit ediyor. Sağlık ve Sosyal Hizmet Emekçileri Sendikası (SES) İzmir 1 No’lu Şube Eş Başkanı Hava Akçan, bazı birimlerde pencere ve yeterli havalandırma bulunmadığını, sitotoksik atık sistemlerinde eksiklikler olduğunu belirterek gerekli koşulların sağlanmasını istedi.

İzmir’de Ege Üniversitesi Tülay Aktaş Onkoloji Hastanesi, Dokuz Eylül Üniversitesi Hastanesi Onkoloji Enstitüsü, İzmir Tepecik Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi, İzmir Katip Çelebi Üniversitesi Atatürk Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi ile Dr. Suat Seren Göğüs Hastalıkları ve Cerrahisi Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi başta olmak üzere kamu ve üniversite hastanelerinde kanser hastalarına tedavi hizmeti veriliyor.

İzmir’de aktif olarak kemoterapi gören hasta sayısına ilişkin güncel ve il bazlı resmi veri bulunmuyor. Sağlık Bakanlığı bu verileri kamuoyuyla paylaşmazken, kanser tanısı alan her hastaya da kemoterapi uygulanmıyor. Hastalığın türü ve evresine göre cerrahi, radyoterapi, immünoterapi ve hedefe yönelik ilaç tedavileri de uygulanabiliyor.

SES İzmir 1 No’lu Şube Eş Başkanı Hava Akçan ise kentte her yıl ortalama 12 bin yeni kanser vakası görüldüğünü belirterek, “Bu kadar yüksek sayıda yeni vaka görülmesine rağmen kentte kaç hastanın aktif olarak kemoterapi tedavisi aldığına ilişkin elimizde net bir istatistik yok” dedi.

Kemoterapi ve port uygulama alanlarında yaşanan sorunlara ilişkin konuşan Akçan, bağışıklık sistemi baskılanmış kanser hastaları açısından tedavi ortamının hayati önemde olduğunu söyledi.

Sağlık emekçilerinden aldıkları bilgiler doğrultusunda port uygulama odalarında öne çıkan sorunları anlatan Akçan, “Ünitedeki arkadaşlarımızla da konuştuk. Port odasına ilişkin en temel sorunlardan biri odanın penceresinin olmayışı. Yeterli bir havalandırma sistemi de bulunmuyor. İğne atık kutusunun sitotoksik atık kategorisine uygun olmaması da diğer önemli sorunlardan biri” dedi.

Bir ünitede klimanın yaklaşık iki haftadır arızalı olduğunu aktaran Akçan, eksik parça gerekçesiyle sorunun giderilmediğini ve çalışanların küçük bir vantilatörle çalışmak zorunda kaldığını söyledi.

Kanser hastalarının bağışıklık sistemlerinin tedavi sürecinde son derece hassas olduğunu belirten Akçan, kemoterapi ve port uygulama alanlarının buna uygun düzenlenmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

Akçan, “Kemoterapi ve port uygulama odalarının hem hastaların enfeksiyondan korunmasını sağlayacak hem de çalışanları sitotoksik ilaçların etkilerinden koruyacak şekilde düzenlenmesi gerekiyor. HEPA filtreli havalandırma sistemleri, sitotoksik ilaç döküntü kitleri, acil durum ekipmanları ve uygun çalışma koşulları sağlanmalı. Bunların eksikliği, zaten bağışıklığı baskılanmış hastaları ciddi enfeksiyonlara açık hale getiriyor” diye konuştu.

Sorunun yalnızca hastalar açısından değerlendirilmemesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Akçan, kemoterapi birimlerinde çalışan sağlık emekçilerinin her gün tehlikeli sitotoksik ilaçlarla temas ettiğine dikkat çekti.

Akçan, “Bu koşullar sağlık emekçilerinin sağlığını da doğrudan ilgilendiriyor. Tehlikeli sitotoksik ilaçlarla çalışan sağlık emekçilerinin gerekli koruyucu donanıma ve güvenli çalışma ortamına sahip olması gerekiyor. Aksi halde meslek hastalıkları ve uzun vadeli kalıcı sağlık sorunları açısından çalışanlar da risk altında bırakılıyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

Kemoterapi odalarındaki eksikliklerin sağlık politikalarından bağımsız olmadığını söyleyen Akçan, eğitim ve araştırma hastaneleri ile üniversite hastaneleri dahil sağlık kurumlarında temel teknik donanımların sağlanması gerektiğini belirtti.

Akçan, “Sağlığa yeterli bütçenin ayrılmaması en temel teknik ihtiyaçların dahi karşılanmamasına neden oluyor. Hastaneleri ticarethane olarak gören anlayış hem hastaların tedavi hakkını hem de sağlık emekçilerinin güvenliğini tehlikeye atıyor. Sağlık politikalarının hasta eden değil, koruyan ve önleyen bir niteliğe kavuşması gerekiyor” dedi.

Sağlıkta Kalite Standartları (SKS) ile İş Sağlığı ve Güvenliği Kanunu’nun gereklerinin yerine getirilmesi çağrısında bulunan Akçan, “Kanser hastalarının enfeksiyonsuz, güvenli ortamlarda tedavi görmesi ve sağlık emekçilerinin güvenli koşullarda çalışması bir lütuf değil, en temel insan hakkıdır” diye konuştu.

Just six years after millions of people across the country took part in racial justice uprisings after the police murders of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor, politicians and pundits of all stripes — from reactionaries like President Donald Trump to progressives like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez — have turned against demands to decrease funding for police. Those demands were popularized over years of organizing from a broad popular movement against decades of unprecedented mass incarceration.

In this interview, Alec Karakatsanis explains the roots of the backlash, how both Republicans and Democrats have used it to increase the powers of police, and why it’s essential to rebuild the movement to fund communities, not cops. Karakatsanis is the founder and executive director of the Civil Rights Corps, an organization that has pioneered landmark litigation challenging systemic injustices in the punishment bureaucracy, author of the book, Copaganda: How the Police and Media Manipulate our News, and publisher of the Copaganda Newsletter.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Ashley Smith: After the police murder of George Floyd, the U.S. exploded in protest, becoming the biggest wave of mass demonstrations in U.S. history with as many as an estimated 26 million people marching across the country. Republicans and Democrats launched a backlash against the movement. What have they argued and done?

Alec Karakatsanis: It’s important to underscore that it’s not just Republicans behind the backlash. It’s a bipartisan establishment assault on the movement that emerged in the decade before 2020. That struggle aimed to reduce the size and power of the punishment bureaucracy, the term I use to describe the institutions the government uses to repress people and the for-profit industries parasitic on them.

That bureaucracy’s role is to control and manage inequality, targeting the most oppressed in our society, from poor people to people of color to people with disabilities and immigrants. It also represses the people involved in social movements that struggle for a more equal society in order to prevent those movements from achieving popular power. Both parties denounced the social movement’s demand to decrease investment in the bureaucracies of repression and increase investment in systems of care.

They used three main tactics. First, they whipped up a frenzy over retail theft and street crimes, harms mainly associated in the public imagination with poor and marginalized people. A lot of this was not founded in facts. For instance, the supposed epidemic of shoplifting turned out to be a lie. It wasn’t going up nationally at all.

They used that fiction to deflect attention from the crimes perpetrated by police, prison guards, bankers, pharmaceutical executives, tax evaders, polluters, and health insurance companies. These cause far more death, injury, and harm to our safety than crimes committed by poor people. For example, FBI figures for all property crimes combined in the United States are dwarfed by estimates of corporate wage theft.

Second, as discussed at length in Copaganda, they claimed that crimes committed by marginalized people are increasing across the country. This fearmongering tricked lots of people into thinking that crime is going up. It’s actually plummeted to historic lows.

Third, liberal and conservative pundits and media claimed that the only solution to their manufactured lie of increasing crime is more investment in the punishment bureaucracy. So, dozens of cities expanded budgets for police and prisons each year since the killing of George Floyd.

Trump in particular has dramatically increased funding of the surveillance state. And he’s deploying its institutions like the National Guard, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to collaborate with the police in city after city to crush marginalized people and political opposition.

How do these two parties carry out the same project in different ways?

title: Jan D. Matthews - Pour la Destruction de l'École
content:
Auteur·e

: Jan D. Matthews

Titre

: Pour la Destruction de l'École

Date

: 2004

Notes

: Titre original : Toward the Destruction of Schooling

Source

:

https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/anonymous-toward-the-destruction-of-schooling


Chapitre 1. Le rôle de l’école dans la société


“

Quand on vous examine, répondez avec des questions

” — Graffiti à Paris, 1968


 La plupart des gens n’aiment pas qu’on leur dise quoi faire. Toute institution qui vise à structurer et enrégimenter la vie d’une personne est, dans une certaine mesure, en conflit avec cette personne. Ce qui est intéressant, c’est que cette personne n’est pas toujours en conflit volontaire avec l’institution. Ceux qui sont obéissants et remplissent leur rôle d’élèves essaient naturellement d’ignorer les effets négatifs que leur scolarité a sur eux. Mais qui nierait honnêtement que ces effets sont bien visibles ? Les étudiants apprennent, tout au long du processus de scolarisation, à être conformistes, sans imagination, dociles et à bien d’autres choses qui sont généralement considérées comme des vertus dans le monde du travail. Restez ainsi et vous ne vous sentirez peut-être jamais bien dans votre peau, mais vous serez félicité par des figures d’autorité pour le reste de votre vie. Je pense que les sentiments antagonistes que les gens ont envers l’école reflètent ce que les écoles essaient de vous faire. Notre situation actuelle dans laquelle l‘école obligatoire semble si naturelle a un contexte historique ; les forces à l’œuvre et les raisons pour lesquelles nous passons une si grande partie de notre vie à l’école ne peuvent être expliquées de manière adéquate que d’un point de vue qui considère l’école historiquement en termes de moyens employés et de fins souhaitées et regarde où ces conceptions institutionnelles laissent l’individu pris jusqu’à l’école. Une telle perspective ne peut être révolutionnaire que si elle s’identifie à l’individu pris à l’école, à ses besoins et ses désirs, sa colère et sa frustration. Nous devons examiner comment l’école s’intègre dans l’ensemble de la société et quelles sortes de relations sociales et d’institutions dépendent du maintien de cet individu — vous, à toutes fins utiles — acquiescement. Le problème, à savoir que la plupart des gens font en fait ce qu’on leur dit, est un problème avec la totalité des relations sociales civilisées.


 La scolarisation est un processus fondamental de notre société. Il peut être compris comme l’ensemble des techniques par lesquelles une société enseigne aux jeunes les connaissances, les valeurs et les attitudes nécessaires pour devenir des membres responsables de la société, reproduisant l’ordre social dominant. Les cloches, les classes, les règles, la discipline — tous sont des aspects importants d’un processus de contrôle visant à modeler l’individu dans une forme plus souhaitable pour les autres — pour les autorités. L’école, comme le travail, est basée sur la coercition. D’une manière générale, on ne fait pas de travail scolaire parce que l’expérience en elle-même est enrichissante. On ne fait pas ses devoirs à sa guise. De plus, il y a une carotte ou un bâton qui guide votre progression, généralement les deux. Max Stirner avait raison lorsqu’il a dit que “la question de l’école est une question de vie”. La compétence de vie la plus importante enseignée dans les écoles est l’asservissement. Il est absolument essentiel à tous les systèmes sociaux hiérarchiques. L’éducation, comme William Torrey Harris (Commissaire américain à l’éducation au tournant du siècle) l’a un jour définie, est « la subsomption de l’individu ». Personne n’est absolument à l’abri des pressions sociales, des forces matérielles, des influences extérieures. Mais il ne s’ensuit pas qu’il faille se soumettre à l’idéal de “l’adaptation” de l’individu au terrain social : la modification des comportements administrée par les gardiens de la République. Il y a ici une tension essentielle : la tension entre des individus uniques et les institutions sociales qui empêchent leur autodétermination.


 La nécessité des écoles est profondément enracinée dans la psyché moderne. Implicite dans l’acceptation de toute idéologie politique moderne est l’hypothèse que l’individu existe pour servir le bien commun ou un principe supérieur extérieur à la subjectivité personnelle — en fait, cela semble être la base de toute idéologie, de tous les systèmes politiques, de toutes les formes de régner. title: Una Mirada Hacia El Futuro
content:
Título

: Una Mirada Hacia El Futuro

Fecha

: 1969

Notas

: Título original:

Looking Forward

. Traducido entre 2024-2026 por

La Conquista del Panda

 bajo licencia

CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

Fuente

: Obra original recuperada desde

archive.org


Dedicado a las personas jóvenes de todo el mundo que deben afrontar los retos del siglo XXI.


Sobre la obra


 Mirando al futuro es un libro imaginativo y fascinante en el que los autores te llevarán de viaje por la cultura y la tecnología del siglo XXI. Tras una sección introductoria en la que se analiza «lo que moldea nuestro futuro», explorarás los porqués del poco familiar, a veces alarmante, pero apasionante mundo de dentro de cien años.


 Verás esta sociedad a través de los ojos de Scott y Hella, una pareja del próximo siglo. Su vivienda está equipada con un cibernador, un dispositivo informático aparentemente mágico, pero basado en principios científicos hoy conocidos. Ayuda a regular las horas de sueño, las comunicaciones en todo el mundo, un increíble complejo de vida submarina e incluso la ingesta calórica diaria de la «joven» pareja. Son cuarentones, pero pueden esperar vivir 200 años. El mundo en el que viven Scott y Hella es un mundo que ha logrado el control total del clima, que ha desarrollado un ordenador del tamaño de un dedo que se implanta en el cerebro de cada bebé al nacer (y los bebés se incuban científicamente para que las mujeres del siglo XXI no tengan que pasar por los dolores del parto), y que ha perfeccionado la manipulación genética que permite mejorar la especie humana por medio de la ciencia.


 Económicamente, el mundo es utópico para nuestros estándares. Hace tiempo que desaparecieron los empleos, los salarios y el dinero. Nada tiene precio y las posesiones personales no son necesarias. Se ha superado el nacionalismo y se ha logrado el desarme total; la tecnología educativa ha dejado obsoletas las escuelas y los profesores. Los niños aprenden haciendo, y son independientes en este mundo amistoso a los cinco años.


 La principal fuente de esta sociedad mayor es el Centro de Correlación, «Cencor», un gigantesco complejo de ordenadores que sirve a la humanidad, pero nunca la esclaviza. Cencor regula la producción, la comunicación, el transporte y todas las demás tareas onerosas y monótonas del pasado. Esto libera a los seres humanos para que vivan experiencias creativas y estimulantes en lugar de vidas vacías de ocio sin sentido.


 Obviamente, este libro es especulativo, pero está sólidamente basado en los avances científicos que ahora se conocen. Y como dicen los autores:


Entenderás mejor este libro si eres de las que ven el hoy como un peldaño entre el ayer y el mañana.


Necesitarás ser sensible a las injusticias, a las oportunidades de felicidad perdidas y a los agudos conflictos que caracterizan a nuestra civilización del siglo XX. Si tu mente es capaz de sopesar nuevas ideas y evaluarlas con perspicacia, este libro es para ti.


No tenemos una bola de cristal. ...Queremos que introduzcas nuestras ideas en tu propio ordenador, para que puedas encontrar ideas aún mejores que puedan contribuir a moldear el futuro de nuestra civilización.


Sobre los autores


 Jacque Fresco trabajó como diseñador industrial durante treinta años, diseñando todo tipo de equipos, desde casas prefabricadas hasta automóviles, equipos electrónicos y médicos, sistemas de ingeniería ergonómica y cientos de productos comerciales e inventos. Ha diseñado y patentado artículos tan diversos como una estructura de ala de avión revolucionaria, patentada por la USAAF, y películas tridimensionales que no requieren el «uso de gafas especiales». Se han publicado numerosos artículos y fotografías sobre su trabajo en muchas revistas y periódicos. Ha ejercido de asesor técnico en varias películas, incluida una de las primeras sobre estaciones espaciales y un viaje a la Luna titulada «Project Moon Base». Vive en Miami.


 Kenneth S. Keyes, Jr., es un hombre polifacético. Estudió en la Universidad de Duke y se licenció en la Universidad de Miami, con la especialidad principal en psicología y la secundaria en música. Entre sus aficiones se encuentran el arte, la música sinfónica, la navegación a vela —vive a bordo de un yate de 71 pies llamado Caprice— y la escritura; es autor de

Cómo desarrollar tu capacidad de razonamiento

 y

Cómo vivir más tiempo, con más fuerza y más delgado

. Ha impartido clases en la División de Cursos Nocturnos de la Universidad de Miami …
