author: Mag
title: Tarifrunde Metall und Elektro 2026: „Die Lage ist extrem differenziert … Was sollen wir fordern?“
content:
Dossier


„

Die Tarifbewegung in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie ist gestartet. Die Tarifkommissionen der IG Metall haben sich zusammengeschaltet, um die Lage und erste Forderungen zu diskutieren. Die Lage ist extrem differenziert: Viele Betriebe stecken in der Krise, andere wiederum machen gute Gewinne. Ab Oktober verhandelt die IG Metall wieder über höhere Entgelte für 3,8 Millionen Beschäftigte der Metall- und Elektroindustrie. Zum Auftakt zur Tarifbewegung haben die Tarifkommissionen der IG Metall am Mittwoch die Kündigung der derzeitigen Entgelttarifverträge in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie beschlossen – die Voraussetzung für Tarifverhandlungen – und die Diskussion über die wirtschaftliche Lage und mögliche Forderungen für die Tarifverhandlungen gestartet

…“

Meldung der IG Metall vom 25. Juni 2026

 

 und erste Beiträge dazu:


Pforzheim lässt grüßen: IG Metall schon vor Beginn der Tarifrunde Metall und Elektro 2026 zu flexiblem Tarifabschluss bereit – (Flassbeck: „ein grandioser Irrweg“)


Christiane Benner: IG Metall ist zu flexiblem Tarifabschluss bereit


„

Die Gewerkschaftsvorsitzende Christiane Benner will bei der Lohnrunde stärker nach Geschäftslage und Region differenzieren. Einen reinen Inflationsausgleich lehnt sie aber ab.


Die IG Metall will in der anstehenden Tarifrunde der Metall- und Elektroindustrie spürbare Lohnzuwächse für die Beschäftigten durchsetzen. „Ein Inflationsausgleich wäre zu wenig“, sagte die IG-Metall-Vorsitzende Christiane Benner

im Interview mit der WirtschaftsWoche


 [paywall].

Zugleich zeigte sich Benner angesichts der schwierigen Situation vieler Industriebetriebe offen für einen Tarifabschluss mit Öffnungsklauseln. „Wir wissen, dass die wirtschaftliche Lage bei vielen Betrieben angespannt ist. Eine solche Situation habe ich während meiner Zeit bei der IG Metall noch nie erlebt“, so Benner. „Flexible Instrumente, die die wirtschaftliche Situation berücksichtigen, sind keine Revolution. Sie sind Bestandteil einer differenzierten Tarifpolitik – und es hat sie in der Vergangenheit auch schon gegeben“, so Benner im WirtschaftsWoche-Interview. Sie verwies darauf, dass es in einigen Branchen sehr gut laufe, etwa in der Luftfahrt, Teilen des Energiesektors, der Medizintechnik und der Rüstungsindustrie. Auch geografisch bestünden große Unterschiede

…“

Artikel von Bert Losse und Annina Reimann vom 31.08.2026 in der WirtschaftsWoche online

 


IG-Metall will mehr betriebliche Lohn-Flexibilität – Das ist ein grandioser Irrweg


„Nicht von den Arbeitgebern, nein, von der IG-Metall selbst kommt ein Vorstoß zur Flexibilisierung der Tarifabschlüsse. Das ist tragisch. Es zeigt jedoch die seit Anfang der 2000er Jahre um sich greifende Desorientierung der Gewerkschaftsfunktionäre. Jahrzehntelang war der Flächentarifvertrag das wichtigste Instrument gewerkschaftlicher Lohnpolitik. Doch das Wissen um die überragende Bedeutung des Flächentarifvertrages für die Arbeitnehmer und für die gesamte Volkswirtschaft ist verloren gegangen. Wer Produktivitätszuwächse und steigende Reallöhne für alle Beschäftigten will, muss auf der strikten Anwendung des Flächentarifvertrages beharren. Wer davon abweicht, führt die Volkswirtschaft auf die falsche Schiene der Rettung von Arbeitsplätzen um jeden Preis. (…) Die Mobilität der Arbeitskräfte, die von der klassischen Theorie unterstellt wird, gibt es (…) auf modernen Arbeitsmärkten nicht. Einerseits sind die Arbeitnehmer sesshaft geworden und können und wollen nicht alle paar Monate umziehen, um sich einen neuen Arbeitsplatz zu suchen. Andererseits ist auch den Unternehmen daran gelegen, gut eingearbeitete Fachkräfte zu halten, weil die Suchkosten auf ihrer Seite u.U. sehr hoch sind. Folglich haben die Gewerkschaften in einigen Ländern in den 1950er- und 1960er-Jahren des vergangenen Jahrhunderts angefangen, Tarifverträge zu vereinbaren, die Gehaltsstrukturen und Lohnsteigerungen über ganze Branchen oder – via Zusammenarbeit verschiedener Gewerkschaften – gar über die Gesamtwirtschaft hinweg ähnlich regeln. Diese Flächentarifverträge sind nichts anderes als ein funktionales Äquivalent zur Mobilität der Arbeitskräfte in einer Welt, in der die Arbeitskräfte nicht mehr so mobil sind. (…) Trotz einer worauf auch immer zurückzuführenden Immobilität der Arbeitskräfte kann dem Gesetz des „gleichen Lohns für gleiche Arbeit“ Geltung verschafft werden. Am besten gewährleistet dies ein Flächentarifvertrag mit möglichst wenigen Ausnahmen. Nur in einem solchen …

title: "Terrorizing Our City": ICE Targets Immigrants in Danbury, CT, Including at School Bus Stops
content:
We go to Danbury, Connecticut, where residents held a mass demonstration this week to protest recent immigration arrests and to support the city’s immigrant community. Danbury, like many other communities across the United States, has been the target of a spike in immigration enforcement under the Trump administration, including local reports of

ICE

 arresting parents at school bus stops.


“We really have been describing it as the administration terrorizing our city, because that is what it felt like. The streets were empty. Kids stayed home from practice. Kids stayed home from school,” says Juliana Soares, the lead organizer for Danbury Unites for Immigrants. “Masked agents often would shut down the street to just abduct people. … They just do a gross display of force and intimidation in a grocery store parking lot, where they’re just walking around, kind of hunting their next target.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Arctic Talent: Pang rapper fights the power
content:
Residential schools, prisons, hospitals, rehab, psychiatric admissions, the foster system — for Iqaluit-based rapper Jeremy Young, these represent cycles of colonization in which Inuit remain trapped.


“Indigenous people live very institutionalized lives,” the 26-year-old artist said. “Just because you see an Indigenous person walking around free doesn’t mean they are not stuck in a cycle of institutionalization.”


That’s the theme of

Institutionalized

, an original rap song Young performs live on stage and in the streets, accompanied by a wireless speaker.


“It’s like that’s our role in life as Inuit — to be a permanent underclass,” he said. “Don’t be ridiculous. We are an amazing people. We are strong.”


Originally from Pangnirtung, Young’s early artistic and political vision grew out of a summer 2017 trip to Greenland with the Students on Ice Foundation, a charitable organization that connects youth between Nunavut and Kalaallit, Greenland.


Ever since, Young has imagined an independent Inuit state combining the regions.


”It is the same Arctic — the same Inuit, just a different colonial language,” he said.


Young describes his artistic journey, in which he blends hip hop with a call for Indigenous liberation.


Spring 2017:

 West Coast rapper Kendrick Lamar drops his critically acclaimed track

Humble

 — a critique of superficiality in rhyme — and 17-year-old Young is hooked on hip hop.


Young shares Lamar’s conviction at the time that art can save the world.


“It is the reason I found direction,” Young said. “I put everything into becoming a rapper.”


Fall 2017:

 Young moves to Iqaluit, “the big city,” and is smacked with culture shock.


“The kids were more like city kids from down south,” he said.


“It was hard.”


Young blares politically conscious old-school 1990s hip hop.


His peers vibe to trap music, an offshoot musical genre featuring a distinct percussion style and tendency towards themes of poverty and drugs.


Winter 2018:

 Young writes his first original rap song. He pens two dozen more over the years.


Spring 2021:

 Ground-penetrating radar locates an estimated 215 potential burial sites at the former Kamloops Indian Residential School in British Columbia.


“That was a turning point for me,” Young said. “I found it was too important to be just an artist.”


Also disturbed by the murder of George Floyd by Minneapolis police officers a year earlier, Young dives into the political theory of 1960s Black Panther co-founder

Huey P. Newton and the

 

The Autobiography of Malcolm X.


”He talks about the nuts and bolts of how to start a revolution,” Young said.


Summer 2022:

 Young performs live for the first time at The Chartroom Lounge. He spits out the song

All Caps

, a nod to graffiti taggers by the late underground British-American rapper MF DOOM.


”I’ve never looked back,” Young said. “Through the lens of storytelling in hip hop, I realized I come from an amazing storytelling culture.”


Fall 2022-Spring 2026:

 Young haunts local open mics, performing up to five songs per night.


Summer 2026:

 Young meets his hero, John Amagoalik, the father of Nunavut, at the Inuit Circumpolar Council General Assembly.


”He is a huge inspiration to me as someone who wants to create our own Inuit state,” Young said.


Talent Tip:

 “I practice a song for 10 hours before I perform it onstage.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "They Got Zero Notice": 2,500 Workers Laid Off as Tyson Foods Shutters Meatpacking Plant in Illinois
content:
Tyson Foods, the United States’ largest meatpacking and processing company, shuttered a beef processing facility in Joslin, Illinois, last month, laying off more than 2,500 primarily immigrant workers “virtually overnight.” Although Tyson Foods

CEO

 and President Donnie King made over $34 million last year, nearly 800 times more than the median Tyson worker, the company cites a historic 75-year low in the U.S. cattle herd as a primary reason for the closure.


We speak to Caitlyn Clark, director of the group Essential Workers for Democracy, which is working to institute democratic reforms within the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (

UFCW

), a labor union that represents more than a million workers across the United States. These workers include the former Tyson plant meatpackers, who worked in “some of the most dangerous jobs in America” while making “billions of dollars in profit for Tyson.” Clark ascribes the U.S. cattle shortage to climate change-induced drought in the American West, rising prices for diesel and fertilizer amid the U.S. war on Iran and years of corporate consolidation that has driven down profits for cattle ranchers.


Since they were suddenly laid off, former Joslin plant workers have been protesting outside the shuttered plant, calling on Tyson “to extend their severance pay, and calling on Illinois Governor JB Pritzker to intervene to help keep the plant open,” Clark tells us. “We need to take on the bosses and be serious about the level of inequality and exploitation that working people are facing today,” she adds. “Working people need more, they deserve more, and they’re ready to fight for it. It’s time that our union leadership catch up.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Stanford Student Newspaper Wins Suit over Trump's Crackdown on Pro-Palestine Speech
content:
A federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration violated the constitutional rights of international students in seeking to deport them for their pro-Palestinian activism and criticism of Israel. The ruling is the result of a lawsuit filed by

The Stanford Daily

, the student newspaper at Stanford University, which claimed that some of its writers on student visas declined to report on topics related to Israel and Palestine, or requested their published articles be removed from the paper’s website, for fear of deportation.


“What we were hearing from the noncitizens in our newsroom and from noncitizens across campus — current students, former students, alumni — was that they were genuinely frightened because of what they saw in the headlines, what they saw happen to Rümeysa Öztürk,” says George Porteous, editor-in-chief of

The Stanford Daily

. Rümeysa Öztürk is the former Tufts University graduate student arrested and detained by

ICE

 after co-authoring an op-ed encouraging Tufts to divest from Israel in her university’s student newspaper.


“The chill is the point,” adds Will Creeley, legal director at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, or

FIRE

, the organization that represented

The Stanford Daily

 in court. “That’s a First Amendment violation every day of the week. It’s flatly un-American.”

title: Kurdish people renew pledge to carry on the struggle of the martyrs
content:
Mothers of the martyrs in Van (Wan) welcomed their loved ones with the words: “Our condolences to the Kurdish people and Abdullah Öcalan. We welcome our martyrs with pride. We will carry the banner they left us to victory and continue their struggle.” The scenes at the commemoration in Van once again reflected the reality of a people who resist and struggle. Through their stance, the Kurdish people created a scene that will remain etched in collective memory. The ululations of the mothers and the slogans of Van’s youth reverberated throughout the gathering. Pain, anger and hope for a free future were experienced simultaneously, with the intensity of the darkest days of war. Pride, a determination to uphold their legacy and a desire for retribution were present at the same time and in the same place. Through his 53-year struggle, Abdullah Öcalan built a people capable of resisting and of finding ways to continue their struggle even amid war. This spirit was visible throughout Van.


The Serhed region has endured countless tragedies and massacres over the past century. Yet it has never ceased to be a centre of resistance and popular uprisings; on the contrary, it has played a leading role throughout every period of the national struggle and remained an important arena of resistance. The emergence of the Kurdish Freedom Movement further strengthened this tradition through organisation. Even in the most difficult periods, the people of Van joined the struggle with a determination that became a source of strength for Kurds and the people of Kurdistan as a whole. The city of Van contributed thousands of courageous young people to the Kurdish people’s struggle. The commemorations held in the city reflected this legacy in every respect.


Kurdish youth entered the commemoration chanting “Şehîd namirin, Bijî Serok Apo (A.Öcalan)” (Martyrs never die, long live Apo) and pledged to uphold the legacy of those who had lost their lives. The stance of Van’s youth became a source of hope for the future of the Kurdish people. Abdullah Öcalan laid the foundations of this spirit of commitment 53 years ago, and today it has become a philosophy of life embraced throughout society.


At the commemoration for the martyrs in Van, mothers spoke of them in the following words:


“We are proud of them; they fought for freedom and dignity and fell courageously. There is no more honourable path or way of life than this. We will uphold their struggle. The entire Kurdish people must honour the sacrifices made by the martyrs.”


These words evoked a painful chapter in history: the Geliyê Zilan Massacre. During the massacre, when soldiers of the Turkish state beheaded Mother Gulnaz’s son and brought his head before her, she proudly lifted it, kissed it and said:


“I gave birth to this son for days such as these, and I am proud of his resistance. My son resisted you for the cause of his people.”


With these words, she faced the death of her son. Mother Gulnaz’s response left the Turkish soldiers astonished. They had expected her to mourn her son and be overwhelmed by grief, but her response instead embodied the resilience and defiance of Kurdish women.


The Kurdish people are now taking ownership of their future


The mothers of Kurdistan know what stance to take in the face of the occupying forces. The losses and deaths experienced in Kurdistan have also given rise to an ideological and political stance. History repeated itself once again through the mothers of Van (Wan). The commemoration held in Van represented a continuation of this stance and determination. Abdullah Öcalan has examined the history of the Kurdish people in all its dimensions and has built a Kurdish consciousness capable of changing the course of history.


Periods of mourning in Kurdistan have brought Kurdish society closer together and strengthened its attachment to the values it holds sacred. This coming together and sense of commitment have brought about fundamental changes in the sociology of Kurdish society. These changes are, of course, the result of Abdullah Öcalan’s 53 years of struggle and resistance. A people once struggling against the threat of annihilation have now broken the chains of subjugation and taken ownership of their own future.

title: Father of Leyla and Welat: I am proud of my children
content:
The past two weeks have been extremely difficult for Kurdish families. As discussions over the Framework Law continue, families have received news that children they had waited years to see again, holding on to the hope of being reunited through a just peace, had lost their lives.


Condolence gatherings and commemorations organised in Istanbul under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER) honoured guerrillas of the People’s Defence Forces (HPG) and the Free Women’s Units (YJA Star) with chants of “Şehîd Namirin” (Martyrs never die). The silent tears of their families carried the pain and sacrifices of many years.


MEBYA-DER Third Region Co-chair Bahattin Bingöl, who has been among those providing the strongest support to families during this difficult period and who himself lost his two children, Leyla and Welat Bingöl, in the Kurdish Freedom Struggle, spoke to ANF.


Years of persecution: Village burnings, torture and forced displacement


Bahattin Bingöl, whose son Welat lost his life in Dersim and daughter Leyla in Kobanê, has a family history that offers just one example of the lived experiences illustrating the cause-and-effect relationship at the heart of the Kurdish question. Bingöl served as the headman of Şilana village in the Kop (Bulanık) district of Muş (Mûş). His village was burned down in 1994 after residents refused the state’s demand that they join the village guard system.


Bingöl, who was forced to leave for Kop with his family at short notice, described what they experienced: “My son Welat was only a few days old. Our village was burned down because we refused the state’s demand that we become village guards. I will never forget it. It was 12 April 1994, and soldiers raided our village early in the morning. The village had a population of 294 at the time, and everyone was forced to leave, just as we were. They too had to move to Bulanık. The pressure was so intense that families who had rented homes for a year were being forcibly evicted after just 15 days.


In 1999, I served as a member of the Muş Provincial General Council in Bulanık. I was detained hundreds of times during this period. I was held for days in the basements and laundry rooms of detention centres and subjected to every kind of torture imaginable, from being suspended by the arms in the ‘Palestinian hanging’ position to beatings on the soles of my feet. State security forces constantly threatened me, saying, ‘Either you will love it or you will go to the mountains.’


As the pressure and torture intensified in the 2000s, I was once again forced to migrate, this time taking my entire family to Istanbul.”


My children were deeply affected, shaping their political path


Bingöl, a father of eight, said Welat and Leyla, like his other children, grew up under state pressure and were deeply affected by what they experienced. He said that when they attended school in Muş as children, speaking Kurdish was prohibited, as it was in many schools across Kurdistan: “All children attending school in Kurdistan faced immense pressure, both through deprivation in education and for speaking Kurdish, their mother tongue. My children witnessed the denial of Kurdish identity and saw me repeatedly detained and tortured. They were deeply affected by this, and it shaped their political path. Welat went to the mountains first, followed by Leyla.”


We buried Leyla and Welat side by side in Bulanık


Bingöl also said: “Leyla lost her life on 7 October 2014 during the fighting against ISIS in Kobanê. Welat also lost his life in Dersim in 2018. The last time I spoke to Leyla was by phone while she was in Rojava, but we were never able to communicate with Welat. My brother’s and sister’s children were also there during the intense fighting in Kobanê. We therefore kept vigil at the border, hoping to receive news from them. I learned there that Leyla had lost her life. It was only six months later that I was able to receive her remains. I did not learn that Welat had lost his life until two months after his death. A month after providing DNA samples, we retrieved Welat’s remains from the Cemetery of the Unclaimed in Malatya. We buried Leyla and Welat side by side in the Bulanık district of Muş.”

author: Unknown
title: More than 100 activists call for an end to executions in Iran
content:
More than 100 former political prisoners, politicians, human rights activists, journalists, and civil society activists from Iran and abroad issued a joint letter titled “End Imperialist Wars and State Executions.” The letter was signed by numerous international figures, including Angela Davis, Judith Butler, Kiana Yamata Taylor, and Rashid Khalidi, as well as many academics and lawyers.


The signatories stressed that the Iranian people should not be forced to choose between “external military and economic aggression” and “state repression.” They called for an end to executions, the release of political prisoners, an end to the war, and an end to the “collective punishment” of the Iranian people.


The letter also stated that describing the conditions in Iran as “two sides of the same coin” does not mean that war and domestic repression are the same thing, nor that people are affected by both forms of oppression in the same way or at the same time.


The signatories rejected the use of the suffering of the Iranian people to justify either foreign military intervention or domestic repression. They condemned the criminalization of protests and the opposition, the extraction of confessions under coercion, the prosecution of demonstrators, and the execution of detainees on baseless charges.


Among the signatories are Mohammad Habibi, spokesperson for the Iranian Teachers’ Trade Association; writer Reza Khandan; sociologist and former political prisoner Saeed Madani; filmmaker Shahrzad Arshadi; Mansour Beikish of the Khavaran Families; former political prisoner Atena Daemi; Janet Afary; Touraj Atabaki; Hamid Akbari; Nayereh Tohidi; Fatemeh Shams; and Parastou Forouhar.

title: Armut als Mileis Erfolg: Argentinien hat die niedrigsten Löhne in Lateinamerika und einen Mindestlohn unter dem von 2001
content:
Dossier


„

Argentinische Arbeitnehmer erhalten die niedrigsten Löhne in Lateinamerika, und der Rückgang ist historisch, so ein Bericht des Lateinamerikanischen Strategiezentrums für Geopolitik (Celag). Im September 2025 lag der Realmindestlohn unter dem Niveau von 2001, vor dem Zusammenbruch der Konvertibilität. In der Casa Rosada gibt man zu, dass die Regierung von Javier Milei das Einkommen der Arbeiter als“Anker der Anpassung und der Verlangsamung der Inflation“ benutzt hat. Und die Zahlen belegen dies.Die Celag hat herausgefunden, dass der argentinische Mindestlohn (Stand November 2025) der niedrigste in der gesamten Region ist. Mit nur 225 Dollar rangiert er am unteren Ende der Tabelle, hinter Bolivien, Paraguay und weit hinter Costa Rica, das mit 729 Dollar an der Spitze liegt. (…) Ein Bericht der Facultad de Ciencias Económicas de la UBA weist zudem darauf hin, dass der Salario Mínimo, Vital y Móvil zwischen November 2023 und September 2025 34 % seiner Kaufkraft verlieren wird

Immer mehr Argentinier brauchen Kredite für Essen und Kleidung


„

Die ultraliberale Politik des argentinischen Präsidenten Javier Milei bringt immer mehr Argentinier wegen sinkender Reallöhne in Zahlungsnöte.


Argentiniens rechtslibertärer Präsident Javier Milei hat eine neue soziale Gruppe geschaffen. Seit Monaten steigt deren Angehörigenzahl. Inzwischen sind es mehr als 5,8 Millionen Argentinier*innen und damit rund 12,5 Prozent der Bevölkerung. Schnell hatte der Volksmund auch einen Namen für sie gefunden: »los Morosos«. Salopp übersetzt: die Zahlungsunfähigen. »Mora« oder »Morosidad« bezeichnet im Spanischen den Zahlungsverzug bei Kreditraten. Nach dem jüngsten Bericht der argentinischen Zentralbank lag die Ausfallquote bei Bankkrediten privater Haushalte im Juni 2026 bei knapp 13 Prozent. Im Juni des Vorjahres lag der Wert noch bei 5,2 Prozent. Besonders betroffen sind Konsumentenkredite und Kreditkarten. (…) Staatliche Hilfen in welcher Form auch immer hat der Präsident kategorisch ausgeschlossen. Für Milei ist das »eine Angelegenheit zwischen Privaten«. (…) Seit dem Amtsantritt von Milei sind die realen Löhne der registrierten Beschäftigten um 3,6 Prozent gesunken. (…) Die Zahlungsprobleme beschränken sich längst nicht mehr auf private Haushalte. Auch Unternehmen geraten zunehmend unter Druck. Laut einem Bericht des argentinischen Industrieverbandes (UIA) stieg die Ausfallquote bei Industrieunternehmen von 0,7 Prozent im Dezember 2024 auf 3,8 Prozent im Juni 2026. Was sich nach einem geringen Anstieg anhört, ist das Fünffache innerhalb von nur anderthalb Jahren. Und die Tendenz weist weiter nach oben. (…) Noch eine andere Entwicklung bereitet Sorgen. Wo der Staat sich zurückzieht, füllen meist illegale Gruppierungen das Vakuum. Das ist nicht neu und lässt sich in nahezu allen lateinamerikanischen Ländern beobachten. Doch seit Milei den Staat massiv abbaut, beschleunigt sich diese Entwicklung in Argentinien. Die Narcos in den Armenvierteln sind nicht mehr nur Verkäufer illegaler Drogen. Sie entwickeln sich zu informellen Kreditgebern und Glücksspielbetreibern. Dabei verleihen sie Geld nicht direkt. Sie bauen ein Netzwerk aus Nachbarn, Freunden, Verwandten und Bekannten auf, die als Vermittler fungieren. Die Einbringung eines Gesetzentwurfs zur Unterstützung verschuldeter und säumiger Familien im Abgeordnetenhaus wurde mit den Stimmen der die Regierung unterstützenden Abgeordneten Ende August verhindert. Dagegen beschloss das Abgeordnetenhaus in der gleichen Sitzung eine Reform der Statuten der Zentralbank. Sollte der Senat ebenfalls dafür stimmen, werden künftig deren Dollarreserven als Garantie für eine Refinanzierung staatlicher Auslandsschulden verwendet. Auf argentinischer Seite federführend sind zwei ehemalige Angestellte der US-Bank J.P. Morgan: der heutige Wirtschaftsminister Luis Caputo und der Zentralbankchef Santiago Bausili, die den Deal mit den internationalen Gläubigerbanken verhandeln. Vom Tisch ist die von Milei im Wahlkampf vollmundig angekündigte Abschaffung der Zentralbank.“

content:
Milli Savunma Bakanlığı (MSB) Silivri'de kazaya karıştıktan sonra batan "Tuğberk İmamoğlu" isimli geminin yerinin tespit edildiğini açıkladı.

Silivri açıklarındaki gemi kazasında iki kaptan tutuklandı

"Alsu"da ağır hasar oluşmazken Tuğberk İmamoğlu battı. Gemide bulunan 10 personel kazadan bu yana kayıp.

Soruşturma kapsamında "Alsu" gemisinde gözaltına alınıp adliyeye sevk edilen 6 kişiden geminin 1'inci kaptanı Ahmet Erarslan ile 3'üncü kaptan Murat Evciman tutuklanırken, 4 kişi adli kontrolle serbest bırakıldı.

title: İstanbul Üniversitesi tabldot küçülttü: Öğrencinin yemeğine yüzde 33’lük zam
content:
İstanbul Üniversitesi 2026-2027 akademik yılının başlangıcı öncesi yemekhane ücretlerine yüzde 33 zam yaptı. Öğün bedeli 52,50 TL’den 70 TL’ye yükseltti.


Okul yönetimi Eylül 2025’te yemekhane ücretini yüzde 50’lik artışla 35 TL’den 52,50 TL’ye çıkartmıştı.


Böylece kampüs yemekhanesinde bir öğün yemeğin bedeli son bir senede yüzde 100 artmış oldu.


"Okumak için çalışmak zorundayız"


Günün büyük bölümünü kampüste geçiren öğrenciler için yemekhane, en temel yaşam alanlarından biri. Ancak artan maliyetler, öğrencilerin günlük yaşam alışkanlıklarını da değiştiriyor.


Kampüsteki durumu değerlendiren İstanbul Üniversitesi Tarih Bölümü son sınıf öğrencisi Salih B., üç-dört yıl öncesine kıyasla akşam yemeği için okulda bekleyen öğrenci sayısının azaldığını belirtiyor.


Öğrencilerin beslenme ihtiyaçlarını ertelemek ya da geçiştirmek zorunda kaldığını kaydeden Salih B.,

 "Evde kalan öğrenciler eve gidene kadar açlığını erteliyor, yurtta kalanlar ise su ısıtıcısı (kettle) veya cezvede noodle yaparak karınlarını doyurmaya çalışıyor"

 dedi.


Yemekhane zamlarının artık bir "dönem başı ritüeline" dönüştüğünü ifade eden Salih B., sorunun yalnızca yemek ücretiyle sınırlı kalmadığını ekledi:


"2022’de üniversiteye başladığım ilk gün yemekhaneye gittiğimde aklıma Sibel Ünli gelmişti. O günden bugüne üniversitede yemek hâlâ ücretsiz ve ulaşılabilir değil; üstelik artık çok daha pahalı. Sorun yalnızca 70 liralık yemek değil; öğrencilerin barınmak, beslenmek ve okuyabilmek için sürekli çalışmak zorunda bırakılması."


Öğrencinin 5 yılda 128 öğünü çalındı


Eylül 2021’de 650 TL olan KYK lisans bursu ile kampüs yemekhanesinde 185 öğün yemek yenebilirken, 2026 itibarıyla 4 bin TL’ye yükselen bursa rağmen alınabilen öğün sayısı 57’ye geriledi.


Böylece öğrencinin aylık bursunun karşılayabildiği yemek miktarı son 5 yıl içerisinde toplam 128 öğün azaldı.


2021'den bu yana geçen 5 yılda KYK bursu yaklaşık 6,1 katına çıkarken, aynı dönemde yemekhane ücreti 3,50 TL'den 70 TL'ye yükselerek 20 katına ulaştı.

title: Agenda cultural: primera semana de septiembre
content:
Hoy comienza el festival en el CAFF, donde se presentan las mejores bandas de Tango. Y hasta el 06 de septiembre continúa el de la Revista Llegás, con más de 500 artistas y 50 funciones a mitad de precio. Hay mucho para ver, gratuito o a precios módicos. 

No dejes de recorrer nuestra agenda, hay mucho para ver, pensar, disfrutar. Elegí compartir cultura. Si tenes propuestas, podés enviarlas a nuestor mail: culturasanred@gmail.com. Revisamos la casilla hasta el lunes previo a la publicación.

Por ANRed.


Jueves 03


FACAFF. 

Octava edición del multitudinario encuentro donde

más de veinte agrupaciones ofrecen una mirada auténtica e innovadora del tango actual

.  Va del jueves 03 al domingo 27 de septiembre en el Club Atlético Fernández Fierro (CAFF), Bustamante 772, CABA. Entradas populares en efectivo en boletería del club o por PlanOut.

Jubiladxs entrada sin cargo y promoción 2×1 para estudiantes.

Acá, toda la programación que necesitás para no perderte nada de este Festival increíble:

www.caff.ar


9° Edición del Festival Llegás.

Este año reunirá más de

50 obras de la cartelera teatral

 de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires con entradas a mitad de precio. Durante una semana, 

más de 500 artistas

 participarán de una programación que se desplegará en 10 salas de la Ciudad para celebrar el encuentro entre artistas, obras y espectadores. En esta edición, el Festival incorpora clases magistrales, actividades especiales, un circuito de obras en espacios no convencionales, espectáculos invitados y producciones seleccionadas mediante convocatoria, además de una amplia selección de propuestas del circuito comercial.

Todas las funciones tendrán entradas a mitad de precio, con el objetivo de ampliar el acceso a las artes escénicas.

 El Festival Llegás es una iniciativa de Revista Llegás, coproducida junto a LEM Asociación Civil, que busca visibilizar las artes escénicas, promover el trabajo interdisciplinario y fortalecer la gestión del arte en la sociedad. «El festival no es el fin: el festival es un medio para generar encuentro. Las obras nos convocan, pero lo que permanece es el encuentro. Queremos compartir una experiencia que nos cambie. Lxs esperamos en esta novena edición del Festival Llegás con el mismo espíritu festivo de siempre. La cultura nos encuentra», expresan Ricardo Tamburrano y Melina Seldes, directores y curadores del festival. Las entradas ya están a la venta en el sitio web oficial del Festival Llegás. Allí puede consultarse la programación completa, los horarios, las sedes y

toda la información sobre esta novena edición:

 

www.festival-llegas.com.ar

.

una de las bandas más importantes del hardcore punk latinoamericano

. Integrada por Guillermo Marmol (voz), Roy Ota (guitarra), Alejandro Navajas (bajo), Tomás Portela (guitarra) y Germán Rodríguez (batería), combina melodías con

letras de contenido social

 desde la ética del Do It Yourself y la autogestión. Con nueve discos de estudio, un disco en vivo y un DVD, giró por Chile, Uruguay, Perú, Colombia, Ecuador, España, Francia, Suiza y Brasil, y hoy atraviesa uno de sus mejores momentos, celebrando los 25 años de su álbum

A Los Que Se Han Apagado

.


Viernes 04


Mala Madre. 

Una obra documental sobre maternidad, duelo y deseo. Relato de una madre que atravesada por la muerte temprana de su hermano, revisa su historia personal para poner en crisis los mandatos, culpas y contradicciones que rodean a la maternidad. A partir de su historia personal y de material audiovisual registrado durante años, la pieza indaga en las zonas menos idealizadas de maternar. Laa obra abre una conversación íntima y colectiva. Protagonizada por la multipremiada actriz 

Raquel Ameri

 y con dirección de 

Paola Luttini.

Se estrena el viernes 4 de septiembre 22.30 HS en Nün Teatro Bar (Juan Ramírez de Velasco, 419, CABA).

Entradas por Alternativa.


Alabanza

. Una performance audiovisual que explora los estados físicos y emocionales del ciclo menstrual. Una investigación escénica que tensiona lo íntimo y lo colectivo, donde los cuerpos se transforman, se expanden, se repliegan y vuelve a comenzar, reivindicando sus naturalezas cíclicas como forma de existencia, percepción y potencia …

author: Unknown
title: Jerusalem Post: İran savaşı için borçlu gençler orduya alınsın
content:
The Jerusalem Post’ta Kanadalı eski asker AJ Jaff imzasıyla yayımlanan “İran’la savaş hava saldırılarıyla kazanılmayacak, peki geriye ne kaldı?” başlıklı makalede, ABD’nin İran’a yönelik savaşı ve olası kara harekâtı seçenekleri ele alındı.

Makalede, ABD’nin İran’a yönelik savaşta aylar süren hava saldırılarına rağmen hedeflerine ulaşamadığı savunuldu. 2003’te Irak’a yönelik hava saldırılarından bu yana gerçekleştirdiği en yoğun bombardımanlardan birini İran’a düzenleyen ABD’nin buna rağmen istediği sonucu alamadığı ileri sürüldü.

ABD yönetiminin savaşı Amerikan kamuoyuna kabul ettirmekte de zorlandığı belirtilen makalede, İran’a yönelik olası bir kara harekâtının ise çok daha büyük bir askerî güç gerektireceği savunuldu.

Makalede, İran’ın 31 eyalet komutanlığı ve “Mozaik Savunma Doktrini”ne karşı başarılı bir kara harekâtı için 750 bin ila 1,5 milyon arasında askere ihtiyaç duyulabileceği öne sürüldü.

ABD ordusunun mevcut aktif personel sayısının ise yaklaşık 452 bin olduğu belirtilerek, “Açıkçası, bu hesap tutmuyor” değerlendirmesi yapıldı.

Makalede, ihtiyaç duyulduğu öne sürülen asker sayısına ulaşmak için Amerikan gençlerinin borçlarının silinmesi karşılığında orduya alınması önerildi.

Yazıda, 18-34 yaş arasındaki Amerikalıların öğrenci kredileri, kredi kartları, otomobil kredileri ve kişisel krediler dahil olmak üzere ortalama 40 bin doların üzerinde ipotek dışı borç taşıdığı, bazı tahminlerde bu miktarın 100 bin dolara kadar çıktığı savunuldu.

Makalede Pentagon’un ihtiyaç duyduğu insan kaynağının bu borçlu gençler olduğu ileri sürülerek, 24 veya 36 aylık askerlik hizmetinin ardından öğrenci kredileri, kredi kartı borçları ve diğer borçların tamamen silinmesini öngören federal bir program önerildi.

Öneride ayrıca böyle bir programın, mevcut Gaziler Yasası kapsamındaki eğitim desteğinin genişletilmesiyle birlikte uygulanması halinde gönüllü asker alımını artırabileceği savunuldu.

Makalede borçların silinmesi karşılığında askerlik hizmetinin teşvik edilmesinin, ABD devletinin ihtiyaç duyduğu askerî personeli sağlamak için geçmişte başvurduğu yöntemlerin bir devamı olduğu savunuldu.

Yazıda bu yöntem için, “Bu, Amerikan devletinin, başka türlü temin edemediği personele ihtiyaç duyduğunda her zaman yaptığı şeyi yapmasıdır” ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Makalede ABD’nin İran’a yönelik savaşta başvurabileceği seçenekler yalnızca asker toplama önerisiyle sınırlı tutulmadı.

İran’ın parçalanmasına yönelik senaryoların da ele alındığı yazıda, ülkedeki farklı etnik grupların merkezi yönetime karşı kışkırtılması ve ABD Kongresi’nin bu grupların bağımsızlığını tanıması gibi öneriler sıralandı.

Böylece makalede, İran’a yönelik hava saldırılarının sonuç vermemesi halinde ABD’nin önünde kara harekâtının yanı sıra ülke içerisindeki etnik ve siyasi fay hatlarını kullanmaya dayalı seçeneklerin bulunduğu savunuldu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Andrea DiP
title: A violência como promessa em ano eleitoral – com Bruno Paes Manso
content:
Quais as consequências quando o discurso de incentivo aos linchamentos deixa as redes sociais e ganha as ruas? Como os candidatos da direita têm usado o medo para incentivar o uso da violência no combate aos problemas históricos de

segurança pública

? Por que a ideia de fazer justiça com as próprias mãos vem ganhando tanta força neste ano eleitoral?


Para falar sobre esses assuntos, o Pauta Pública desta semana recebe o jornalista e pesquisador Bruno Paes Manso, autor dos livros “A República das Milícias” e “A Fé e o Fuzil”. Na conversa com Andrea Dip, Paes Manso reflete sobre os discursos que associam violência à produção de ordem e comenta o recente caso de Cláudio Rafael Landeiro, ciclista que foi acusado injustamente de roubar uma bicicleta e morreu após ser linchado nas ruas de Copacabana, no Rio de Janeiro.

author: dialogocomospovos
title: Analise de Conjuntura - Mestre Joelson
content:
Mestre Joelson Ferreira oferece uma análise de conjuntura que situa o momento atual como um ponto de inflexão histórica. Para ele, a humanidade atravessa uma crise profunda, marcada por sofrimento e destruição, mas também pelo amanhecer de um mundo multipolar. Esse novo cenário, em sua visão, rompe com a hegemonia unipolar e abre espaço para a construção de uma nova civilização, baseada em princípios distintos do modelo predatório vigente.


Central em seu discurso é a necessidade de saldar duas dívidas históricas no Brasil: uma com os povos originários, guardiões ancestrais da terra, e outra com a diáspora africana, trazida à força para o trabalho escravo. Mestre Joelson argumenta que o pagamento dessas dívidas não se resume à reparação material, mas exige um amplo projeto de transformação social que inclui educação, saúde, terra e moradia. Ele critica veementemente o modelo capitalista e a perspectiva eurocêntrica, responsáveis pela destruição ambiental e pela desigualdade, propondo em seu lugar um modo de vida inspirado nos saberes ancestrais.


A reconstrução do Brasil, em sua perspectiva, é uma tarefa coletiva e política que deve envolver universidades, escolas e movimentos sociais. Ele vislumbra um futuro onde a agroecologia e o conhecimento tradicional se combinem para criar uma sociedade harmônica e sustentável. A luta, portanto, é contra a elite racista capitalista e pela restituição da terra e da natureza, num grande mutirão nacional que celebre a riqueza e a diversidade do povo brasileiro.

author: Unknown
title: Mustafa Karasu: The doors of Imralı must be opened - Part Three
content:
KCK Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu spoke to journalist Erdal Er during a special program on Medya Haber, and made important assessments on current developments.


The first part of the interview can be found 

here

 and the second

here

.


In recent days, a number of meeting notes or transcripts attributed to Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan were published on various social media platforms – more than one set. First, transcripts purported to be notes from meetings between the Imrali delegation and Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan were published. Let’s start there. A statement also came from the DEM Party’s Imrali delegation. “The notes have been tampered with,” they said. We’ve seen this before. Take the Oslo process, the previous peace process, and now this. The time and place change, but the method remains the same. What is your assessment of this? Are these notes the same ones you have? Do you have such notes in your possession? Are they accurate or not? I’d like to hear your assessment on this.


There are opponents of the process. There is also a struggle in this regard. It’s not just a process taking place between us and the state officials who speak with Rêber Apo on Imrali. There are also opponents who genuinely want to derail the process. They want to sabotage it. These are not ordinary matters. They exist within the state as well. Outside the state, there are also certain political parties and institutions involved. In this regard, if you look closely at the so-called “meeting notes” – whatever the documents, papers, or minutes may be – you’ll see they were published during the process leading up to the passage of this law, at a time when the process was moving into its second phase. The timing is significant; it could not be prevented, and it will continue to develop, entering a new phase. This is being targeted for sabotage. It is a provocation. They are trying to provoke the process. Some of these meetings have been reported on before. Yes, there are some dialogues from the meeting held there, but the main issue is that they are trying to create a certain perception by distorting certain dialogues and other details. They’re taken out of context. They’re sharing some of the things discussed at Imrali, but alongside that, they’re adding content of their own – ones they think will provoke and muddy the waters – in an attempt to create a provocation. There are also minutes of supposed meetings that never took place.


I’ll get to the part regarding your actions in a moment, but first, regarding the state and government channels – which you’ve pointed out as having significant timing and which you’ve described as provocative – when we look at the past, specifically the Oslo process and the subsequent peace process, it creates the impression that information was leaked as if it originated from you or from someone on your side. On this matter, do you have any findings or evidence regarding where the leaks are coming from or how they’re happening? What is your assessment of this? Are these notes only in your possession?


First of all, it must be noted that all this speculation, provocation, and attempts to sabotage these talks stem, in part, from the inadequacy of the approach being followed. If Rêber Apo were to hold press conferences, if intellectuals were to discuss these matters, and if the views of Rêber Apo were presented to the public, what would that mean? There would be no such provocation. They couldn’t do it. Because the views of Rêber Apo have been clearly presented to the public and discussed with journalists. The entire public has learned this directly from Rêber Apo. In that case, there would be neither speculation nor provocation.


This also stems, to some extent, from the inadequacy of the method. This shows that the government is under pressure, and they are struggling as well. They question why this is happening. Therefore, to eliminate all of this, it is necessary to arrange for Rêber Apo to meet with intellectuals and journalists immediately. It seems as if this is being reflected by us. That is not the case. We absolutely have no role in reflecting their views, nor do we have any interest in doing so. We want to advance this process. We are opposed to those who seek to sabotage the process. These are factors that affect the process.


There’s the saying to look at who benefits from the results of a specific actions.


Such results only serve the interests of …

author: Unknown
title: Çetin Arkaş joins youth gathering in Cologne
content:
Young people from Kurdistan living in Europe will gather in Cologne today to demand the physical freedom of Abdullah Öcalan.


Organisers said the march, which will bring together Kurdish and internationalist young people, will be more than an act of solidarity. They described it as a powerful initiative for freedom that will demonstrate the organised will of young people, their determination to struggle and their commitment to a free future.


At the Cologne march, young people will raise the message, “Öcalan’s freedom is our freedom.” The march will also be held in memory of the recently announced martyrs of the Kurdistan revolution.


A major youth gathering will be held in Cologne on 3 September, one day before the march. Çetin Arkaş, a member of the Imrali Secretariat, will address the young people via a live link.


The programme will include a video presentation featuring protests, events and organising activities carried out by young people from Kurdistan living across Europe. The presentation will highlight their history of struggle and solidarity in Europe, as well as their pursuit of freedom.


Artists Hozan Diyar and Talat Yeşil will also take part in the event, lending their music to the young people’s demand for freedom.


Three-day programme


Young people met on Thursday, 3 September, and today they will march through the streets of Cologne demanding the physical freedom of Abdullah Öcalan. The program will conclude tomorrow, 5 September, with the participation in the 34th Kurdistan Culture Festival in Dortmund.


The three-day program will bring young people together around the demand for Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom, commitment to the legacy of the martyrs of the Kurdistan revolution and the building of a free future. Kurdish and internationalist young people living in different European countries have been called on to join the march and strengthen the struggle for freedom.

author: Unknown
title: Bayık: How you treat a people’s Leader reflects how you treat the people
content:
KCK Executive Council Co-Chair Cemil Bayık answered ANF’s questions about the process.


The Kurdish people have recently been commemorating their martyrs everywhere, particularly in the cities of Bakurê Kurdistan. Memorial gatherings and condolences are being held in many cities. Thousands of people are attending these gatherings and messages are being expressed. On this occasion, what message would you like to convey to Kurdish people, particularly the families of the martyrs?


I extend my condolences to the families of our fallen comrades and to the entire Kurdish people. In particular, commemorations are being held for our martyrs whose deaths were not made public during the intense warfare of recent years. Holding commemorations for the fallen guerrillas during the Peace and Democratic Society Process was necessary for the healthy conduct of the subsequent stages of the process. Because if the process moved forward, the guerrillas’ return to Turkey would become an issue. These commemorations were therefore held to prevent room for different debates and speculation later on. Tens of thousands of our people have participated in these commemorations. They have demonstrated in a very striking way the meaning and value our people attach to the martyrs. At the same time, this expresses the Kurdish people’s commitment to the goals for which these martyrs sacrificed their lives.


Our people are deeply conscious that whatever has been achieved in the name of existence, freedom and democracy has been achieved through the struggle of these self-sacrificing people. The guerrillas waged this struggle and risked their lives on the basis of their commitment to Leader Apo. [Abdullah Öcalan]. For this reason, posters of Leader Apo were carried at the commemorations, and the slogan “Long live Leader Apo” was repeatedly chanted. This stance also represents strong support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process being pursued through Leader Apo’s initiative. Indeed, in every speech, the families of the martyrs have emphasized that the Peace and Democratic Society Process is the result of the martyrs’ struggle. If today Leader Apo is negotiating with the Turkish state for peace and a democratic society, and if the Kurdish question has been brought from the gallows to the negotiating table, it is the struggle of our martyrs that made this possible.


If our martyrs had not made the ultimate sacrifice, our struggle would have been eliminated and would have met the fate of previous Kurdish uprisings. In this respect, it is very important to view the Peace and Democratic Society Process as a process created by the martyrs. The stance of the martyrs’ families is very meaningful. Their stance also has a determining influence on the stance of the Kurdish people. If the Kurdish Freedom Movement has left such a mark on Kurdish life socially and historically, the stance of the martyrs’ families has played a major role in this. The stance of the martyrs’ families and the strong participation of our people in commemorations have demonstrated that the Kurdish people will undoubtedly attain a free and democratic life.


Our martyrs undoubtedly also place a responsibility on the families of the martyrs. This means remaining committed to the goals for which the martyrs gave their lives. If the families of the martyrs properly represent these values, these values will inevitably become concrete in the free and democratic life of the Kurdish people. When the entire Kurdish people remain committed to the values for which our martyrs gave their lives, the future of the Kurdish people will inevitably be free. No force will be able to deprive this people of existence, freedom and democratic life.


How should the legacy of the martyrs be approached? How will commitment to their memory, the values that led them to sacrifice their lives, and their aspirations be kept alive from now on?


Keeping the legacy of the martyrs alive means struggling for the values they sought to achieve. The existence of the Kurdish people has been strongly established. Now this existence must attain a free and democratic life. For this, we must first make the struggle for peace and a democratic society successful. 


This is possible by creating an organized democratic society based on communes. The values created through the martyrs’ struggle can only be protected and developed through an organized society. In this respect, it is necessary to resist the consumerism of …

author: Unknown
title: Öcalan’s views from Imrali would strengthen public support
content:
The adoption of the framework law marked the beginning of the second phase. The board headed by the Vice President also decided to establish four additional committees. Abdullah Öcalan is expected to play an active role in the committee to be established as part of this process, because disarmament cannot take place without such a role. Those who carry arms say: “We will not return unless our leadership plays an active role in this process and guides us not only in going to Turkey, but also in our transition to political life in Turkey.”


Disarmament also directly concerns the leadership of the armed organisation. It will therefore be difficult for the process to proceed and develop in a healthy manner unless the movement’s leadership plays a role and maintains contact with Imrali and the state throughout this period.


It is equally important for Öcalan’s views to be conveyed to the public in Turkey through journalists and intellectuals and for the process to gain broader social support. State officials have indicated, either explicitly or indirectly, that journalists and intellectuals would be allowed to visit Imrali. This had been particularly expected with the beginning of the second phase. Many journalists and intellectuals have applied to interview and meet Öcalan on Imrali, but these requests have still not been granted. There is considerable expectation that such meetings will take place. Without them, it will not be possible to dispel the speculation surrounding the process among various sections of society.


Certain reports have recently appeared on digital media platforms claiming to reveal the content of meetings held on Imrali. It is noteworthy that the platforms publishing these claims are opposed to Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Indeed, the fact that individuals presenting themselves as Kurds began making accusations against Öcalan and the Freedom Movement following this digital media provocation has once again demonstrated why these platforms resort to such tactics.


The Justice and Development Party (AKP) government, however, is creating the conditions for such speculation and provocations by failing to take steps that would allow Abdullah Öcalan’s views to reach the public through journalists and intellectuals. Those responsible for such provocations should, of course, be criticised and condemned. But steps must also be taken to prevent them from carrying out such provocations. This means ensuring that Öcalan’s views are presented openly to the public. Some may criticise what he says in these interviews and meetings. Those criticisms or attempts at defamation can then be answered accordingly. In this way, deliberately constructed narratives and distortions can be prevented.


If journalists and intellectuals are not allowed to meet Öcalan on Imrali, provocations and attempts at sabotage carried out through digital media may come to be seen as something the government itself wants. The government has the power to prevent this. Otherwise, arguments over who leaked the information or where it came from become meaningless. It must be stressed once again that the Kurdish people, the wider public in Turkey and democratic forces want to hear directly from Abdullah Öcalan about his views.


Commemorations held for guerrillas in Kurdish provinces have shown that the Kurdish people fully support the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Mothers and fathers who have lost their children say, “We, too, are part of this country. Let peace and democracy come.” They speak of fraternity with the Turkish people. They also want peace to be honourable and just. The peace being sought must not be “a peace that puts an end to peace.”


The Kurdish people no longer want war, conflict or death. They do not want soldiers, police officers or guerrillas to die. The Peace Mothers say, “Let us join mothers of soldiers and police officers in leading the way towards peace and strengthening Turkish-Kurdish fraternity.” Mothers and fathers with such an outlook, and a people with such aspirations, represent an opportunity for Turkey. It is Abdullah Öcalan who has created this opportunity. If the Turkish people are able to hear Öcalan’s views, they will undoubtedly support the political project he has put forward. Until now, however, these views have been prevented from reaching the people of Turkey. Hopefully, this will no longer be the case.

title: The Paris Commune and the Idea of the State by Mikhail Bakunin
content:
PDFs of article imposed for printing as an A5 saddle-stitched pamphlet. First PDF is a double-sided cover intended to be printed in colour, second is the double-sided inside pages intended to be printed in black and white.

“The message which Bakunin tried to preach was that only the workers could free the workers; in other words, he desired to stimulate the self-activity of the working-class. He was never tired of quoting the celebrated slogan of the First International: “The emancipation of the toilers must be the work of the toilers themselves,” and he expressly excluded from the concept of ‘toilers’ those ex-workers who, having gained the leadership of a working-class movement, endeavour to make themselves masters of it and lead it where they are determined that it shall go. To Bakunin that was not emancipation, it was merely a change of masters. But he wanted the triumph of humanity – a full human development of all in conditions of liberty and equality.” Bakunin's essay is presented with a short biography by K J Kenafick.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Can the Greens Win in Keir Starmer’s Old Seat?
content:
In

one last U-turn

 for the lads, Keir Starmer announced he was stepping down as an MP on Tuesday – convenient timing after he’d just enjoyed nearly seven weeks of paid summer recess. Yes, the man who loved banging on about

“public service”

 decided it was the “right time” to sack off the chore of representing the good people of Holborn and St Pancras.


Starmer said he’ll be leaving parliament

to focus on “international affairs”

, an area he had a decent opportunity to make a difference in as prime minister – namely, fulfilling the UK’s international legal obligations to prevent genocide – but we all know

how that turned out

.


As for Starmer’s plan to “continue [his] work on combatting violence against women and girls”, I’m sure lasses around the world are breathing a big sigh of relief that

the man who appointed Jeffrey Epstein’s “best pal”

 to the top diplomatic role in government is on the case.


His decision to step down has triggered a contest in his London seat – and it could be a spicy one. Green party leader Zack Polanski

signalled his intention to run

 on Thursday, pending approval by the party’s local branch. 


While this could be a risky move for the Greens at a time when they’re vulnerable – the percentage of Brits who say they intend to vote Green fell to 13% in August,

according to YouGov

, down from a high of 21% in March – a win for Polanski could also serve as an energising reset for the party. 


If he’s successful, Polanski will become the Greens’ first London MP (the party already controls four councils in the capital) and gain a renewed mandate to heap pressure from the left onto newly-minted PM Andy Burnham. 


Some of the Greens’ poor recent polling can be attributed to the much-vaunted ‘Burnham bounce’ (although positioning yourself as a charismatic new leader is probably not that hard if you’re following Starmer), while

some is a consequence

 of the media uproar in May around a retweet Polanski made that was critical of how police handled the suspect in the Golders Green stabbing. 


A renewed torrent of negative attention from the mainstream press is basically guaranteed if Polanski is selected to run by local Green members – you know, the kind of scrutiny only seen in the Corbyn era.


Andrew Feinstein – the former South African MP who came second in Starmer’s seat in 2024 as an independent, capitalising on anger over

Labour’s handling of the genocide in Gaza

 – has confirmed he won’t be standing. While the Camden Peoples Alliance (CPA) – the community organisation born out of Feinstein’s 2024 campaign – hasn’t formally decided its position,

Feinstein called this

 “a crucial time for progressives in Camden and across the country to be united” (and this journalist hears that the CPA is likely to endorse Polanski). 


Holborn and St Pancras has been held by Labour continuously since it was created in 1983. At the 2024 general election, Starmer held the seat

 with 48.9% of the vote

, while Feinstein and the Greens came in second and third with 18.9% and 10.4% respectively. The Tories, Reform UK and Lib Dems trailed behind in single digits. 


If the left can get behind one candidate, we’re looking at a two-horse race between a progressive challenger and the establishment party. Camden’s demographics

slant fairly young

 (the average age is in the 30s) with a student population above the national average – both could work in favour of the Greens if they can get people to the polls. 


Polanski has already indicated his priorities,

telling the Camden New Journal:

 “Too often Labour has stood up for corporations and big money. I will stand up for people struggling to pay their bills.” While Burnham has positioned himself as a cost-of-living PM, movement on

water nationalisation is mixed

 and we’re all seeing

energy bills rise (again) next month

. 


Labour’s candidate is tipped to be Camden council leader

Sagal Abdi-Wali

, who immediately became the target of

a racist tweet

from Reform’s unelected

Question Time seatwarmer

 Zia Yusuf. Reform’s team will have less time for tweeting today, as the party scrambles to

limit damage

 from a

Channel 4 and Verbatim Media investigation

revealing a “plot to break the law on party funding at the highest levels”.

author: Trojka
title: Mamy więcej wspólnego z eksmitowanymi niż z milionerami.
content:
Oto kolejna eksmisja na Osiedlu Maltańskim. Chociaż teren został sprzedany za 421 milionów deweloperowi, za eksmisje odpowiada komornik, który działa na zlecenie kurii. W dokumentach sądowych wierzycielem chcącym odzyskać teren jest nadal parafia, która ten teren sprzedała. Takie absurdy tylko w Polsce. Warto to wyjaśnić, bo kościół umywa ręce od bronienia swoich parafian, za to z ochotą przelicza pieniądze i czynnie wspiera działania eksmisyjne. Na bruk w imię Boga.


A co robi miasto Poznań? Miasto Poznań jest jedynym podmiotem, do którego odsyłani są mieszkańcy Osiedla Maltańskiego, którzy starają się o inny lokal mieszkalny. Uszczuplany jest zasób lokali komunalnych i socjalnych, w tym samym czasie kościół i deweloper oszczędzają, cały zysk z obrotu terenem będzie ich. Deweloper nie musi się martwić o zastępcze lokale dla eksmitowanych, zresztą jak już zauważono wyżej, na dziś za cały proces brutalnych eksmisji odpowiada Kościół. Sprzedał teren, ale nadal to on występuje w dokumentach jako wierzyciel. Kto wie może biznesmeni od dewelopera i biznesmeni od sutann tak się dogadali. Pytanie tylko, dlaczego miasto Poznań i jego władze, które od mieszkańców Osiedla pobierały podatki, meldowały ich, pomogły stworzyć osiedlową świetlicę i faktycznie utwierdzało mieszkańców w tym, że stan prawny osiedla jest uregulowany przez władzę, dziś odwracają się od nich i nie starają się im pomóc? W trakcie działań eksmisyjnych nie można było spotkać Dobrosławy Janas, Pełnomocniczki Prezydenta Poznania ds. Ochrony Praw Lokatorów i Projektów Mieszkaniowych, która pełni jednocześnie funkcję Dyrektora Biura Spraw Lokalowych. Bardzo długa i skomplikowana nazwa stanowiska, za którą nie idą realne działania. To akurat symptomatyczne w środowisku prezydenta Jacka Jaśkowiaka, który osobiście, zasłynął głównie w tym konflikcie z szykanowania i powielania fałszywych informacji na temat m.in. jednej z zaangażowanych w protest mieszkanek osiedla.


Na końcu zostajecie wy(czytelnicy), my i wszyscy mieszkańcy Poznania, którzy dajemy się wmanewrować w absurd całej tej sytuacji. Kryzys mieszkaniowy w Polsce to fakt niezaprzeczalny. Stosowane przez aktywistów i aktywistki lokatorskie takie określenia jak „patodeweloperka”, czy „czyściciele kamienic” są dziś powszechnie używane i rozumiane. Pytanie, czy na pewno? Bo każda blokada eksmisji pozwala ujawnić się tym, którzy pytają się o zapisy w księgach wieczystych, umowy, prawo własności. Dzieje się to w kraju, w którym trzeba żebrać o kredyt, pracować ponad siły, lub sprawdzać kurs franka i prosić o litość banku. Nawet jeśli plasujemy się w tej grupie Polaków, którym udało się choćby połowicznie zapewnić własny dach nad głową (pamiętajmy, do czasu spłacenia kredytu nic nie jest jeszcze wasze), to przecież wszystko wisi na włosku. Choroba, utrata pracy, zmiana koniunktury, kryzys, wojna i nagle sytuacja się sypie. Ci którzy są zmuszeni do wynajmowania, powinni już absolutnie rozumieć w jak słabej są sytuacji. Umowy na najem okazjonalny pozbawiają ich gwarancji związanych z prawem lokatorów. Mogą być zmuszeni do wyprowadzki w zasadzie z dnia na dzień i kolejnego uporczywego, a często wręcz poniżającego szukania mieszkania, zabezpieczania swoich oszczędności na kaucję czy sam transport dobytku. I to jest zastanawiające, że ten permanentny kryzys mieszkaniowy nie nauczył nas wszystkich tego, że więcej wspólnego mamy z osobami, którym grozi czy wobec których przeprowadzane są eksmisje, niż z ludźmi, którzy je zlecają i przeliczają zyski w postaci 421 milionów. Oczywiście te miliony to dla nich początek, bo później liczą na kolejne i kolejne, takim nigdy nie jest dość. A my dajemy się jeszcze wodzić za nos i potrafimy w internetowych komentarzach dopingować policję przeprowadzającą faktycznie bezprawne działania. Takie absurdy tylko w Polsce. Funkcjonariusze nie dopytują się o faktyczny tytuł wykonawczy, nie słuchają pełnomocnika eksmitowanej. Nie mają przygotowanej pomocy medycznej, dla które osób będą za moment szarpać i siłowo wyciągać. Działają na rozkaz, choć takie tłumaczenie musi budzić najgorsze skojarzenia. Działają opłacani z podatków nas wszystkich, w czasie kiedy nabywca terenu, zakupionego razem z ludźmi, przelicza swoje zyski. Przeliczają je również przedstawiciele kościoła, a może i miejscy urzędnicy skoro nie kwapią się do obrony akurat mieszkańców tego Osiedla. Wśród władz miasta Poznania nie byłaby to przecież pierwsza afera korupcyjna.


I na koniec, czy naprawdę Ja, czy Ty mamy coś …

En souvenir de Flore

SS

Elle fut conduite sur le pont suspendu au-dessus de l'Isère, qui relie le centre ville au quartier Saint Laurent, exécutée d'une balle dans la tête, et son corps jeté dans l'Isère. Son fils Jack, son père et sa mère connurent le même sort.


Ces meurtriers sont des membres de la Milice française et du Parti Populaire Français qui en profitèrent pour piller son logement et son commerce.

Il y a d'un côté les résultats électoraux du Rassemblement nationalou de Reconquête, très inquiétant lors des élections européennes ou législatives, et plus nettement en retrait lors des élections municipales. Nous avons aussi largement insisté sur les réseaux des catholiques intégristes, leurs diverses associations, leur volonté d'imposer leurs visions rétrogrades et leurs tentatives de contrôler la jeunesse.


Plusieurs groupes activistes et agressifs ont tenté de se constituer sur la métropole. Ils s'inscrivent dans un courant suprémaciste qui fait de la violence le fondement de leur projet. Pour l'instant, aucun de ces groupuscules n'a réussi à s'imposer.


Alimentant cette extrême-droite, plusieurs structures développent des discours complotistes et conspirationnistes. La crise du Covid a été un accélérateur : nombre des théories fumeuses et dangereuses ont proliféré et elles imprègnent largement la fachosphère.


L'objectif de ce travail est de faire un état de l'extrême-droite sur Grenoble et de souligner les pratiques locales de ces groupes. Une cartographie permet d'identifier les réseaux et de proposer une grille de lecture. Au centre de ce livret, une cartographie a été réalisée pour une meilleure compréhension spatiale de notre propos

author: Author and Editors
title: Artificial Intelligence in the Hands of the People: The Rongjiang Experiment
content:
A small county folded into the mountains of south-west Guizhou, Rongjiang was among the last counties in China to be

lifted

 out of extreme poverty, crossing the line only on 23 November 2020, and as late as 2022 its

per-capita output

 stood at about a third of the national average. ‘Eight parts mountain, one part water, one part field’ is how an old upland saying counted the land in Guizhou — the only province in China without a plain. Its valleys are terraced and narrow, its villages strung along the rivers and ridgelines beneath Moon Mountain. There was never much land here to produce wealth, and no easy road to carry the little produce out.


The Red Army crossed these mountains in 1934, on the march that would take it north. Football arrived a decade later,

brought

 by students of Guangxi University, evacuated to Rongjiang to escape Japanese aggression. Villagers have organised their own matches nearly every year in the eight decades since.


In May 2023, that tradition found a new expression in

Cun Chao

, the Village Super League: a competition organised by villagers, played by villagers, and watched by villagers. Within weeks of its launch, the stadium’s stands were filled to the brim, and footage carried by the short-video platforms drew the eyes of the whole country and then of the world. None of it ran itself. Packing a stadium every weekend, keeping order, feeding the broadcast — all of that took an organisational capacity the county had not required before.


This organisational capacity became an engine for real economic outcomes. Tourism revenue

rose

 from 8.4 billion yuan in 2023 to 10.8 billion in 2024, and the county’s gross domestic product reached 10.496 billion yuan in 2024, a rise of 9.5 per cent. The league

brought

 more than 2,700 new market entities into being, over thirty per cent of the whole prefecture’s new total, and village collective income

climbed

 from 58.9 million yuan in 2022 to 121 million in 2024.


It also opened a door to something else entirely. Since 2023 the county has set itself a less likely task: to put artificial intelligence (AI) into the hands of the villagers. It has built no large language model, no data centre, and no semiconductor plant. What it has built instead is its own people, organised across government offices, villages, and enterprises, so that residents who had never written a line of code, among them elderly farmers and village cadres, now use AI in their everyday work.


Building the Institutional and Material Conditions


The experiment was made possible by conditions built at multiple levels.


Cun Chao

 was no technology project but a feat of organisation, and the organisational structure was standing before the first ball was kicked. In October 2021, a year and a half before that match, the county set up a leading small group for new media and rural e-commerce, headed jointly by the county Party secretary and the county governor. In a Chinese county the Party committee leads and the government departments administer, and those departments — agriculture, commerce, culture and tourism — each holds responsibility for part of any new undertaking; a leading small group is how a Party committee concentrates the efforts of different departments on a common task. Here the two highest officials in the county took the headship themselves, one from the Party and one from the government, which put new media at the top of the agenda.


Beneath the group the county

placed

 a working team at the county level, a new-media service centre in every township, and a new-media service station in every village, and it set up a new-media company besides, a county state enterprise holding shares with private partners. The result was a single organisational chain linking three different but complementary capacities: Party leadership, grassroots mobilisation, and market activity. The Party committee provided political leadership; grassroots cadres reached every household; private firms and traders connected production to the market. When

Cun Chao

 began in May 2023, the county set a dedicated

Cun Chao

 Office on top of that standing structure, to mobilise cadres, coordinate security, and keep the media channels fed across all three levels at once.


When the county later turned toward AI, the mechanism had already put thirty-five thousand person-times — a tally of training instances, not unique individuals — through new-media

training

 and built more …

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Suspension of Maguindanao student journalist sparks outrage
content:
Photo from MSU-Maguindanao’s Facebook page

Institutional authority should not become a license to silence criticism.

CAGAYAN DE ORO — Any disciplinary action should have legal basis.

Alyajier Midtimbang, editor-in-chief of The Scribe, student publication of the state-run Mindanao State University (MSU)-Maguindanao, stressed this point after his suspension from his position over a column he wrote questioning the school’s non-participation in an annual event.

He said that there was no provision in the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 that stipulated suspension as a penalty if the student paper failed to obtain the administration’s comment.

“[W]e recognize that journalists have an ethical responsibility to provide relevant parties a fair opportunity to respond and to correct substantive errors when necessary,” Midtimbang said in a statement sent to Bulatlat. “However, it is also important to distinguish between an ethical or editorial standard and an express statutory requirement.”

On September 1, The Scribe released a column article titled “One MSU, but Maguindanao is out of the Unity Games 2026? Trailblazer no longer on the trail?” It questioned MSU-Maguindanao’s non-participation for this year’s MSU System Athletic Association (MSUSAA) Unity Games, asking what contributes to such a decision and wondering if it has something to do with insufficient funding.

Midtimban wrote in his column that the annual event is more than a competition. It is also a venue for celebration and for building camaraderie.

The article demanded that the school administration issue a statement which it did later on the same day.

The Office of the Chancellor, which also issued the memorandum regarding Midtimbang’s suspension, stated that the administration, in consultation with the deans, made the decision not to participate in the annual unity games and to direct their resources toward completing their facilities and accreditation commitments.

On the same day, however, a memorandum addressed to the vice chancellor and The Scribe’s adviser was issued, directing their immediate action following the publication of the said column article which allegedly raised insinuations against the university’s management of public funds without hearing its side.

Midtimbang’s suspension, based on the memorandum, also means revocation of his access to all The Scribe accounts.

In a statement, MSU Lantaw, the alliance of campus journalists in MSU Main Campus in Marawi City, questioned the school administration’s directive, calling for fair, impartial, and lawful proceedings, especially to The Scribe and its editor-in-chief.

The group said that institutional authority should not become a license to silence criticism. “If the story is wrong, answer the story. If The Scribe questioned the funds, then show the figures. If it questioned the participation of athletes, then explain the policy. If there were errors, present the correct information.”

“The strongest answer to journalism is not censorship. It is transparency,” MSU Lantaw added.

The Davao chapter of the College Editors Guild of the Philippines (CEGP), a national alliance of student publications and campus journalists, also condemned the school administration’s act, calling for the immediate withdrawal of Midtimbang’s suspension.

“The MSU–Maguindanao administration cannot invoke ‘discipline’ as a shield against scrutiny while leveraging its administrative authority over students and refusing to subject its own decisions to examination,” the group said.

Read: Political content led to attacks vs campus press

From July 2023 to June 2024, CEGP documented 206 cases of alleged campus press freedom violations. This is apart from the over 1,000 cases from 2010 to 2021. Censorship topped the list, according to the group.

Lawmakers belonging to the Makabayan bloc filed House Bill No. 4172 (Campus Press Freedom Act) in August 2025 which seeks to replace the current Campus Journalism Act of 1991.

It aims to authorize concerned government agencies to investigate campus press freedom violations and impose administrative sanctions on the violators. (DAA)

title: Daniela Klette: Knastkundgebung in Vechta am 19. September 2026 um 14 Uhr
content:
Solidarität mit Daniela Info Nr. 56/2.9.2026


„Die Solidarität lässt für sie, so sagt Daniela, die Sonne aufgehen“


Hallo, wir rufen zu einer weiteren Kundgebung am Samstag, d. 19. September 2026 um 14 Uhr vor dem Frauenknast in Vechta auf. Daniela ist weiterhin in der JVA Vechta, wie lange sie noch dort sein und wann sie nach Frankfurt verlegt wird, wissen wir nicht.


Es hängt von einer Entscheidung des Oberlandesgerichts (OLG) Frankfurt, 8. Strafsenat, wann die Anklageschrift, die Ende März von der Bundesanwaltschaft an das OLG ergangen ist, für einen weiteren Prozess in Frankfurt zugelassen wird.


Wer einen Redebeitrag auf der Kundgebung halten möchte, sagt uns bitte rechtzeitig Bescheid.


Gruppe: Solidarität mit Daniela


solidarisch-mit-daniela@t-online.de / www.solidarisch-mit-Daniela.de


Solidarität mit Daniela


Kundgebung am 19. September 2026 um 14 Uhr


Vechta, Franziskanerplatz/Kleine Kirchstraße


Daniela Klette, die weit über 30 Jahre in der Illegalität lebte, wurde nach ihrer Verhaftung Ende Februar 2024 in Berlin in die JVA Vechta gebracht. Dort war sie in den ersten sieben Wochen in Einzelisolation gewesen, dies bedeutete: 24 Stunden wurde die Zelle videoüberwacht, eine Metallblende war vor dem Fenster angebracht, so dass kein Sonnenlicht in die Zelle drang, Einzelhofgang, keinen Kontakt zu anderen gefangenen Frauen. Dies ist Folter! Nur durch Öffentlichkeitsarbeit wie z. B. die ersten beiden Kundgebungen im März und April 2024 wurden die Haftbedingungen für Daniela gelockert. Seitdem hat sie „normale“ Haftbedingungen.


Am 27. Mai 2026 ist Daniela vom Landgericht Verden – im ersten Prozess wegen acht Geldbeschaffungsaktionen – zu 13 Jahren verurteilt worden. Die Verteidiger von Daniela und auch die Staatsanwaltschaft haben Revision eingelegt. Ein zweiter Prozess gegen Daniela wird vor dem Oberlandesgericht Frankfurt/M stattfinden. Die Anklageschrift der Bundesanwaltschaft (BAW) u.a. wegen zwei Aktionen der Roten Armee Fraktion (RAF) in 1991 und 1993 sowie einer dritten einer Kämpfenden Einheit in 1990, an denen laut BAW Daniela mutmaßlich beteiligt gewesen sein soll, wird in den nächsten Monaten vom OLG zugelassen werden. Wann der Prozess beginnen wird, ist zur Zeit noch nicht absehbar. Auf jedem Fall wird dann Daniela vor Prozessbeginn nach Frankfurt verlegt. Im Frauenknast Frankfurt-Preungesheim sind die Haftbedingungen schlechter als in Vechta, z. B. hier hat sie 4x im Monat Besuch, in Frankfurt nur 2x.


V.i.S.d.P. und Kontakt: solidarisch-mit-daniela@t-online.de / www.solidarisch-mit-daniela.de


passiert am 19.09,2026

title: Film Ruina – über ein besetzes Woh- Projekt in Venezuela
content:
Sonntag, 5. September, 21 Uhr


Wagenplatz

Revaler- Ecke Modersohnstr.


10245 Berlin


Was passiert, wenn eine Bank scheitert? Zum Beispiel wird es von 3000 Menschen besetzt und in ein Wohnprojekt umgewandelt. Die Innenstadt von Caracas, eine 200 Meter hohe Wolkenkratzer-Ruine, ragt bis zum karibischen Himmel empor und dient als Unterschlupf für 750 Familien. Von der Stadtverwaltung ignoriert und von der Nachbarschaft gefürchtet, bauen die Bewohner von Torre Confinanzas ihr eigenes Modell einer sozialistischen Mikrogesellschaft in ihrer vertikalen Stadt auf. Ruina erzählt von Schwierigkeiten und Erfolgen, indem es aus einer Masse von Menschen eine soziale Gemeinschaft aufbaut.


Der Film soll auch wieder einmal den Blick auf Venezuela richten, ein Land, das vor 20 Jahren für mancheLinke ein Vorbild war.
